title: Place: with no frame selected, the graphic loads into the place cursor
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes the misplaced images and extra links in #593. Fixes #931.

- File › Place (and the PDF page dialog, browser import and Place with Import Options) loads the graphic into the place cursor when no empty or graphic frame is selected: click to place it at its natural size, drag to draw its frame. Before, it made a frame at the first page's top-left margin, often out of view, and each try added another link. This also places on a parent page while parents are being edited.
- With an empty or graphic frame selected, Place fills it as before.
- Escape unloads the place cursor; switching tools does too.
- `file.place` gains `loadCursor: true` for this; without it the command works as before, so the control channel is unchanged. Text and media files are placed as before.
- A file dropped on the window lands on the spread under the pointer (or the spread in view), a parent spread included: a graphic's top left at that point, text in a new frame on the document page there. Before, it went to the first spread.

Tests: with nothing selected, Place leaves the place cursor loaded and adds no item; Escape unloads it; a click places the image at natural size; with an empty graphic frame selected, Place fills it. `a_file_dropped_while_a_parent_is_open_lands_on_the_parent`.

title: Toolbox: Shift+X, D, X and / for the Fill/Stroke proxy
author: aiongg
body:
- Shift+X swaps fill and stroke, D sets the default (fill None, stroke Black), X brings fill or stroke to the front, and / applies None to the one in front. The toolbox buttons and the keys run the same commands. The keys don't fire while typing.
- Swap and Default are one undo step and work per object in a multi-selection, keeping each object's tints; locked objects are skipped. New engine commands: `object.swapFillStroke`, `object.defaultFillStroke`.
- Which of fill and stroke is in front is one setting shared by the toolbox and the Color panel.
- `/` can be used in keyboard shortcuts.

Tests: the keys on a selected frame (swap keeps tints, default, front toggle, None on the stroke, no effect while typing); two selected objects swap each, a locked one stays, one undo restores both.

title: Tables: drag row and column borders with the Type tool
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #595.

- With the Type tool, the pointer over a column or row border shows a resize cursor; dragging resizes instead of selecting text. A click without a drag changes nothing.
- A column border changes the width of the column before it and the columns after it move along; with Shift the next column gives or takes the same amount, so the table keeps its width. Rows work the same way; a dragged row becomes At Least that height.
- The table's end and bottom edges resize the last column and row; with Shift they scale all columns or rows in proportion.
- Sizes stay between 3 pt and 10,000 pt. One undo step per drag; Escape cancels. Locked frames and layers are refused. Rotated frames, turned spreads, merged cells and right-to-left tables are handled.
- New engine command `table.resizeBorder` `{story?, table?, frame?, axis: column|row, index, delta? | size?, keepTableSize?}`; the last index is the outer edge.

Tests: column drag, Shift keeping the width, Shift scaling on the edge, row drag to At Least, clamping, bad parameters, one undo step, locked frame refused; the Type tool on a plain and a 90° rotated frame shows the cursor, resizes from the border, ignores a 1 px wobble, cancels on Escape and still places the caret inside a cell.

title: MCP: confine file access with --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root
author: isaac-levine
body:
`designcraft-cli mcp` gives the agent on the other end the same file access as the user running it. VectorCraft already has two flags for this, so this adds the same ones here with the same names and behaviour, and one client config works across the apps. It is the same change as storytold/wordcraft#798, storytold/gridcraft#480, storytold/deckcraft#247, storytold/pdfcraft#1448 and storytold/soundcraft#309.

    designcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out

An earlier attempt at this (#290) put the check in the MCP layer and mapped request parameters to read or write by name, and review kept finding paths that slipped past the map: `links.copyTo`, `links.relinkFolder`, `media.options` poster paths, paths stored inside documents, dangling symlinks, and the connected-mode `app.*` commands with their file pickers. This puts the check in the engine instead, at the one place every path a command opens already ends up, so there is no list of parameters to keep complete. That covers the paths a document names for itself (linked images, data sources, book chapters, IDML links, Document Fonts) and the output folders of `file.package` and `links.copyTo`, and a guard test fails if a command module starts touching the file system on its own. Connected mode is not confined at all here: the flags are an error together with `--connect`, so the app-side pickers never come into it.

**How it works**

Every user-named file the engine opens now goes through a small `io` module (`read_file`, `read_to_string`, `write_file`, plus `metadata`, `is_file`, `is_dir`, `exists` and `read_dir` for the places that only probe), and the checks sit there. The new `crates/engine/src/file_access.rs` holds the roots and the path logic: make the path absolute, follow symlinks (for a file that doesn't exist yet, resolve its nearest existing ancestor and require the rest to be plain names), then compare with the root by whole path components. On Windows…

title: Styles: selection capture accepts deleted-swatch fills
author: KnottyDyes
body:
Follow-up to #403. Creating a paragraph style from a selection failed after a swatch was deleted: `swatch.delete` leaves the swatch's name in the text, and `style.paragraph.create` with `fromSelection` checked that inherited name as if the caller had passed it. The Paragraph Styles panel's New Style button then created nothing.

- Only character fills the caller passes in `chars` are checked, before the selection's attributes are merged in.
- A fill inherited from the selection is kept as it is, including the name of a deleted swatch.

title: MCP: reconnect closed sockets before sending the next request
author: KnottyDyes
body:
Follow-up to #514. After the app restarted, the MCP remote backend sent the next request on the old, closed connection, and the call failed with "operation may have completed" although the restarted app had received nothing. A failed reconnect got the same message.

- Before reusing a connection, the backend checks without blocking whether the app has closed it, and if so reconnects before writing anything. The request was never delivered, so this is not a resend.
- When the app can't be reached, the error says so and that nothing was sent.
- "Operation may have completed" is kept, still without a resend, for failures after the request has been written.

Validation: two new loopback tests fail before the change. One restarts the server on the same port between calls and checks that the next edit is applied exactly once; the other checks the message when nothing is listening. The lost-reply test from #514 still passes. `cargo test -p designcraft-mcp` (20 passed) and `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm) pass.

Thanks to @aiongg for spotting this in the #514 review.

title: Links: placed Word, RTF and text files can stay linked
author: thaynej
body:
Closes #597.

### What
Placed text files can now stay linked, as in InDesign:
- `file.place {…, link: true}`, or Preferences › File Handling › Create Links When Placing Text Files (`prefs.set {linkTextFiles}`, off by default), records on the story the file's path, size and hash, and the style map and style-conflict option used (`Story.file_link`, a new `TextFileLink`; `Story.link` stays the Place and Link parent). The fingerprint is size plus a content hash rather than Data Merge's size plus modification time: re-saving or syncing an unchanged file (e.g. through Dropbox) changes its modification time and would show a false Modified, while a content check only flags real changes. The hash is FNV-1a, for change detection rather than security, so no new dependency.
- The Links panel and `links.list` show linked text files with the same OK / Modified / Missing status as graphics, plus `edited` when the story was changed in the layout.
- `links.update` imports a modified file again into the same story, keeping its frames and threading, with the saved style map. Names Auto Rename chose are kept, so updates don't add `_wrd_2`, `_wrd_3`…. As in InDesign, edits made in the layout are replaced. The Links panel (and Window › Links › Update Link) asks first when a linked story was edited in the layout ("“chapter.docx” has been edited in this layout. Updating replaces those edits with the text from the file.", Update / Cancel), as InDesign's Links panel does. The `links.update` command updates without asking and returns a warning, as InDesign scripting's `link.update()` does. Either way it is undoable.
- `links.relink`, `links.goTo` and `links.embed` (shown as Unlink for text) take `{story}`.
- Saved in the native format. IDML export writes the text unlinked.
- Tracked changes import as `file.place` does today (as if accepted).

Placing into an insertion point doesn't create a link (a link replaces a whole story) and says so in `warnings`.

title: Add a Nix flake (NixOS, GNOME and Hyprland)
author: untypequicode
body:
## What

Adds `flake.nix` and `nix/package.nix` so that `nix build`, `nix run` and an overlay give a source-built designcraft and designcraft-cli on NixOS, modelled on the existing LightCraft flake.

- `Cargo.lock` drives the dependencies (git sources through `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`), so there is no `vendorHash` to maintain. The version comes from `[workspace.package]`.
- Installs the desktop file, hicolor icons, MIME types and AppStream metadata from `packaging/linux/`, validated at build time (`desktop-file-validate`, `appstreamcli`).
- Wayland and X11: the binaries are wrapped so the libraries winit/wgpu/rfd `dlopen` are found on NixOS — `libwayland-client`, `libxkbcommon` (incl. x11), the X11 libs, the Vulkan loader, `libEGL` and `libdbus` (xdg-desktop-portal file chooser). It runs natively on Wayland under GNOME and Hyprland, with X11/XWayland as fallback. Hyprland needs a portal backend for the file dialogs (`xdg.portal.extraPortals = [ pkgs.xdg-desktop-portal-gtk ]`); this is noted in `nix/package.nix`.
- The fonts from `storytold/craft-fonts`, where the app embeds them, are a pinned non-flake input at the revision the release workflow uses.
- Also: `overlays.default`, `apps.default`, a dev shell, `nix fmt` and a formatting check.
- `doCheck` is off: the suite needs corpora and a GPU the sandbox cannot provide (`cargo xtask ci` stays the gate); it can be turned on with `overrideAttrs`.

No Rust, packaging or CI file is touched.

## Testing

`nix build .#designcraft` builds both binaries and passes the desktop-file and AppStream validation, on NixOS.

title: fix(save): preserve live state when persistence fails
author: skylartaylor
body:
Follow-up to #485.

Failed Save As could change data-source paths and the document revision before its write failed. Library add/remove and book add/remove/style-source edits likewise changed their live collections before persistence succeeded. Save a Copy also kept paths relative to the original document directory.

Prepare and persist prospective values first, then install them in the live session. Save As keeps the atomic writer; Save a Copy rebases the saved copy without changing the open document.

Validation: seven permanent regressions cover failed Save As (document, saved state, undo/redo, selection, journal and original file), copy path resolution, and failed library/book writes. The regressions fail on current main and pass with the fix. Full `cargo xtask ci` covers formatting, clippy with warnings denied, native tests, assets, layers and WASM compilation.

title: fix(export): replace desktop and CLI outputs atomically
author: skylartaylor
body:
Follow-up to #485.

The desktop write callback and CLI raster exporter still overwrote files in place. Route both through the engine's atomic writer, preserving the original file until replacement succeeds.

Atomic replacement requires a writable parent directory; errors leave the original untouched instead of falling back to in-place writes.

Two permanent regressions exercise the actual desktop callback and CLI process: an already-open reader keeps the old bytes, the new output is complete, private Unix permissions survive, and a symlink to a valid long filename remains intact. Both regressions fail with the old callers and pass after routing. Full `cargo xtask ci` covers formatting, clippy with warnings denied, native tests, assets, layers and WASM compilation. Windows runtime and power-loss durability are not claimed.

title: fix(book): stage chapter updates before saving
author: skylartaylor
body:
Book numbering and style updates could rewrite earlier chapters before encountering a later error, replace IDML inputs with native bytes, or overwrite a chapter that is still open. This prepares every target before saving, permits writes only to closed native chapters, and preserves IDML as a read-only style/PDF source.

Snapshots are staged on disk with a 4,096-chapter limit. Later write failures list the completed chapter paths; each file is atomic, while the whole book is not a transaction. Adds regressions for partial updates, imported formats, open aliases, cleanup and compatible book exports.

Validation: six regressions fail on the original baseline and pass with this change. All 11 book safety and compatibility tests pass. The refreshed candidate passes all six `cargo xtask ci` gates: 1,251 native tests and checks for 15 WASM crates.

Follow-up to #485.

title: fix(recovery): retain recovered checkpoints until save or close
author: skylartaylor
body:
Recovering a document currently removes its only checkpoint before the next autosave. Keep a snapshot until successful Save, Close or Revert, and preserve other entries when IDs restart or recovery uses another folder.

This focuses on the recovery-retention concern also addressed in #380; its GPU startup and fallback work remains separate.

Validation: all six local `cargo xtask ci` gates pass against the refreshed candidate: 1,270 native tests passed, 4 ignored, and 15 WASM package checks. The recovery tests include nine fresh-process drivers that explicitly execute the subprocess helper, plus second-crash, failed-publication and Save/Close/Revert cleanup coverage.

title: fix(recovery): preserve documents on orderly app exit
author: skylartaylor
body:
Edits made after the last recovery timer can be lost on orderly native shutdown. Write the latest recovery state after honoring complete quit approvals, retain incomplete or stale plans, clear stale recovery after Undo, and report unavailable or failed storage.

Cancelable macOS Dock Quit remains open (#544).

Validation: four permanent exit regressions and an isolated actual `App::on_exit` fixture that fails before and passes after; all six local gates against the refreshed candidate (1,274 passing native tests, 4 ignored; 15 WASM crate checks).

title: Paste vector art from Illustrator, VectorCraft or Figma as editable paths
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

InDesign pastes art copied in Illustrator as editable paths. LYH Studio's word-spiral tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27U7g94S2zs), 4:37) depends on it: the spiral is drawn in Illustrator, copied, pasted into InDesign, then reshaped with the Direct Selection and Pen tools before text goes on it.

Illustrator, VectorCraft, Figma and Inkscape put copied objects on the system clipboard as SVG markup. In DesignCraft, Ctrl/Cmd+V with that markup on the clipboard pasted the markup itself: main pastes other apps' text as a new text frame (#518).

Now the SVG pastes as editable paths, centred in the view and selected, in one undo step.

## How

- **New engine command** `edit.pasteSvg {svg, spread?, at?}` (`cmd/paste_svg.rs`). The markup is parsed with usvg, which DesignCraft already uses to place SVGs.
  - **Paths:** each path becomes a DesignCraft path, or a graphic line for a straight two-point segment. Transforms are applied, and CSS pixels become points (0.75 pt/px, as placed SVGs already use), so a 1-unit stroke in a pt-sized SVG is 1 pt.
  - **Fill and stroke:** colours become unnamed swatches (an existing swatch of the same colour is reused). Strokes keep weight, caps, joins, miter limit and dashes. Fill/stroke opacity and wrapping-group opacity become the object's opacity.
  - **Groups and text:** an SVG group of several objects stays a group; the single-object groups usvg adds for transforms and opacity don't. Text comes in as outlines.
  - **Not converted:** gradients and patterns paste as their first colour, and embedded images are left out; the result's `warnings` says so. Nesting beyond 64 groups is dropped rather than recursed into.
  - **Errors:** text that isn't SVG, unreadable markup, or SVG with nothing to paste is refused, with no undo step.
- **`DesignApp::run`:** Edit › Paste whose system-clipboard text is SVG markup, with no text being edited, runs `edit.pasteSvg` at the centre of the view (main's `canvas::view_centre`) inste…

title: fix(macos): make Dock Quit cancelable
author: skylartaylor
body:
Dock Quit currently reaches AppKit termination before the unsaved-document flow can cancel it. This routes native termination through the existing close-request transaction, restores a hidden or minimized window for the prompt, and keeps partial answers intact when Quit is requested again. Cancel keeps every document; the app exits after all current answers are approved.

The change pins a small opt-in patch to winit 0.30.13 at [`3d51077`](https://github.com/skylartaylor/winit/commit/3d51077fd1a966f84df9ef287839dc84fd5b4ca7). Other platforms and applications using the default winit behavior retain their existing termination behavior. The AppKit callback queues normal close events rather than running dialogs inside a termination modal loop.

- `cargo xtask ci`: all six gates passed, including 1,277 native tests (four existing ignored tests) and WASM.
- The dependency's unit tests and six native subprocess scenarios passed, including actual `NSApplication::terminate`, cancellation/retry and stale-window handling.
- An additional native probe established an actually hidden app, requested termination, and verified that the same public window commands asynchronously unhide, restore and focus it. The final combined build also passed a fresh minimized-window prompt/Cancel smoke.
- Native macOS smoke: the baseline exited with a dirty document; the patched build stayed open, restored a minimized window and displayed the prompt. Later Cancel retained both documents, selection, undo history and recovery. Saving wrote a reopenable document; a subsequent approved discard exited and cleared recovery.
- Three UI regressions cover prompt visibility, repeated requests/later Cancel, and completed Save/Don't Save. Existing canceled/failed Save As and final recheck regressions also pass.

The live smoke used the native Cocoa `terminate:` menu action that enters the same termination boundary as Dock Quit. Force Quit, logout and physical shutdown were not exercised.

title: test(recovery): make failed republishing fixtures deterministic
author: skylartaylor
body:
The FreeBSD root runner can write through the recovery tests' read-only directory permissions. Republish then succeeds and removes the old checkpoint, causing six retention assertions to fail while expecting a failed write.

These fixtures now obstruct the actual reserved destination with a directory and call the real publisher. They assert that the write was attempted and failed, then check the same checkpoint, provenance, Save/Close/Revert and autosave behavior. A private helper supplies this test boundary; ordinary `recovery::open` still uses the same writer and ordering. The fixtures can also run on Windows.

title: Pen tool: continue an open path from either end point; Reverse Path
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

In InDesign, the Pen tool over an end point of an open path shows a "continue" cursor. Clicking there carries on drawing that same path, and clicking its other end closes it. LYH Studio's word-spiral tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27U7g94S2zs), 5:25) extends the pasted spiral's tail this way, so the text can run off across the spread.

On main, the Pen always starts a new path, so the same clicks leave two separate objects.

## How

- **Tools (`pen.rs`):**
  - **Finding an end point:** with no path being drawn, the Pen looks for an open path's first or last anchor under the pointer. It checks the selection first, then the frontmost item, and skips locked paths, closed subpaths, groups and frames with content. It shows `Cursor::PenContinue` there.
  - **Clicking it:** the tool takes over that path. New anchors go on its subpath through `path.appendAnchor {subpath}`, and clicking the other end closes that subpath through `path.close {subpath}`.
  - **First anchor:** continuing from the first anchor reverses the subpath first (`path.reverse`), so new anchors follow on from it.
  - **Dragging it:** dragging from the end point reshapes its direction lines (`path.setAnchor`), as in InDesign. A plain click changes nothing and adds no undo step.
- **Engine (`object.rs`):**
  - `path.reverse {ids?, subpath?}`, which is also Object › Paths › Reverse Path (InDesign has it in the same menu).
  - `path.setAnchor {id, subpath?, anchor: index|first|last, p?, in?, out?}`. Collinear, opposite direction lines make the anchor smooth.
  - `path.appendAnchor` and `path.close` take an optional `subpath`. `appendAnchor` refuses a closed subpath instead of growing it.
- "Reverse Path" and "Set Anchor" are translated into all nine interface languages. ROADMAP updated.

On this branch the UI cursor uses the same crosshair for both pen states. aiongg's #487 adds the per-state Pen cursor images; with both merged, `PenContinue` only needs an image there.

## Before /…

title: Windows: dragging across monitors with different scales doesn't grow or crash the window
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #612.

- winit is pinned (`[patch.crates-io]`, git rev 39c4009c) to the 0.30.x backport of rust-windowing/winit#4694, which stops the window flipping between scales and growing during a drag across monitors. The same pin as storytold/gridcraft#761; remove it once eframe uses a winit release with the fix.
- The GPU device asks for the adapter's own maximum texture size instead of 8192, so a large window on a high-scale display gets a surface.
- After start-up, uncaptured wgpu errors (such as a surface configure over the limit) are logged instead of panicking; the window keeps its last surface until it shrinks. During start-up the existing adapter fallback still works.

#623 also patches winit (Dock Quit, skylartaylor/winit 3d51077); only one `[patch]` for winit is possible, so landing both needs one winit branch with both commits.

Tests: the surface limit is the adapter's own and a 9048×5757 window fits from a 16384 limit. Not tested on Windows hardware here.

title: Text frames: auto-size grows and shrinks frames to fit their text
author: aiongg
body:
Part of #180 (auto-size).

- Height Only, Width Only, Height and Width, and Height and Width (Keep Proportions) resize a frame to fit its text after every edit, as part of the same undo step, around one of the nine reference points. Rotated frames keep the reference point in place.
- Minimum height and width, and No Line Breaks, are honoured; an empty frame keeps one line's height or the minimum.
- IDML import fits auto-size frames after fonts load, so single-line labels in frames shorter than their text come back. The minimum and No Line Breaks settings are imported and exported.
- Text Frame Options has an Auto-Size section; `object.textFrameOptions` takes the reference point, minimums and No Line Breaks.
- Out of scope: frames of a thread other than the last, vertical frames, type on a path.

Tests: Height Only grows and shrinks with the top or bottom edge fixed; Width Only with No Line Breaks; minimum height; one undo restores text and size; rotated frame; threaded frame; IDML import of a too-short label; IDML round trip.

title: Text frames: Balance Columns evens out the last frame's columns
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #609.

- With Balance Columns on, the columns of the frame a story ends in finish at about the same depth (the last column at most a line shorter). A frame the text runs on from, or an overset frame, fills normally.
- An explicit column break starts balancing after it; keep options are respected; spanning paragraphs keep their own balancing. Vertical frames work too.
- The search is bounded (at most 16 tries) and only the last band of the last frame is laid out again.
- Text Frame Options has a Balance Columns checkbox; IDML `VerticalBalanceColumns` already round-trips.

Tests: two and three columns, a kept-together paragraph, a vertical story, a frame the text runs on from, a column break, IDML import.

title: Document tabs: long names are shortened so the close button stays visible
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #603.

- A document tab is at most 260 px wide; a longer name ends in "…" (cut at a grapheme boundary, right-to-left names included) while the unsaved marker, zoom and "[Preview]" stay readable. The close button stays inside the tab, and the full name shows on hover when it was shortened.
- Tabs and close buttons have accessible labels.

Test: long Latin and Hebrew names and a short one in a 1200 px window: long tabs are at most 260 px wide and each close button lies inside its tab.

title: Pages panel: double-clicking a parent shows that parent; parent thumbnails
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #624.

- Double-clicking a parent shows that parent, and only its row is highlighted. `layout.parents.edit {on?, parent?}` takes a parent id or label and asks the view to show it, so the control channel does the same.
- Parents are identified by id: rows, drag payloads and Apply Parent send the id. A parent name resolves by id, then full label, then prefix only when one parent has it; an unknown or shared name is an error instead of silently clearing the page's parent. `"[None]"` still clears.
- Parent rows get thumbnails like document pages.
- Delete All Guides while editing parents acts on the parent in view.

Tests: double-clicking the third of four parents shows it and highlights only its row; parents sharing a prefix stay distinct by id and label; shared and unknown names are errors; `layout.parents.edit` with an id or label shows that parent.

title: Type on a path: drag the start and end brackets
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

Selected type on a path in InDesign shows brackets across the path where the text starts and ends. Dragging the start bracket slides the text along the path, and dragging the end bracket shortens the room it has. LYH Studio's word-spiral tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27U7g94S2zs), 8:07–8:40) drags the start bracket outward to clear the middle of the spiral for a photo.

On main, path type only has a start offset, set numerically in Type on a Path Options. Nothing is drawn on the path, and a drag at the start of the path grabs the corner resize handle instead (left image below).

## How

- **doc:** `PathType.end: Option<f64>`, the end bracket as a distance along the path. `None` is the path's end, so existing documents are unchanged; the field isn't written when it's `None`.
- **geom:** `PathWarp::nearest(p)`, the arc length of the point on the path nearest `p`. For flipped path type it is measured the way `at` measures it, from the path's end.
- **compose:** the path line runs from the start bracket to the end bracket; text past the end bracket is overset.
- **engine:** `type.pathOptions {end}`, a distance or `null`.
  - Both brackets stay on the path.
  - An end at or past the path's length means the path's end.
  - The bracket being moved stops at the other one, so they can't cross.
  - The result reports `end`.
- **tools:** with the Selection or Direct Selection tool, selected path type shows its brackets in the layer colour: a line across the path with a tick pointing toward the text.
  - Over a bracket the cursor is `Cursor::PathBracket` (a column-resize cursor in egui).
  - Dragging a bracket previews `type.pathOptions {start|end}` at the pointer's nearest point on the path, then commits as one undo step ("Move Bracket").
  - Brackets take priority over the resize handles, and locked items aren't dragged.
- **idml:** `EndBracket` is now read; it was already written, as the path length. It is written from `end`.

## Before / after

…

title: fix(index): keep level 3 and 4 topics in a run-in index
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Run-in indexes stopped after level 2, dropping deeper topics and their page references. InDesign's Run-in formats all levels of an entry in one paragraph, separated by Between Entries. This lists every subtopic after its parent in sort order, using the existing entry text and the configured separator, so levels 3 and 4 stay in the same paragraph.

Adds a regression test covering four topic levels, sibling order, a custom separator and a cross-reference. My contributor display name is in a separate commit.

Tested:
- The new test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `cargo test -p designcraft-doc index::tests`: 2 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed (fmt, clippy with warnings denied, tests, assets, layers, wasm).

title: fix(color): mirror gradient midpoints when reversing
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Reverse in the Gradient panel (and `object.gradient` with `reverse: true`) reversed the stops and mirrored their locations, but each stop kept its own midpoint. A stop's midpoint describes the segment after it (`Gradient::sample` reads `a.midpoint`, and IDML export writes `stops[i - 1].midpoint` on the next stop), so after reversing every midpoint sat on the wrong segment and was not mirrored. A white to black gradient with its midpoint at 25% ended up with the midpoint at 50% instead of 75%.

`reverse` now moves each midpoint to its reversed segment as `1 - midpoint`. The last stop has no following segment and gets the default 0.5.

`reverse_stops` now checks the two-stop case and that a three-stop gradient with uneven midpoints samples as the original mirrored.

Testing: `reverse_stops` fails on main (17cf5b4) and passes with the fix. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: fix(fonts): fall back to a font made for Malayalam (part of #628)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #628 (Malayalam); span columns is a separate feature, happy to take it on next.

With fallback fonts on, Malayalam in a Latin font took the first installed file that maps it. On macOS that's Arial Unicode MS (`/Library/Fonts` sorts first), which has the characters but no Malayalam shaping, so ക്ഷ came out as ക + ് + ഷ instead of the conjunct, and the same for every cluster. With a Malayalam font picked directly the shaping was already right. Same idea as vectorcraft's script fallback in storytold/vectorcraft#1185 (Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar); vectorcraft's list has no Malayalam entry yet. The family list is a judgement call, happy to switch.

Validation:

title: feat(type): kern the pair at the caret with Alt+Left/Right
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #621.

The text model already has manual pair kerning (`Kerning::Manual`, applied after its character) and tracking, but nothing reached them from the keyboard: in the Type tool Alt+Left/Right moved the caret by a word. This adds a `type.adjustKerning {by}` command and routes Alt+Left/Right to it, as in InDesign/Quark: with a caret it adds to the manual kerning of the pair the caret sits in (stored on the character before it, starting from 0 if the pair used Metrics/Optical/None), with a selection it adds to the tracking. The step is 20/1000 em, 100 with Cmd (Ctrl+Alt on Windows/Linux). Each press is one undo step.

This takes Alt+Left/Right away from word movement. Ctrl+Left/Right still jumps by words, and Alt+Shift+Left/Right still extends the selection by words, but on macOS the plain Option+arrow word jump is gone (InDesign uses Cmd+arrow for that, which here is line start/end today). Happy to switch to a different split if you prefer keeping Option+arrow for words.

Validation:
- `kerning_nudges_the_pair_at_the_caret_and_tracking_on_a_selection` (engine): fails on main (`UnknownCommand("type.adjustKerning")`), passes here
- `alt_arrows_kern_the_pair_at_the_caret` (engine, through the Type tool keys): fails on main (Alt+Left moves the caret, kerning stays `None`), passes here
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine -p designcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(textimport): keep a leading empty paragraph in Tagged Text
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Importing Tagged Text dropped an empty first paragraph. The importer treats paragraph breaks before any text as header lines, so once `<ParaStyle:Head>` had started an empty first paragraph, its break was skipped and the next `<ParaStyle:Body>` overwrote its style. A story exported by DesignCraft's own Tagged Text export as `\nText` (Head, Body) came back as `Text` with only Body.

The header check now stops once a ParaStyle tag has started the story.

Tested:

- New `tagged_text_keeps_a_leading_empty_paragraph` round-trips such a story through `tagged_text` and `import`. It fails on main (`64f0ca8`) with `Text` instead of `\nText` and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p designcraft-textimport`: 15 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all 6 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).

title: fix(idml): text strokes aligned outside stay behind the fill
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #619.

InDesign stores "stroke behind fill" for text as `StrokeAlignment="OutsideAlignment"` on character style ranges and character styles. The import never read it, and the text model had nowhere to put it, so every text stroke was drawn centred on top of the fill and ate into the letters. This adds a `stroke_alignment` character attribute (reusing `StrokeAlign`, defaulting to Center so existing documents don't change), reads and writes it in IDML, and draws an outside stroke as a double-width stroke under the fill, on screen and in PDF. Create Outlines carries it over to the shape's stroke alignment.

An outside stroke with no fill (or a transparent one) shows its inner half too, since it's paint order rather than a true offset. I kept it that way so screen and PDF match; happy to switch to subtracting the glyphs like shape strokes do if you'd rather. There is no Character panel control for it yet, only `type.char {"strokeAlignment": "outside"}`.

Validation:
- `idml` `tests::text_stroke`: fails on main (`StrokeAlignment="OutsideAlignment"` resolves to Center), passes here; covers local, character style, local override of the style, and round trip
- `engine --test text_stroke_alignment` (raster and PDF): fails on main (stroke covers fill pixels at the glyph edge), passes here
- `engine --lib create_outlines`, `engine --test text_decorations`
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-doc -p designcraft-compose -p designcraft-render -p designcraft-pdf -p designcraft-idml -p designcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: The Effects dialog: Object › Effects and the panel's fx button, with Preview
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

InDesign sets every object effect in the Effects dialog. Object › Effects › Drop Shadow… (or Inner Shadow…, Transparency… and the rest), their shortcuts, and the fx button at the bottom of the Effects panel all open it on that effect, turned on. Its parts:
- the effect list on the left, each effect with a checkbox;
- the chosen effect's settings on the right (Blending, Position with X/Y offsets, Options);
- a summary line of what's applied;
- Preview, Cancel and OK.

LYH Studio's word-spiral tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27U7g94S2zs)) uses it twice: an Inner Shadow on the circular photo at 9:50, then a Drop Shadow instead on the second photo at 12:06.

On main, Object › Effects › Drop Shadow toggles the effect with no way to set it, and the panel only has a few drop-shadow fields. Nothing else (inner shadow, glows, bevel, satin, feathers) can be set from the UI.

## How

- **Engine:** `object.effects {effects?, opacity?, blend?, ids?}` sets transparency and any number of effects in one undo step.
  - `effects` is merged field by field into each object's settings, so unlisted fields stay.
  - Values are kept in range: opacities 0–1, sizes and distances ≥ 0, percentages 0–100, angles within ±180°.
  - Non-finite values, a wrong type or an unknown blend mode change nothing.
  - Locked objects are skipped.
- **UI (`effects_dialog.rs`):**
  - **Opening:** `menus::activate` with no params for `object.dropShadow`, `object.innerShadow`, … (the menu items and shortcuts such as Cmd+Alt+M) opens the dialog on that page, turned on. Scripts calling those commands with params still set the effect directly. Object › Effects gains Transparency… (`effects.dialog {page}`), and the Effects panel gains the fx button with every effect.
  - **Pages:** Transparency (mode, opacity), Drop Shadow, Inner Shadow, Outer Glow, Inner Glow, Bevel and Emboss, Satin, Basic, Directional and Gradient Feather. Each has the settings the document model holds, in the document'…

title: feat(i18n): translate the French interface
author: Atalantis
body:
## What and why

The French column of the shared table in `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs` repeated the English text on 1,217 rows, so most of the interface stayed in English when French was selected. Those rows now carry a French translation. 60 rows stay identical on purpose (format names, Japanese composition terms, words French shares with English).

Strings the shared table has no row for (248, already translated in `ja.rs`, `it.rs` or `ar.rs`) go in a new `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/fr.rs`, looked up before the shared column, the same way `ja.rs` is. Its keys and the shared table's keys are disjoint, so `cached_lookup_preserves_every_translation_across_language_switches` still holds by construction.

The diff on `i18n.rs` is larger than the change: `rustfmt` rewraps rows that became longer than the line width.

## Second commit: vocabulary

`feat(i18n): align French terms with page-layout and InDesign vocabulary`

82 entries are reworded to the terms French layout artists know: « Associer », « Assemblage », « Repères commentés », « Magnétisme », « Déformation », « Décalage vertical », « Options d'arrondi », « Exécuter et répéter », « Rééditer le lien », « Masque » for Clipping Path, « Sommet / Aboutée / Projetée » in the stroke settings. Only 8 are attested in Adobe's public French help pages for InDesign; the others come from the reviewer's knowledge of the French interface, so this is the commit most open to discussion.

title: Type on a path: the Type tool clicks and selects along the curve; caret and highlight follow it
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

In LYH Studio's word-spiral tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27U7g94S2zs), 12:50), the Type tool selects words in the tail of the type on a path and sizes them up, word by word (14, 18, 24, 30 pt). Later (13:50) it selects more words there to recolour them. InDesign selects along the curve, and the highlight follows the letters.

On main, type on a path is composed as one straight line and then bent along the path for drawing. Clicks weren't bent back:
- **Clicking and dragging:** the Type tool's click, drag and double-click picked the character at the same spot of the straightened line, so you got the wrong letters or none.
- **Caret and highlight:** both were drawn on the straight line, away from the text (left image below).
- **Missing clicks:** clicks on the letters themselves (above an open path) didn't hit the frame at all.

## How

- **compose:** `PathTextMap`, built from the item and its composed frame, maps between the composed line and the path, exactly as `path_glyphs` places the glyphs. It handles the start bracket, flip and alignment (baseline, ascender, descender or centre on the path).
  - `to_path(line point)` gives the point on the path, offset across it.
  - `to_line(path point)` gives the point on the line at the nearest arc length.
- **engine:** `hit_byte`, behind `text.placeCaret`, `text.extendTo`, `text.selectWord` and `text.release`, maps the click through `to_line` for type on a path, so the click lands on the character under the pointer.
- **doc:** `item_hit` reaches 12 pt further from the path for type on a path, so a click on the letters (which stand over the path) hits the frame.
- **canvas:**
  - The highlight of path type is drawn in 2 pt slices, each turned with the path, so it bends with the text.
  - The caret stands across the path at its position.
  - Other frames draw as before.

## Before / after

Type on an arch, 24 pt; with the Type tool, drag from the H of ARCH to SELECT:

| Before (main): the selecti…

title: Eyedropper: a sampled colour goes to the stroke when the Stroke box is in front
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

InDesign's Eyedropper puts a colour sampled from a placed image on whichever of the toolbox's Fill and Stroke boxes is in front. In LYH Studio's word-spiral tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27U7g94S2zs), 11:12), a line is drawn under the quote. With the Stroke box in front, the Eyedropper samples the red of the dress in the photo, and the line turns red.

With #572 the Eyedropper samples images, but always into the fill. A line has no fill to show it, so nothing visible changes (left image below).

## How

- **engine:** `ViewInfo` gains `stroke_in_front`, the toolbox state the UI passes with each pointer event, and the tool context carries it.
- **tools:** `ToolContext::stroke_in_front`. When it's set, the Eyedropper's `color.sample` gets `target: stroke`, which `object.color` already supports for objects and for selected text.
- **ui:** the toolbox's Fill/Stroke proxy keeps `DesignApp::stroke_in_front` up to date when it's drawn and when it's clicked.

ROADMAP updated.

## Before / after

A line (6 pt, [Black]) selected, Stroke box in front (click it); Eyedropper on the dress:

| Before (#572): the colour goes to the line's fill, nothing shows | After: the line's stroke is the sampled red |

| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/eyedropper-stroke/before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/eyedropper-stroke/after.png) |

## Tests

title: feat(text): select sentence, paragraph and story on 3, 4 and 5 clicks
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #622.

The canvas took the double-click from egui's `button_double_clicked`, which egui reports on the *release* of the second click, while the canvas only looks for it on the *press*: so unless both landed in the same frame, a double-click was just two plain clicks, and egui stops counting at three anyway. The canvas now counts presses itself (each within egui's double-click delay and click distance of the previous one) and passes the count on `PointerEvent::clicks`. The Type tool maps it to 2 = word (unchanged `text.selectWord`), 3 = sentence, 4 = paragraph, 5 = the whole story, threaded frames included, through three new commands (`text.selectSentence`, `text.selectParagraph`, `text.selectStory`). A sentence ends at `.` `!` `?` `…` (plus closing quotes/brackets) followed by a space or the paragraph end, or at a CJK full stop, and takes its trailing spaces.

One difference from InDesign: there a triple click selects the line by default (Preferences > Type > "Triple Click to Select a Line"), and the paragraph comes at four. I followed the issue (sentence on three); happy to switch to the line, or to add that preference.

Validation:
- `canvas::tests::clicks_in_a_row_select_word_sentence_paragraph_and_story` (kittest, real presses at 60 fps): fails on main (`["", "", "", "", ""]`: not even the double-click selects the word), passes here
- `canvas::tests::slow_clicks_do_not_add_up`, `cmd::text::multi_click_tests::*` (sentence/paragraph bounds)
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-tools -p designcraft-engine -p designcraft-ui-egui -p designcraft-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: Autoflow: one frame per column, as the page's columns are set
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #625.

- Autoflow fills each column of the page with its own frame, threaded in order, then adds pages and does the same on each; on a two-column page the text no longer runs across the gutter. Right-to-left stories take the columns right to left.
- A frame the user drew or selected stays as it is; if it matches one of the page's columns, the columns after it on that page are filled first. Empty frames autoflow made at the end of the thread are removed (never a page's first frame).
- Smart Text Reflow adds one frame per page with the page's columns and gutter, like the primary text frames a new document gets, and removes a trailing page that holds only empty frames of the story.
- One-column documents and vertical stories behave as before.

Tests: the issue's two-column Letter repro (left-to-right and right-to-left binding): every frame equals its page's column, two per page; one column unchanged; a drawn frame is kept; Smart Text Reflow pages get the page's columns.

title: Type: Alt+Left/Right kerns at the caret and tracks a selection
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #621.

- With the Type tool, Alt+Left/Right changes the kerning between the two characters at the caret by the kerning/tracking increment, or the tracking of a selection; with Alt+Cmd (macOS) or Alt+Ctrl it changes by five times the increment. Each press is one undo step.
- Preferences › Units & Increments has Kerning/Tracking (1/1000 em, default 20), stored as the document's `kerningIncrement`.
- Word movement is Cmd+Left/Right on macOS and Ctrl+Left/Right elsewhere; Alt+Shift+Left/Right still extends the selection by words, and Alt+Backspace/Delete still delete words.
- New command `type.kernStep {steps?, amount?}`.
- A pair set to metrics or optical kerning starts from 0, since the font's pair value is applied during shaping.

Test: Alt+Right gives +20 and keeps the caret, a second press +40, undo back to +20; Alt+Cmd+Left gives −100; the increment preference applies; a selection gets tracking; Cmd+Right moves by a word; Alt+Shift+Right selects a word.

title: Text: stroke behind fill
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #619.

- A character setting draws the text's stroke outside the letters: the stroke is painted at twice its weight under the fill, so the full weight shows outside each glyph and the letter keeps its shape. Off, the stroke is centred on the outline as before.
- IDML `StrokeAlignment="OutsideAlignment"` / `CenterAlignment` on character ranges, character styles and paragraph styles import and export as this setting (the root paragraph style is Outside in nearly every IDML file, so imported stroked text needs it).
- Screen, PNG and PDF follow it; in PDF the fill stays real text, so text is copied once. With no fill, the stroke is clipped to the outside of the glyphs. Create Outlines gives paths with an outside stroke.
- Properties has a Stroke Behind Fill checkbox under the text Fill/Stroke, and Character Style Options › Character Color has it too.

Tests: native save only when set; IDML import/export of Outside, Center and absent; a render test (inner pixel is fill, outer is stroke; no fill keeps the inside empty); PDF paint order (stroke path before filled text, text extracted once).

title: Word import: bullets and numbering from numbering.xml
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #626.

- Placing a .docx reads `word/numbering.xml`: a paragraph's list comes from its own `numPr` or its paragraph style's (following `basedOn`), and becomes bullets or numbering with the level's format, label text, start value, separator (tab, space or nothing) and left/hanging indents. The paragraph's own indents win.
- Formats: bullet, decimal, decimal with leading zero, upper/lower roman, upper/lower letter, chicago; other formats fall back to decimal. Symbol and Wingdings bullets become the matching Unicode characters.
- Counters run per level and restart lower levels (`lvlRestart`); `num` instances of one abstract list share counters unless they override the start.
- A malformed or oversized `numbering.xml` leaves the paragraphs plain and adds one import warning.
- Not handled yet: `numStyleLink`, level alignment, the label's own font and size, level tab stops.

Tests: the issue's example (two bullets, two numbered items), nested levels with restarts and a start override, style-based lists, numId 0, Symbol/Wingdings bullets, and hostile numbering data.

title: Images: CMYK and profiled photos show in their colours
author: aiongg
body:
- CMYK JPEGs (including Adobe-inverted and YCCK), CMYK TIFFs and CMYK PSDs are converted for the screen through their embedded CMYK profile, else the working CMYK space from Color Settings, instead of a naive formula that made them look oversaturated.
- RGB and grey images with an embedded profile (Adobe RGB, Display P3, ProPhoto…) are converted to sRGB for display; untagged and sRGB images are unchanged. PSD ICC resources are read too.
- Display conversion uses the Color Settings intent and black point compensation.
- A damaged, oversized or mismatched profile is ignored with a log line; CMYK then falls back to the working space.
- The conversion sits in one module (`designcraft_images::colour`) with the same names as craft-cms (storytold/craft-libs#39), so moving to the shared crate is a dependency change. It uses moxcms, already a dependency.
- PDF export still embeds the original images and profiles; only the paths that already wrote decoded pixels now carry managed RGB.

Tests: a CMYK JPEG built in the test converts through the working space (not to the naive cyan), YCCK and non-APP14 variants; embedded vs working CMYK; an Adobe RGB PNG converts like the colour crate's float conversion while sRGB and untagged PNGs stay identical; a gamma-1.0 grey profile; damaged profiles leave pixels unchanged; PSD CMYK and an Adobe RGB PSD resource.

title: Color Picker and Color panel: typed values stay; colours are read on a fixed scale
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #323.

- The Color Picker's hex field keeps what is typed and applies the colour each time the text is a valid code (`#rgb`, `rrggbb`, with or without `#`); invalid text is replaced by the colour when the field loses focus. Its R/G/B and C/M/Y/K fields keep typed text too (C/M/Y/K are now fields, not a label).
- Color panel fields keep typed text and apply on Enter, on leaving the field or at the end of a drag; a dragged value is no longer lost on release.
- Colours from the panel, the spectrum and the picker are sent as `{model: rgb|cmyk|gray, …}` fractions and read without guessing: M 1% no longer applies 100% magenta. The bare forms keep their documented scales.
- The picker keeps a CMYK colour CMYK when picking on the square, the hue slider or by hex (converted through the working CMYK space); typing R/G/B makes it RGB, typing C/M/Y/K makes it CMYK. OK without edits leaves the fill and its swatch alone.
- A colour whose name rounds to an existing process swatch reuses it instead of adding a near-duplicate "… 3".
- Dialogs no longer dim the page behind them.

Tests: hex typing keeps text and commits once valid, invalid text restores on blur; typed channel values are kept; CMYK stays CMYK unless RGB is typed; OK without edits; the model form is read as fractions; rounding-equal colours share a swatch; dialogs leave the page undimmed; the panel's typed M 1 applies 1%.

title: Text frames: lines follow an oval or polygon frame's shape
author: aiongg
body:
Fixes #646.

- In a text frame whose path isn't a rectangle (ovals, polygons, corner options, freeform closed paths), each line takes the part of the outline that its whole band covers, kept the top inset inside the outline. Bands narrower than 1.5 em get no line; text continues below. Each column of a multi-column frame follows the outline.
- Text wraps from other objects still apply on top of the shape. Concave shapes use the widest interval, the same rule as wrap.
- Reshaping or resizing the frame reflows the text. Rectangular frames, including rectangles with extra collinear points, lay out exactly as before.
- Vertical frames follow the shape in the turned box.
- Vertical justification, paragraph shading and column rules still use the rectangular text area.

Tests: lines inside an ellipse (first line narrower, no slot under 1.5 em), inset clearance, a triangle whose lines widen downward, rectangular paths unchanged, resizing reflows, a vertical oval, multi-column ovals, and degenerate outlines (collinear, NaN, huge) without panics.

title: fix(cmd): reject unknown spread values instead of falling back to page 1
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #651.

Commands that create items already accept a parent spread as `"spread": {"kind": "parent", "index": 0}` (the serialized `SpreadRef`, the same form the tools send), but nothing said so. And the shared `spread_param` turned anything it couldn't read into spread 0, so `"spread": "A-Parent"` (or `"0"`, `-1`, `{"kind": "master"}`) put the item on page 1 without an error. I made `spread_param` strict: a body spread index, `{kind: doc|parent, index}` or absent (spread 0), and anything else is a `BadParams` error. That's the check `guides.rs` already did on its own, so the guide commands now use the shared one. This covers `frame.create`, `frame.grid`, `line.create`, `path.create`, `file.place`, `place.drop`, `snippet.place`, `story.placeAndLink`, `math.insert`, `object.qrCode`, `gap.move` and `guide.liquid`. I also documented the parent form in `frame.create`'s params and in `docs/mcp.md`.

I kept the existing `SpreadRef` form rather than adding a `"parent": "A"` prefix param or a `layout.parents.activate` mode, because that's how the commands and tools already address spreads. Happy to switch if you'd rather address parents by prefix.

Still open from the acceptance list in the comments: `edit.paste*` takes no `spread` at all (it always pastes on spread 0), and `type.onPath` follows its path's spread, so neither can target a parent yet.

Validation:
- `cmd::object::spread_target_tests::creating_on_a_parent_spread_and_rejecting_unknown_spreads`: fails on main (`frame.create {"spread": "A-Parent"}` is accepted), passes here
- `cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib -- spread_target_tests cmd::guides cmd::variables cmd::overrides cmd::datamerge cmd::library cmd::linked cmd::layout` (41 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(cli): accept a UTF-8 BOM in scripts and document the syntax in script --help
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #654.

`script::parse` trims the text before splitting it into steps, but `str::trim` doesn't treat U+FEFF as whitespace, so a file saved as "UTF-8 with BOM" kept the BOM in front of the first command id. `parse` now drops a leading BOM before anything else. Every entry point (`script FILE`, `script -`, `script.run {text}`, MCP `batch`) goes through it, so all of them are fixed. CRLF already worked because `lines()` strips the `\r`, and the new test pins both together. `script --help` / `-h` now prints a syntax reference to stdout and exits 0, the same way the top-level `--help` does. It covers the line forms, `$N` as the 0-based step index (comments aren't steps), paths through fields and array indices (`$1.story`, `$3.ids.0`), `\n` for a paragraph and ` ` for a forced line break, and the fact that most commands ignore unknown parameters. docs/agents.md says the same, and the README points to `script --help`.

Thanks @DanielGemm for the correction on ` `: the code agrees (`FORCED_LINE_BREAK`). I left out the two related points from that comment, accepting or rejecting `\u000b` and making `story.setText` treat `\r` the way `frame.create` does. They're in the text commands rather than the script parser, and the first needs a call on accept vs reject. Happy to send them as a follow-up. The same goes for rejecting unknown parameters (#651): for now this only documents the current behaviour.

Validation:
- `script::tests::a_leading_bom_and_crlf_parse_like_plain_text`: fails on main (first step parses as `"\u{feff}file.new"`), passes here
- `cli::script_help_documents_the_syntax`: fails on main (``unknown script option `--help` ``), passes here
- `cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib script::`, `cargo test -p designcraft-cli --test cli`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine -p designcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: macOS: open the window on Intel Metal by skipping indirect-call validation
author: fabian-co
body:
## What this changes

On a Mac whose integrated GPU is an Intel Iris Pro (MacBookPro11,3, macOS 12.7.6), DesignCraft can't open its window when it draws on that GPU: the device is lost and the process exits. On this dual-GPU machine the default picks the NVIDIA GPU, so it shows with `WGPU_POWER_PREF=low`; a Mac with only that Intel GPU has no other Metal adapter to fall to.

The cause is wgpu's indirect-call validation: when the device is created, wgpu compiles a compute shader to validate indirect draw/dispatch arguments, and Metal's Intel compiler aborts on it. The log shows:

```
ERROR [main] wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("new_compute_pipeline_state: NSError { code: 2, localizedDescription: \"Compiler encountered an internal error\", domain: \"CompilerError\", .. }"))
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
```

and each attempt leaves `MTLCompilerService` crash reports ending in `IGILErrorMessageHandlers::reportUnsupportedMaxWorkGroupSizeMetadataError` (libIGIL-Metal).

DesignCraft draws and dispatches nothing indirectly (no `draw_indirect`, `draw_indexed_indirect`, `multi_draw_*` or `dispatch_workgroups_indirect` in `apps/` or `crates/`), so this removes `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` from the window instance's flags. `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=1` turns it back on. This is the same fix VectorCraft already has (storytold/vectorcraft#651); PhotoCraft and LightCraft skip the check too.

Docs: a row for the variable in the README's environment table. No asset or dependency change.

- `cargo clippy --locked -p designcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- No new test: the setup is inline in `main`, so there is nothing to call from a test without restructuring it. Say if you want it pulled into a function with one.

title: Honor quoted fields when detecting data-source delimiters and records
author: sanyamsingh001
body:

Bare-CR endings can collapse records, and multiline quoted surplus fields can create phantom records. Track logical headers and field-start/quote state independently of cell retention, recognizing LF, CRLF and CR boundaries while preserving quoted newlines. Delimiter inference uses each candidate's own quote state and prefers consistent quoted-field boundaries, including trailing header whitespace. Explicit delimiters and known filename extensions retain precedence.

title: fix(import): preserve XLSX numeric and cached text values
author: storybored379
body:
XLSX imports rounded fractional values to ten decimal places, turning `1e-12` into `0` and overflowing large finite numbers. Cached formula strings also passed through numeric conversion, so `00123` became `123`.

Show numbers the way Excel's General format does: up to 15 significant digits (so a cached `0.30000000000000004` from `=0.1+0.2` reads `0.3`), whole numbers without `.0`, and an exponent for very large or small values (`1E+300`, `1E-12`). Honor `t="str"` for cached text. This covers both placed tables and Excel data-merge records. Cached formula strings follow [ECMA-376 Part 3, §3.16.10](https://download.microsoft.com/download/e/1/4/e14fb96f-83b8-4a2a-84db-7fa8acbe061a/Office%20Open%20XML%20Part%203%20-%20Primer.pdf).

title: Parents: a parent can be based on another parent
author: aiongg
body:
- A page whose parent B is based on A draws A's items, then B's, then its own. This holds on the canvas (including on B itself while editing parents), in PDF and image export, in snapping, and in the flattener's check for transparent parent items. Chains (C on B on A) are followed base first, with a depth bound.
- On B itself, A's page-number markers show B's prefix.
- `layout.parents.options {"parent": "B", "basedOn": "A" | null}` sets or clears the base. It takes a prefix or label like the other parent commands, is undoable, and refuses a base that would make a cycle, however long. `document.inspect` reports `basedOn` per parent.
- `layout.overrideParentItems` and Cmd+Shift-click reach items that come from A. The click hits what is drawn: it respects Show Parent Items, hidden and locked layers, facing pages and layer order.
- Opening a `.designcraft` or IDML file clears a cyclic or dangling base with a warning, so the open still succeeds.
- IDML already wrote and read the base as the parent pages' `AppliedMaster`. A test now covers the round trip. Import warns when a parent spread's pages name different bases (the first page's is kept) or name their own spread.
- There is no Parent Options dialog in the Pages panel yet, so this adds the command only. Overriding A's items on B itself is not supported yet (docs/gaps.md).

Tests: draw order A under B under page items (pixels), B showing A's items, PDF export of both parents' items in order, markers on B, a chain of three, cycles refused by the command and broken on open (`.designcraft`, IDML, and a 65-parent cycle), a dangling base, IDML round trip, overriding A items on single and facing pages, hitting A's items under B's, undo.

Closes #652

title: Styles: object styles carry effects
author: aiongg
body:
- An object style can hold effects (drop shadow, feather, inner shadow, outer glow, inner glow, bevel, satin, gradient and directional feather). A style without effects leaves items' effects alone, as before; documents saved without style effects open unchanged.
- `style.object.create {"fromSelection": true}` keeps the selection's effects. `style.object.create` also takes `effects` and the per-effect keys (`dropShadow`, `feather`, …) to set them without a selection.
- `style.object.apply` gives the items the style's effects. New frames that get a default object style take its effects too. Render and PDF draw the item's effects, so they show the style's effects or the item's own.
- `style.object.edit {"name": "Photo", "dropShadow": {"size": 20}}` changes the style's effects. Effect objects merge field by field into what the style has. Items using the style whose effects still match the style's take the new effects; items with their own effects keep them. When the style didn't set effects before, only the items without effects of their own take them, so editing a default style doesn't wipe shadows set on frames. `"effects": null` makes the style stop setting effects. One undo step; returns how many items changed; no undo step when nothing changes.
- Effect values that aren't finite numbers are refused, and the others are clamped (opacities 0–1, percentages 0–100, sizes, widths and distances not below 0). This applies to these commands and to the existing `object.*` effect commands, so a document can't end up with a value it can't save and open again.
- `style.object.clearOverrides {ids?}` gives items their style's fill, stroke, effects and text frame options again.
- IDML carries only the drop shadow and feather, for styles as for items. Export writes them to the ObjectStyle `TransparencySetting`, with `ObjectStyleObjectEffectsCategorySettings` saying whether the style sets them. An item whose style sets effects writes its own drop shadow and feather even when they ar…

title: Check transformed image resolution during preflight
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
In a Print document, enlarging a raster placed at 300 PPI fourfold through a parent group currently evades the default 150 PPI preflight warning; height-only enlargement can also go undetected. Accumulate ancestor, frame and image transforms in rendering order and use the lower PPI of the two transformed image axes. This produces one low-resolution warning per affected raster, evaluating the fourfold enlargement at 75 PPI. Use ancestor-transformed frame bounds to attach these warnings to the correct facing page.

Synthetic regression cases cover nested and noncommuting transforms, height-only scaling, rotation and reflection, cropping versus content fitting, threshold equality, SVG exclusion, print intent, and query-state preservation. Existing PDF/SVG exclusions, Print-only gating and strict threshold comparison remain: resolution equal to the threshold produces no low-resolution warning.

Adobe's [effective-PPI scaling explanation](https://helpx.adobe.com/indesign/kb/indesign-links-panel-fails-show.html) documents inverse scaling of effective resolution, and its [Preflight panel guide](https://helpx.adobe.com/indesign/desktop/print/preflight/configure-and-use-the-preflight-panel.html) describes resolution checks. The transform order and two-axis calculation follow DesignCraft's rendering geometry.

title: Embed craft-fonts by default via .cargo/config.toml [env]
author: sblount2025-design
body:
A plain `cargo build --release` from a clean clone silently produces a CJK-blind binary. build.rs warns and carries on:

```
warning: no craft-fonts embedded: Chinese and Japanese text will render as empty
boxes. Clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts next to this repo and
rebuild with CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts
```

With craft-fonts already cloned beside the repo exactly as the warning asks, the build *still* needs `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` passed by hand on every invocation. A build-time requirement that lives only in a warning is one that gets forgotten, and then comes back as a bug report about missing glyphs.

This adds it to `.cargo/config.toml`:

```toml
[env]
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR = { value = "../craft-fonts", relative = true }
```

**This is not a new convention — it mirrors `deckcraft/.cargo/config.toml`, which already ships this exact block.** The other craft apps that read `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` don't, which is the inconsistency this closes.

Properties:

- `relative = true` resolves against the repo root, so no absolute path is committed.
- No `force`, so a `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` already in the environment still wins for a one-off build against a different font set.
- If craft-fonts is **not** cloned beside the repo, behaviour is unchanged — build.rs warns exactly as it does today.
- The existing `[alias]` entry is untouched.

## Verification

Built with the variable explicitly removed from the environment, so only the config could supply it:

```
env -u CRAFT_FONTS_DIR cargo build --release
```

The crate recompiled and the "no craft-fonts embedded" warning did not appear. Tested on macOS (Apple silicon), Rust 1.99.0, against craft-fonts at its current main.

title: New Document: Preview
author: aiongg
body:
Stacked on #325 (New Document window); review after it.

- A Preview checkbox beside Close and Create. It is off by default and keeps its state for the session.
- With Preview on, a document with the window's settings shows in the workspace behind it: page size, orientation, page count, facing pages, margins, columns and gutter, bleed and slug. Turning Preview on shows it at once; after that it is rebuilt once the fields have stayed the same for 200 ms. An empty, half-typed or negative field, or a size `file.new` refuses (a zero width), keeps the last preview, and a refused size is not retried until it changes.

If `file.new` fails, the window comes back with the error.
- Close, Escape, `ui.dialog.cancel`, turning Preview off, or another dialog replacing the window removes the preview. If the preview was still the active document, the previously active one is shown again; a document opened or activated meanwhile stays active.

It takes no Untitled number, never touches the other documents, and recovery saves skip it. title: Bump quick-xml to 0.41: linear-time attribute check on .docx/.xlsx import (RUSTSEC-2026-0194, -0195)
author: natocool2
body:
Bumps quick-xml from 0.38 to 0.41, which fixes two advisories:

- [RUSTSEC-2026-0194](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0194.html): `Attributes` with the default `with_checks(true)` takes O(N²) time on a start tag with N attributes.
- [RUSTSEC-2026-0195](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0195.html): `NsReader` allocates for every `xmlns` declaration on a tag with no limit.

**Exposure today.** 0194 is reachable: `crates/textimport/src/docx.rs` `parse` (used for .docx and .xlsx import) and `crates/engine/src/dtd.rs` `read_tree` iterate attributes with the default duplicate check. A file with one start tag carrying a very large number of attributes keeps the import busy for seconds to minutes (80,000 attributes is about 6 s in a release build, per the advisory), and in the web build that freezes the tab. 0195 is not reachable (no `NsReader` in the workspace). `crates/idml` already uses `with_checks(false)`.

## Changes

- `Cargo.toml`: `quick-xml = "0.41"`.
- `crates/idml/src/xml.rs`, `crates/textimport/src/docx.rs`: `unescape_value()` is deprecated in 0.40+ (and `clippy -D warnings` would fail). It is replaced with `normalized_value(XmlVersion::Implicit1_0)`, which is the call the deprecated method now makes.
- New test `an_element_with_many_attributes_parses_in_linear_time` (textimport): one `<w:p>` with 100,000 attributes must parse in under 5 s, and the first and last attributes must be read. With 0.38 this is quadratic. With 0.41 it is linear, because the duplicate check uses a hash pre-filter for large tags.

## How this was checked

- The quick-xml API used here was diffed between 0.38.4 and 0.41.0 (`Reader`/`Config` fields, `Event` variants, `BytesStart`/`BytesText`/`BytesRef`, `escape`): the only changes that touch this workspace are the deprecations above. `Attribute::normalized_value*` is exactly what the deprecated methods call in 0.41, so behaviour is the same as a plain bump. title: Create Outlines makes one compound path per line, so Ungroup separates the lines
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

In InDesign, Type › Create Outlines on a text frame gives a group with one compound path per line. Ungroup then leaves each line as its own object, so you can move the lines apart or together, and Object › Paths › Make Compound Path joins them again.

LYH Studio's "Good Morning" tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TkF_y1nf8EE)) does exactly this. On main, Create Outlines makes one compound path per text colour across all the lines. A one-colour title becomes a single path, so Ungroup does nothing and the lines can't be spaced.

`create_outlines` (engine, `cmd/paths.rs`) keys the glyph outlines by line as well as by look (fill, tint, stroke, stroke tint, weight). Each line's glyphs, split by colour within the line, become one compound path. Several parts are grouped as before; a single line in one colour is still a single compound path. The command's help text and the ROADMAP are updated.

title: Ungroup leaves frames with pasted-in content whole; name them by their shape
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

A frame with an image or objects pasted into it (Edit › Paste Into) isn't a group. In InDesign:
- the Properties panel and Layers panel name it by its shape (Ellipse, Rectangle…);
- it has no Ungroup quick action;
- Object › Ungroup leaves it whole.

On main, any item holding nested items counts as a group:
- Properties titles a pasted-into ellipse "Group" and offers **Ungroup**;
- clicking it (or Object › Ungroup) removes the frame and leaves its content loose on the page, losing the clipping shape;
- Ungroup on objects that aren't groups also clears the selection.

LYH Studio's "Good Morning" tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TkF_y1nf8EE)) pastes photos into compound paths made from outlined text (5:56, 9:02). Selecting one of those afterwards on main shows "Group" with an Ungroup button that would destroy it.

## How

title: Copy a selected placed graphic on its own, so Paste Into puts the whole image in place
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

In InDesign, when you select a placed image itself (Direct Selection, or double-clicking into the frame until the inner, brown bounding box shows) and Copy, the clipboard gets **just the image**: all of it, uncropped, where it sits on the page, without the frame's stroke or fill. Paste Into a shape then puts the whole picture in place inside it. Delete with the image selected removes the image and keeps the empty frame.

LYH Studio's "Good Morning" tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TkF_y1nf8EE)) relies on this. At 5:44 it says to click into the image "till you see that secondary border show up" and copy it. At 5:56 it pastes into the outlined title, adding that "wherever the picture is … it's going to paste it right in that same location". At 9:02 it does the same with the second title.

On main, `edit.copy` ignores the content selection and copies the whole frame: cropped, with its stroke and effects. Pasting into a shape then shows the frame's cropped rectangle and its stroke. Delete with the image selected deletes the frame.

## How

- `clip_doc` (engine, `cmd/edit.rs`) handles a content selection (`Selection.content`) of a graphic frame with the new `graphic_alone`. It makes a rectangle the size of the whole graphic, with transform `parent × frame × graphic`. Its graphic has an identity transform, no fitting and no crop. The frame's fill, stroke, effects and object style don't come along.
- Every copied item now keeps its spread position, nested ones included (the parent transform is applied). Before, a nested item, such as one selected inside a group, was copied with its local transform.
- `edit.clear` with the graphic selected (and no explicit `ids`) empties the frame and keeps it selected; other selected items are still deleted. Cut follows, since it copies and then clears.

title: Effects apply to frames with pasted-in content (Inner Glow, Basic Feather, shadows…)
author: moppeeer
body:
## What

In InDesign, effects apply to the whole object they're set on. A frame holding an image or objects pasted into it (Edit › Paste Into) feathers, glows and casts shadows as one object.

LYH Studio's "Good Morning" tutorial ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TkF_y1nf8EE)) does this at 11:51–12:23. It pastes the photo into the outlined "GET MORE." title, then gives the title an Inner Glow (Screen, white, 75 %, 0.25 in) and a Basic Feather (0.0625 in) for a "softer look".

On main the effects are stored but never drawn on such a frame. `draw_item` handled frames with nested items in a branch of their own that drew the fill, the clipped items and the stroke, and returned before any effect.

## How

- `draw_item` (render) sends a frame with pasted-in items down the same path as every other object. Opacity and blend layers and culling include the effects' reach, and `draw_item_fx` runs when the frame has effects.
- `draw_body` draws pasted-in items as content: clipped by the frame, between its fill and its stroke, as before. Every effect therefore wraps the fill, the content and the stroke together: drop shadow, outer and inner glow, inner shadow, bevel, satin, and basic, directional and gradient feather.
- Shadows and glows treat the frame's silhouette as solid (their spread grows it), as for an image frame.
- ROADMAP progress log updated.

**Not included:** PDF export has no soft effects (glows, feathers, inner shadow) for any object on main. That's a separate, larger change.

title: fix(tables): keep each table anchor in its own paragraph
author: noah1400
body:
Fixes #686.

## Summary
- Backspace at the start of the second of two consecutive tables merged their anchor paragraphs: one table was dropped and the remaining paragraph held two anchors. Saving worked; reopening failed with `paragraph must hold exactly one anchor`.
- Pasting a table right next to an anchor replaced the existing table the same way. Pasting several paragraphs right before an anchor left its table unreferenced (`1 tables but 0 anchored`), with the same reopen failure.

## Fix
- `fix_tables` now splits a table paragraph that holds further anchors, so every anchor gets its own paragraph again.
- `Story::delete` and `Story::insert_story` tell it which table each surviving anchor belongs to (`fix_tables_with`). Before, they kept one table id per merged paragraph and lost the other.
- `insert_story` fixes tables up once after the whole paste instead of after every run, so a split can't shift the rest of the paste.

Side effect: after Backspace between two tables, the second table's paragraph takes the first one's paragraph format (merged paragraphs keep the first one's format). Undo restores it.

## Tests
- doc: Backspace between two tables, deleting the middle of three, pasting a table before/after an anchor, paragraphs pasted before an anchor.
- engine: `text.delete` and `edit.paste` through commands, then a file round-trip.
- All new tests failed before the fix. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch (fmt, clippy, test, assets, layers, wasm).
