title: Type: formatting set on a blank line applies to the text typed there
author: aiongg
body:
- With the caret on a blank line (an empty paragraph), `type.char` formatted only the line's paragraph mark. Text typed next took the previous paragraph's format instead, so a size, leading or bold chosen there was lost on the typed text.
- The blank line's paragraph mark still takes the format right away (it sets that line's height), and the format is also kept as the typing format at the caret.
- Text inserted on a blank line takes that line's paragraph mark format (`Story::insert_format_at`), so the format also holds after the caret leaves the line and comes back, after undo or after reopening the file. Every other caret position keeps taking the format of the character before it. Typing with Track Changes on and the Character panel's reading at the caret use the same rule.

Follow-up to #949.

Tests: `cmd::text::open_type_tests::text_typed_on_a_blank_line_takes_the_format_set_there` (sets size 30 on the blank line between two paragraphs, types "Middle", checks the typed text and its mark have size 30 and the first paragraph's mark does not) and `cmd::text::open_type_tests::a_blank_lines_mark_format_is_typed_after_the_caret_returns` (the same after moving the caret away and back, with no typing format pending); `leading_applies_to_an_empty_lines_hidden_paragraph_mark` no longer asserts that no typing format is pending.

title: Effects: wide feathers and inner effects stay sharp at high zoom
author: aiongg
body:
- A blur wider than 1,024 device pixels is drawn offscreen at a reduced resolution. Basic Feather drew the whole object in that offscreen image, so a wide feather (for example 200 pt at 400% on a 2x screen) made the object itself look blurry. Inner shadow, inner glow, satin and bevel clipped to the shape inside the reduced image, so their edge was coarse and bled outside the shape.
- `with_filters` takes an optional clip (path and transform). At reduced resolution it clips the composited image on the device context; at full resolution it clips as before. The inner effects pass their shape as that clip.
- Basic Feather draws the object and its clip on the device context and only renders the blurred mask through `with_filters`.
- Effects whose blur fits at full resolution render as before.

Follow-up to #912.

Tests: `a_wide_feather_keeps_the_object_sharp_at_high_zoom` (the inside of a 1,000 pt feathered frame at 8 px/pt matches the unfeathered frame) and `a_wide_inner_effect_stays_inside_the_shape_at_high_zoom` (a 2,000 pt inner shadow and inner glow at 8 px/pt leave the pixels just outside the shape's edge unchanged), both in `crates/render/tests/effects.rs`.

title: Typography panel: every OpenType toggle, exported figure styles, working Standard Ligatures
author: aiongg
body:
- Proportional Metrics, Horizontal Kana, Localized Forms, Mark Positioning, Justification Alternates and Roman Italics had no control for local text after the OpenType menu became the Typography panel. A new Other Features section lists every character-format toggle (`otf::TOGGLES`) the other sections don't show, when the selection's fonts offer it.
- Lining, Oldstyle, Tabular or Proportional chosen alone set one tag, which IDML export wrote as `OTFFigureStyle="Default"`. Choosing one now also sets the other axis: the choice all of the selection already has, else Proportional (for a style) or Lining (for a width). Turning a checked one off clears both axes, back to the font's default figures.
- Standard Ligatures showed checked with Character › Ligatures off, and checking it couldn't turn ligatures back on; its `-liga` was also dropped by IDML export. The switch now reads and sets the `ligatures` attribute (`type.char`), and `type.openTypeFeatures` reports `liga` from it. `liga` stays out of the feature list, and a `-liga` already there (from `type.feature`) counts as off and is cleared when the switch is used.

Follow-up to #881.

Tests: `panels::typography::tests::every_character_format_toggle_has_a_control`, `panels::typography::tests::a_figure_style_or_width_chosen_alone_exports_as_a_figure_style` (clicks Lining, Tabular, Oldstyle and checks the exported `OTFFigureStyle`), `panels::typography::tests::standard_ligatures_switch_the_ligatures_attribute`, `panels::typography::tests::standard_ligatures_switch_on_clears_a_feature_list_liga_off`, `cmd::text::open_type_features_tests::standard_ligatures_follow_the_ligatures_attribute`.

title: Paths: Join and Convert Point respect locked layers and groups
author: aiongg
body:
- `path.join` and `path.convertPoints` checked only the path's own lock, so they closed, joined or reshaped a path on a locked layer or inside a locked group.
- Both now use the same check as the other path edits: a path that is locked, on a locked layer or in a locked group is left unchanged. Join refuses with "the path is locked" when no selected path is editable, or when two are selected and either is locked (it no longer closes the editable one instead); Convert Point does the same when none of its points is editable, and otherwise converts only the editable ones.

Follow-up to #960.

Tests: `joining_two_paths_with_one_on_a_locked_layer_changes_neither` (in `cmd::object`); `path_edits_leave_a_path_on_a_locked_layer_alone` and `path_edits_leave_a_path_in_a_locked_group_alone` (in `cmd::object`) now include `path.join` and `path.convertPoints`; all three fail before the fix.

title: Kerning: a value at the caret kerns the pair at the caret
author: aiongg
body:
- A kerning value or preset chosen in the Character panel or Properties with a bare caret in text was stored only as the format for the next typing, so the pair at the caret did not move.
- New command `type.kernPair {kerning}`: at a caret it sets the kerning of the character before the caret (manual kerning is added after a character, so that character spaces the pair), in one undo step. At the start or end of a story or paragraph there is no pair and the value is kept for the next typing. A selection or selected frames take it exactly as `type.char` does.
- The Kerning control in both panels calls it, and at a caret its label shows the pair's current kerning.

Follow-up to #901.

Tests: `kern_pair_tests::kerning_at_a_caret_kerns_the_pair_in_one_undo_step`, `kern_pair_tests::kerning_a_selection_or_at_the_story_start_works_like_type_char` (engine), `a_manual_kerning_value_at_a_caret_kerns_the_pair` (ui-egui Character panel).

title: Type tool: a drag after several clicks extends the selection by words, lines or paragraphs (#981)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #981

## Before
A double click selected a word (triple a line, quadruple a paragraph), but holding the button and moving did nothing: `TypeTool` set `unit_selected` on the press and returned no action for every `Drag` while it was set. In InDesign the drag grows the selection a word (line, paragraph) at a time, in either direction, anchored on the unit first selected.

## Change
- Engine (`crates/engine/src/cmd/text.rs`, `lib.rs`): `text.selectAt` records the unit it selected (`Session::text_unit`). `text.extendTo` takes an optional `unit: word|line|paragraph|story`; with it, and after a `text.selectAt` in the same story/cell, the selection becomes whole units from the first unit to the unit under the point: forward, anchor = start of the first unit, focus = end of the unit under the point (never shrinking inside the first unit); backward, anchor = end of the first unit, focus = start of the unit under the point. The unit computation moved into `unit_at` (shared by both commands; an unknown unit is the same error). Without `unit` nothing changes.
- Tool (`crates/tools/src/text.rs`): the press keeps the unit its click count chose and every drag sends `text.extendTo {frame, point, unit}`; a single-click drag still sends it without `unit`. Table cell drags are untouched.

## Tests
- `multi_click_tests::a_drag_after_several_clicks_extends_the_selection_by_units` (engine): double-click "brave", extend into "world." → `(7, 18)`; back inside the word → `(7, 12)`; into "Hello" → `(12, 0)`; triple-click the first line, extend into the second → the whole text; a drag without `unit` still moves the focus by characters; `unit: sentence` is an error.
- `clicks_in_a_row_edit_and_select_text` (tools): a drag after two presses emits `text.extendTo` with `unit: "word"`, after three with `"line"`, after one without `unit` (it previously asserted the drag emitted nothing).

title: Importers: XML element nesting and DTD group nesting are bounded (#712)
author: wstock
body:
Addresses #712 for three of its four sites; the fourth (math arguments/groups, `crates/engine/src/math.rs`) already carries `MAX_NESTING` on `main` and is unchanged here.

## What was unbounded
- `textimport::docx::parse` and `idml::xml::parse` build the element tree iteratively (a stack), so parsing itself never recursed — but `El::text()`, the block walk and the tree's `Drop` all recurse one frame per level. A document nested a few hundred thousand levels deep parses fine and overflows the stack the first time anything walks it; `catch_unwind` does not recover a stack overflow.
- `engine::dtd::particle` recurses once per `(` group with no budget: `<!ELEMENT a ((((…b…))))>` with enough parens overflows while parsing.

## Change
- `textimport::docx::MAX_DEPTH = 256` and `idml::xml::MAX_DEPTH = 256`: a `Start` event that would push past it is an error (`XML elements nested deeper than 256 levels`, with the position for IDML), before the element is built. Word's and InDesign's own XML stays well under a hundred levels.
- `dtd::MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 64`: `particle` takes the enclosing group depth and refuses a group past it (`content-model groups nested deeper than 64 levels`); real content models are single digits deep.

Nothing changes for input inside the budgets; the error paths are the parsers' existing `Corrupt` / `String` errors, so importers report them like any other malformed input.

## Tests (budget and budget+1, as the issue suggests; no real stack exhaustion)
- `docx::tests::nesting_past_the_budget_is_refused` — 256 nested `<w:p>` parse, 257 are refused with the message, 100 000 are refused.
- `xml::tests::nesting_past_the_budget_is_refused` (idml) — the same for `<A>`.
- `dtd::tests::content_model_groups_past_the_budget_are_refused` — 64 nested groups parse, 65 are refused, 100 000 are refused.

`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport -p designcraft-idml --lib` (24 + 92), `cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib dtd::`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-textimport -p…

title: Tools: Cmd held with another tool borrows the Selection tool for one gesture (#919)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes #919

## What InDesign does
With the Type tool (or any drawing tool) chosen, holding Cmd (Ctrl on Windows) turns the pointer into the Selection tool for as long as the button is down: you can click to select a frame, drag it, or pull a handle without going to the Tools panel. With the Pen family and the Pencil, Cmd gives the Direct Selection tool instead. Releasing the button leaves the chosen tool in place.

## Change (`crates/engine/src/tooling.rs`, one field in `lib.rs`)

title: Scaling a text frame scales its text, as InDesign's When Scaling: Apply to Content
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while replaying Dansky's *Masking with Exclude Overlap InDesign Tutorial* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TYzFYxJN-Rg)). At 2:16 he Cmd+Shift-drags the corner of the "LEARN" text frame: "you can see it will scale it proportionately, so this is a really quick way to scale text up or down". In InDesign the text grows from 70 pt and the frame still shows 100%.

## Problem
DesignCraft put the scale on the frame (Transform panel: 214.3%) and the Character panel still read 70 pt. The text only looked bigger. Type › Create Outlines, the Character panel and text added later all worked from 70 pt, and the frame's 1 pt stroke turned into 2.143 pt.

## Change
Scaling a text frame with its content now works like InDesign's default *When Scaling: Apply to Content*:
- **The frame:** its path takes the scale, so it shows 100%.
- **Character attributes** follow the vertical scale:
  - point size, absolute leading and baseline shift;
  - the text stroke weight (stroked text only);
  - underline and strikethrough weights and offsets, when they are set.
- **Horizontal scale** takes the difference between the two axes (a frame made wider than high).
- **Paragraph attributes:** left, right, first-line and last-line indents follow the horizontal scale; space before and after follow the vertical scale.
- **Where it applies:**
  - a handle drag with Cmd (`transform.resize {content: true}`);
  - the Scale command (`transform.scale`);
  - the Transform panel's scale fields (`transform.set {scaleX, scaleY}`).
- **Unchanged:** these cases keep the old behaviour, with the scale on the frame as a whole:
  - a story threaded through other frames;
  - vertical text;
  - a scale that flips the frame, or isn't along its own axes.
- One undo step, as before.

Not done: InDesign's *Adjust Scaling Percentage* preference (keep the scale on the frame and show "70 pt (154 pt)"). Liquid Layout's scale rule still scales text frames as a whole.

title: IDML: preserve liquid guides on document and parent pages
author: keynepekar
body:
IDML currently imports every guide as a ruler guide and exports every guide as `GuideType="Ruler"`. A guide-based layout therefore loses its adaptive guides after interchange. Preserve `GuideType="Liquid"` in the existing shared page mapping, on document and parent pages. Ordinary, omitted and unrecognized types retain the existing ruler-guide behavior.

Regression tests use hand-written XML independent of the exporter, inspect literal exported attributes, and round-trip mixed horizontal/vertical guides. They cover spread/page/spine ruler origins, page/spread scope, positions, locks, layers, and liquid guides on a page whose adaptive rule is off. Both new tests fail before the two-line production fix.

Refs #872 (liquid guides only). #972 already handles stored page rules; object pins and resize constraints remain out of scope, so #872 should stay open. The relevant crate documentation, format-parity notes and progress log are updated.

Validation on Ubuntu/WSL, Rust 1.99.0:

- `cargo test --locked -p designcraft-idml liquid_guides -- --nocapture`: both tests pass; both fail on the original implementation.
- CLI smoke test: create two frames and a liquid guide, export IDML, reopen, create an alternate layout at twice the page width. The crossed frame grows from 200 to 400 pt; the other remains 100 pt.
- `cargo xtask ci`: all seven gates pass (fmt, clippy with warnings denied, 1,968 tests passed / 5 ignored, PDF dependency pins, assets, layers and WASM).
- `cargo check --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p designcraft-web`: passes.

No manual InDesign runtime verification was performed.

title: fix(text): Character panel: VF sliders preview live implementation
author: andrestelex
body:
Dragging a variable font axis slider previews the change on the page and commits it as one undo step when the slider is let go. The panel gathers what every axis slider did in a frame before acting, so with several axes a drag no longer commits and reopens the change on every frame. A click, an arrow key or a value typed in the field beside each slider applies at once. Narrow axes (Skia's weight runs 0.48-3.2) step by hundredths; a slider snapping a value that is off its steps no longer counts as a change.

Live previews are commands, so the panel stays on app.run: edit.preview {label, command, params} shows an edit on the document as it was before the preview began, edit.commitPreview makes it one undo step, edit.cancelPreview drops it. A preview no panel held in the last frame (its slider let go, or the panel closed) is committed at the start of the next one.

The Character panel drops its repeated heading, lays Size, Kerning and Baseline, and Leading and Tracking, out in two columns whose captions and fields line up, shows auto leading in parentheses, and shows a style with axis settings as its axes alone, here and in the Text Frame floating bar.

This is an update to previous pull request https://github.com/storytold/designcraft/pull/885

title: fix: IDML links in a subfolder beside the package load on another machine
author: Kerrrunchhh
body:
An IDML package opened away from its author's machine keeps image links such as `/images/logo.png` that don't exist on the new machine. Link lookup only tried the package folder and its `Links/` folder, so images kept in an `images/` folder next to the .idml showed as missing.

Link lookup now also tries the link's trailing folders under the package folder, longest first (at most 8 components): `/images/logo.png` finds `<package>/images/logo.png`.

- Regression test: `opens_links_from_a_subfolder_beside_the_package`
- Checked on a real 16-spread package: 22 links went from missing to ok
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers, wasm)
- ROADMAP.md progress-log entry added

title: feat(text): TextFrame: double-clicking handles fits to content
author: andrestelex
body:
Double-clicking a handle of the selected text frames fits them to their text: a corner fits the width and height, the top or bottom handle the height, a side handle the width. Object > Fitting > Fit Frame to Content (object.fit fitFrameToContent) now fits text frames too, with an `axes` parameter (both|width|height); the handles run it for every selected text frame, so fitting several is one undo step.

Fitting only shrinks a frame bigger than its text, measured by composing the story at trial sizes (alignment, indents, tabs, drop caps and wraps all count):
- the height is the smallest that keeps the frame's text, when the frame holds its story's end; text that runs on (overset, or into the next frame of its thread) keeps the frame's height, so it never stretches down a long story;
- the width shrinks only when no line wraps (every line ends at its paragraph or a break), to the narrowest that keeps every line as it is.

The text stays in place: the edge kept is the one the text sits against (left, right or centre) and, vertically, the frame's vertical justification. Rotated frames fit in their own space; insets stay around the text. Empty, locked, vertical and type-on-a-path frames are left alone.

On a one-line frame the threading ports sit on the side handles: a double click on a port with no link to break now reaches the handle under it.

title: Tables: Fit to Frame Width option, columns follow the text frame's width
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1025.

A table can now follow its text frame's width. InDesign users asked for this in the InDesign team's own table thread (https://redd.it/1luvoma, the reply with 134 points: "lock a table to 100% of the frame width").

**Behaviour**
- New table option **Fit to Frame Width** (`TableOptions::fit_to_frame`, default off). When it is on, composition scales the stored column widths by *available width / natural width* in both directions, so the table fills the text column (minus paragraph indents) and follows every frame resize, wider or narrower. Without the option nothing changes: a table is only scaled down when it is wider than the column, as before.
- The stored column widths are not rewritten; with the option on they act as proportions. Undo, save and reopen keep the option. It is written to the document only when on, so older files and readers are unaffected.
- `table.options` takes `fitToFrame: bool`; any other value is an error that leaves the table unchanged (the whole call is rejected). `table.get`/`table.options` report `options.fitToFrame` when it is on.
- Applying a table style keeps the option (styles set borders and fills field by field).
- Table panel: a "Fit to Frame Width" checkbox under "Repeat Header Rows".

**IDML:** InDesign has no equivalent table attribute, so this stays a DesignCraft-only option: IDML export writes the stored column widths and drops the flag. Noted in `docs/file-format-parity.md`.

**Tests** (test-first; both engine tests failed before the composition change)

title: idml: one unusable CJK metric no longer refuses the whole file
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Composite-font and mojikumi metrics are taken from the file with no sanity check (`crates/idml/src/import.rs:502`, `:536` — `El::num` at `crates/idml/src/xml.rs:96` has no filter), and `Document::check()` refuses exactly the values a hostile or merely unusual part can carry — a zero or non-finite `relative_size`/`horizontal_scale`/`vertical_scale`/`baseline_shift` (`crates/doc/src/lib.rs:734`) — with `import_idml` running that check on the finished document (`crates/idml/src/import.rs:93`). So `RelativeSize="0"` or `BaselineShift="NaN"` on one `CompositeFontEntry` anywhere in the package fails the whole import with *"invalid composite font metrics"*: a document that can no longer be opened, with nothing in the UI saying which value caused it.

Every neighbouring number in this importer already filters (`Prefs::num`, `inset_spacing::number`, `KerningValue`, guides), and the command path rejects the same metrics (`style.rs:31`) — the import path was the one gap.

**Fix:** filter where the number is read — `.filter(|v| v.is_finite() && *v > 0.0).unwrap_or(100.0)` for the three scales, `.filter(|v| v.is_finite()).unwrap_or(0.0)` for the shift and the three mojikumi values. One unusable entry degrades to a usable default instead of refusing the file.

**Regression test:** `unusable_cjk_metrics_do_not_refuse_the_whole_file` — on main the import fails with `Invalid("invalid composite font metrics: Rubies")`; with the patch it opens and the entries carry the fallbacks. Full `designcraft-idml` suite green (92 passed).

title: format: refuse to save a document that can't be read back
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The document JSON is written without ever being read back (`crates/format/src/lib.rs:66`), and serde_json serializes a non-finite `f64` as `null` — which a coordinate can't be deserialized from (`invalid type: null, expected f64`). A non-finite coordinate is easy to reach through the app's own command surface: `file.place` computes `x + bw * k` with `k = w / nw` straight from the parameters (`crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:370`), so `{"command":"file.place","params":{"base64":"<1×1 png>","x":1e308,"width":1e308}}` overflows to infinity in the placed item's path anchors (`transform.scale` and `frame.create` reach it the same way; unlike `guides.rs`, `flex.rs`, `object.rs:2186` and `table.rs:859`, these entry points don't filter finiteness).

`file.save` then writes the archive — the `document.json` inside holds `null` where the coordinate was — marks the document clean, deletes the recovery copy, and reports success. The next `load` rejects the file the app itself just wrote: the user's document is reported saved and is then unopenable.

**Fix:** `format::save` checks the serialized bytes against the reader before writing them and refuses with a clear error instead of producing an unloadable file. (The complementary entry-point filters and making `to_bytes` fallible are a wider policy change deliberately left to the maintainers — `to_bytes` has six call sites.)

**Regression test:** `a_document_with_a_non_finite_coordinate_is_not_saved` — on main the save succeeds and hands back an archive `load` rejects; with the guard the save is refused. Full `designcraft-format` suite green (15 passed).

title: docx: an explicit off imports as off
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`ST_OnOff` (ECMA-376 §17.17.4) is `xsd:boolean ∪ {on, off}`: `true`/`1`/`on` are on, `false`/`0`/`off` are off. The toggle reader only counted `"0" | "false" | "none"` as off (`crates/textimport/src/docx.rs:50`), and the underline reader had the same list (`:170`) — so a property the document explicitly switches **off** imports as **on**.

Reachable through File › Place (or `links.update`, `place.styles`) on any `.docx` containing `<w:b w:val="off"/>`, `<w:i w:val="off"/>`, `<w:strike w:val="off"/>`, `<w:caps w:val="off"/>`, `<w:u w:val="off"/>` or `<w:isLgl w:val="off"/>` (through the same `on()`) — spellings produced by non-Word writers (LibreOffice/POI, Word 2003 XML conversions). Every such run comes in bold / italic / struck through / all-caps / underlined / legal-numbered, the opposite of what the document says. Word itself writes `0`/`false`, which is why existing tests never caught it; the same file already matches the `on` spelling for `w:default` (`docx.rs:472`), which is what makes this look like an oversight.

**Fix:** add `"off"` to both off-lists.

**Regression test:** `off_valued_toggles_stay_off` — on main the `off` run imports bold (`Some("Bold")`); with the patch it stays regular, `on` still means on, and the full `designcraft-textimport` suite is green (24 passed).

title: images: the DOS EPS TIFF preview is read where the spec puts it
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The EPSF binary header (Adobe TN 5002; the same layout Pillow's `EpsImagePlugin` reads) is 22 bytes: magic `C5 D0 D3 C6` (0–3), `psStart` (4–7), `psLength` (8–11), `tiffStart` (12–15), `tiffLength` (16–19), checksum (20–21). The PostScript pair is read correctly at 4/8, but the TIFF pair is read at **20/24** (`crates/images/src/eps.rs:20`) — the checksum plus the first two bytes of the PostScript section (`"%!"`), i.e. an offset around 5.5×10⁸ that is always past the end of a real file. So for a spec-compliant DOS EPS, `bytes.get(..)` returns `None` and `eps_proxy` always falls through to the drawn rectangles or the grey placeholder: the TIFF preview the module documents ("the file's TIFF preview when it has one") is never used on exactly the legacy files (Illustrator 3.0, CorelDRAW, older QuarkXPress) that carry one.

The unit test encoded the same wrong layout (a 26-byte header with the TIFF fields at 20/24 and the checksum at 28), so it passed and could never catch this.

**Fix:** read `tiffStart`/`tiffLength` at 12/16, document the 22-byte header, and rebuild the test fixture on the real layout.

**Regression:** with the spec fixture, the preview assertion fails on main (`pixel_size` is `201×101` — the rectangle stand-in) and passes with the fix (`10×5` — the TIFF). Full `designcraft-images` suite green (33 passed).

title: Direct Selection moves a placed graphic inside its frame
author: pepen11
body:

`transform.move` now honours the content selection (or an explicit `content: true`): a frame's placed graphic is translated in the frame's inner space (`Graphic.xf`), also for rotated frames, and the frame stays. Text frames, copies (`copy: true`) and moves to another spread move as a whole, as before. A degenerate frame matrix falls back to moving the frame, never to NaN in the document. No tool changes were needed: Direct Selection already emits `selection.set {content: true}` and `transform.move`.

Test `direct_selection_moves_the_graphic_inside_its_frame`: content move, undo, explicit `ids`, a 90° rotated frame, a text frame with the content selected. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: Fix \rightarrow closing a \left fence early in math expressions
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/math.rs:393` (no existing issue): Math expressions: \rightarrow (or any command starting with "right") inside \left…\right closes the fence early.

## Cause
`list_until_right` ended a `\left` group with a plain prefix check for `\right`. It never checked that the command name stopped there, so `\rightarrow` and other `\right…` commands closed the fence. The closing delimiter was then read from the following letter, which garbled the output.

## Fix
The fence now closes only when `\right` isn't followed by another ASCII letter. This matches how `command()` reads names. `\rightarrow` and unknown `\right…` commands stay inside the fence, while `\right)` and `\right.` still close it.

## Verified
- Regression test `right_prefixed_commands_do_not_close_a_fence`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib right_prefixed_commands_do_not_close_a_fence`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The rest of the math parser, the symbol table and the layout/SVG code are unchanged.

title: Keep '-' after an RTF control word when no digit follows
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/rtf.rs:160` (no existing issue): RTF import drops a '-' that directly follows a control word when no digits follow it.

## Cause
The RTF control-word scanner consumed a '-' directly after the word as the start of a numeric parameter, even when no digit followed. The parameter then parsed to None and the hyphen was never emitted, so `Rock\emdash-roll` lost its '-'.

## Fix
The scanner now consumes a '-' only when an ASCII digit follows it. Otherwise the '-' stays in the input and is imported as literal text. Negative parameters such as `\li-720` are still consumed as parameters.

## Verified
- Regression test `hyphen_after_control_word_without_digits_is_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport --lib hyphen_after_control_word_without_digits_is_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The handling of control symbols such as `\-` (soft hyphen) and of the delimiting space is unchanged.

title: feat: EPS support through a clean-room PostScript interpreter (designcraft-postscript)
author: Kerrrunchhh
body:
> **Update after review:** the findings are fixed in 8f0c5b5 (work charged per operator, reads and decoding included; copies charged to the memory cap; defaults 50 M steps / 1 GiB, 20 M / 256 MiB on wasm; the font.rs underflow, with a regression test). Placed EPS files used to show only their TIFF preview, or a grey placeholder when they had none. This adds `designcraft-postscript`, a PostScript interpreter written from the PostScript Language Reference (3rd ed.), the Type 1 Font Format, and Adobe TN 5176/5177 (CFF, Type 2 charstrings) and TN 5012 (Type 42). No Ghostscript or other GPL code was used.

It runs an EPS program and writes what it paints as a one-page vector PDF of its bounding box. The rest of DesignCraft treats that PDF as a placed PDF.

## In the app
- **Placing** an EPS keeps the EPS as the asset (`application/postscript`). It is no longer replaced by its preview, so the link compares equal to the file and no longer shows as modified.
- **Screen**: the renderer converts the EPS (cached by content) and draws it through hayro, like a placed PDF.
- **PDF export**: embedded as vectors through krilla. CMYK and spot colours are kept; the PDF is 1.4, so it is fine for PDF/X-1a.
- **IDML** import keeps linked EPS as EPS; export writes `<EPS>` elements.
- An EPS whose program fails before painting anything falls back to the existing preview/placeholder path.

## What the interpreter covers
- The language: scanner, an explicit execution stack (procedures, loops, `stopped`, `exit`; no Rust recursion for PostScript control flow), dictionaries, strings and arrays, resources, about 330 operators.
- Graphics: CTM, paths, fill/stroke, clipping (synced to the PDF with q/Q, independent of the program's gsave pattern), `strokepath` (kurbo's stroker), user pat…

title: Keep text of inline content controls in DOCX import
author: Silvertree2010
body:

`Ctx::inline` now recurses into the `w:sdtContent` of an inline `w:sdt`, the same way it handles hyperlinks and smart tags. The regression test covers a content control between runs and one that wraps a hyperlink.

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Block-level and table-cell `w:sdt` handling, and the content control's properties (`w:sdtPr`), which are still ignored.

title: Canvas: pages show their paper while their render is on its way, not black
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while replaying Learn Skills Daily's *InDesign Full Course Tutorial* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY), chapter "Overview of the Pages Panel", 28:10). The instructor double-clicks thumbnails in the Pages panel to jump between pages. InDesign shows each page at once.

## Problem
When the view moved to pages the canvas texture didn't cover yet (a jump from the Pages panel, Go to Page, a fast scroll), the pages showed solid black until the background render arrived. The black was the page shadow: a page-sized black rectangle offset by 1.5 pt, painted under the texture. Only the frame edges and guides showed over it. In a release build the black lasts a moment; in a debug build, or on a heavy page, it's clearly visible.

## Change
- **Paper under each page:** every page is painted in the document's Paper colour (`[Paper]`, white by default) over its shadow and under the rendered content.
- **Page by page:** the paper is painted per page, not per spread, so spreads with pages of different sizes are covered exactly.
- **Where the render is:** nothing changes there, as it paints the paper itself.

## Context
The same moment before and after, on the course's long document:

![paper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/page-paper-while-rendering/paper_compare.png)

## Tests
- `canvas::tests::pages_show_paper_under_their_render`:
  - On a 3-page facing document, each page has a rectangle in the paper colour exactly at its place on screen.
  - Without the change, it fails.
- The UI tests pass; clippy and fmt are clean.

No dependencies.

title: Keep documents with extreme story revisions editable
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
Opening a native ZIP or legacy JSON document with a top-level story revision of at least 2^63 rebases that saved counter while preserving linked stories’ fresh or stale state and local content. Normalization runs after the existing reader validates the document. Low-revision documents retain their complete model unchanged.

Five dedicated regressions cover both readers, threshold boundaries, a linked child that is also a parent, whole-document allowed changes, repeated loading, subsequent edits and explicit link updates with Undo/Redo. This PR changes only the loader and its dedicated test file.

title: Pages: deleting pages that contain objects asks first, with Don't show again
author: moppeeer
body:

The instructor clicks Delete selected pages in the Pages panel on the cover page. InDesign asks first, and he cancels: "it's going to say, hey, there's an issue here. Don't show again. Click okay or whatever. I'm going to cancel that cuz I did that by accident."

## Problem
DesignCraft deleted the page and everything on it straight away, from these places:

- the Pages panel's Delete Page and Delete Spread;

title: Styles: captured text follows later style edits
author: moppeeer
body:
Creating a style from locally formatted text, applying that style, and editing it left the original text frozen in its old formatting. In the [styles tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pG9JkAPLgs8) this breaks both the Header color changes after 2:16 and the character-style workflow after 6:02. A CLI replay on `origin/main` confirmed that the original cyan headline stayed cyan after Header became red, and the original underlined words stayed underlined after their character style disabled underline.

Applying a paragraph or character style now removes local values already supplied by that style. Real differences and named character styles remain intact. Paragraph applications also respect an exclusive selection endpoint at the next paragraph's start; Clear Overrides limits character-level clearing to a nonempty text selection. Paragraph-level formatting still applies to the affected whole paragraphs.

Five regression tests pass: capture-source inheritance and undo/redo, preservation of different overrides and named styles, sparse character styles inheriting later paragraph size changes, a UTF-8 paragraph boundary, and partial clearing. `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` passed formatting and stopped on unchanged `clippy::nonminimal_bool` diagnostics in UI `lib.rs:783` and engine `tests_file_guard.rs:161`; the remaining full-CI stages were not reached. Those repository-wide gate failures remain documented.

No hard dependency on another PR. #1060 provides the corrected override feedback; it is separate from this command behavior. Existing open PRs were checked for overlap before implementation.

title: Styles: preview paragraph and character style edits before applying them

title: Styles: redefine paragraph and character styles from local formatting
author: moppeeer
body:
The Styles panel had no Redefine Style action, so the [tutorial's global color, size and paragraph-spacing updates](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pG9JkAPLgs8&t=310s) could not be followed.

They incorporate the first selected text's local changes into its style, update all uses, and remove matching source overrides in one undo step. A mismatched name or the no-style entry is rejected without changing the document.

author: moppeeer
body:

title: Table › Convert Rows › To Header, To Body and To Footer, as in InDesign
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Table › Convert Rows › To Header / To Body / To Footer on the selected rows (gap 12, and the Convert Rows item in gap 16).

InDesign turns the selected rows at the top of a table into header rows and the ones at the bottom into footer rows, and To Body sends them back. This follows that: rows become header rows when they touch the top of the table or the existing header rows, footer rows when they touch the bottom or the existing footer rows, and To Body takes header or footer rows next to the body (or the whole table), so the header and footer stay one block each. The items are greyed out when the rows can't change: a body row in between, the last body row (the table keeps one, like `table.options` already does), or a merged cell that would end up half in the header and half in the body. Each conversion is one undo step. The logic is `Table::convert_rows_counts` in the doc crate; the three commands (`table.convertRowsToHeader` / `ToBody` / `ToFooter`) only apply it with `set_header_footer`, so agents get them too, with `rows: [a, b]` like the other table commands. The menu labels follow InDesign's (To Header, To Body, To Footer) with Georgian for them, since the menu test asks for it; happy to switch the command labels to something longer like "Convert Rows to Header" if you'd rather have that in Quick Apply. Edit Header/Footer and Go to Row stay out.

Validation:
- `tests_table::convert_rows_follows_the_table_edges` and `tests_table::convert_rows_keeps_merged_cells_on_one_side`: fail on main (`UnknownCommand("table.convertRowsToHeader")`), pass here, also alone with `--test-threads=1`; dropping the merged-cell check makes the second one fail again

title: Table of Contents: page number and separator character styles, Sort Entries in Alphabetical Order
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1069.

Three per-style options of InDesign's Table of Contents dialog, found by following a standard TOC tutorial ([Redokun](https://www.redokun.com/blog/indesign-table-of-contents), [Webucator](https://www.webucator.com/article/how-to-create-a-table-of-contents-in-adobe-indesig/)) in DesignCraft:

- **Page Number › Style**: a character style for the page number.
- **Between Entry and Number › Style**: a character style for the separator (for example the dot leader in another colour).
- **Sort Entries in Alphabetical Order**.

![Table of Contents dialog with the new options](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/switch87/photocraft/issue-assets/issue-assets/designcraft-1069-toc-dialog.png)

The generated table, with a bold red number style and a red leader style on Headline entries (sample document):

![Generated table of contents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/switch87/photocraft/issue-assets/issue-assets/designcraft-1069-toc-page.png)

## Changes

- **Model** (`crates/doc`): `TocEntry` gets `pageNumberStyle`, `separatorStyle` (character style names, `None` is [None]) and `sort`. All three are optional with serde defaults, so older `.designcraft` files read unchanged and unchanged entries serialize as before.
- **Engine** (`crates/engine/src/cmd/toc.rs`): `toc.generate` and `toc.update` set the page number and separator of each entry in their character styles. A sorted style's entries change places among their siblings (entries under the same higher-level entry), case-insensitively, each taking the lower-level entries under it along. Entries of unsorted styles keep their places, and children are sorted within their own parent only. The `toc.entries` preview sorts the same way. Unknown character styles are errors, as unknown paragraph styles already were; `""` and `[None]` mean no style.
- **Regenerating the story**: `toc.update` used to give the whole new text the format of the old first character. With a styled page number before the first entry (no title),…

title: Restore GNOME Wayland window controls without bundled fonts
author: danielmigueltejedor
body:
GNOME Wayland leaves window decorations to the client, but the desktop build did not enable a frame renderer. Enable winit’s Adwaita vector minimize, maximize/restore and close controls without a title-font renderer. The outer client frame intentionally omits title text; window titles remain available to the desktop and DesignCraft keeps its own application header.

The feature is Linux-only. Existing backend selection is preserved, including the X11 preference when DISPLAY is present. X11 and compositors offering server decorations retain their existing frame path. No engine, composition or UI implementation changes. Package the dependency’s MIT notice; no font or asset files are added and no Cantarell is embedded.

Validation with Rust 1.98.1 on Linux:

title: Thread the loaded text cursor into a text frame inside a group
author: Hamza0101
body:
Closes gap **27** in `docs/gaps.md` ("Loaded text cursor can't thread into a frame inside a group", 2–4 h).

## The bug

A click with the loaded text cursor on a text frame **inside a group** showed the not-allowed cursor and did nothing.

`Document::hit_item` walks a spread's top-level items, so the hit is the group. `item_hit` already looks inside a group, but only to answer whether the group was hit at all, so the frame in it is never named. The thread tool then tests `is_text_frame` on a group, fails, and reports `Target::Invalid`.

Measured before the change, with a text frame moved into a group:

```
hit at grouped frame      = Some(ItemId(19))   (group = 19, frame inside = 17)
cursor over grouped frame = NotAllowed
```

## The change

`hit_descendant` in `crates/doc/src/edit.rs`, beside `item_hit`: the frontmost descendant under a point that a predicate accepts, through nested groups, front to back, skipping hidden children. `ToolContext::hit_text_frame` asks it for a text frame, and `Loaded::target` resolves through that, falling back to the plain `hit` so a click on anything else means exactly what it meant before.

`hit` itself is untouched, so selection still picks the group. After:

```
cursor over grouped frame = ThreadLink
click action = text.thread {"from": 10, "to": 17}
```

`"to": 17` is the frame inside the group, not the group. One change covers the cursor and the click, because `click` resolves through `target`.

## Tests

`loaded_text_cursor_threads_into_a_frame_inside_a_group` asserts four things, the last two to stop the fix over-reaching:

- the cursor is `ThreadLink` over the grouped frame;
- the click threads to that frame, not the group;
- `hit` still returns the **group**, so plain selection is unchanged;
- a group holding nothing threadable still gives `NotAllowed`.

On `main` it fails with `NotAllowed` against `ThreadLink`.

I also checked the existing test most likely to notice this: `alt_click_stays_loaded` threads to a plain rectangl…

title: Hyphenate Greek
author: Hamza0101
body:
Closes #1008.

## The bug

Greek text set unhyphenated however narrow the column.

`Lang::for_language` already resolves a language generically, through `hypher::Lang::from_iso`. But `from_iso` answers only for a language whose patterns were compiled in, and the compose crate asked for `["alloc", "portuguese", "spanish", "norwegian"]`. Greek was never in the binary:

```
before:  for_language("Greek") = false   hypher from_iso("el") = false
after:   for_language("Greek") = true    ανθρωπος → breaks at [2, 5]  (αν-θρω-πος)
```

## The change

The `greek` feature is asked for. Nothing else was needed — because the lookup is by ISO code, `"Greek"`, `"Greek: Greece"`, `"el"` and `"el-GR"` all resolve, and the test asserts all four.

## Licence and provenance

`NOTICE` records the patterns per language, so this does too. The published `hypher` crate ships the compiled tries rather than the pattern files, so the licence is not readable from the dependency; I took it from the file in hyph-utf8:

> `% copyright: Copyright (C) 2008-2011 Dimitrios Filippou`
> `% licence: This file is available under any of the following licences: LPPL, MIT`

So: `hyph-el-monoton.tex` 5.0, Dimitrios Filippou, taken under MIT, with the MIT text in `NOTICE` beside the Spanish and Portuguese entries.

## One caveat, documented rather than left to be found

These are the **monotonic** patterns — `hypher` maps `el` to `hyph-el-monoton.tex`, not to the polytonic set — so polytonic Greek hyphenates by monotonic rules. For a page-layout app that may meet classical text, that seemed worth stating in the module's documentation rather than discovering later. If polytonic support matters, it is a second `hypher` language rather than a change here.

## Docs

`gaps.md` 13, `target-app-parity.md` and `typography-parity.md` each listed the four languages that hyphenate. They now list five.

## Tests

`greek_text_gets_greek_hyphenation` composes Greek in a narrow frame and asserts hyphenation happens, that **e…

title: Text parameters: a vertical tab is a forced line break
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Text parameters read U+000B (vertical tab) as a forced line break instead of drawing a box.

Follow-up to #654 (thanks @DanielGemm). In Word and PowerPoint the forced line break (Shift+Enter) is Chr(11), and python-pptx writes it the same way, so it is what text pasted or generated from those tools carries. Until now `frame.create`, `story.setText`, `text.insert` and the other commands that go through `text_param` kept it as a character and drew a missing-glyph box. `text_param` now turns it into U+2028, the same forced line break the Type menu inserts, right next to the existing CR handling, so every text parameter gets it. One line in `script --help` and `docs/agents.md` says so. For InDesign's own scripting I couldn't confirm from public docs which character `contents` uses for a forced break (forum answers point to `\n` and `SpecialCharacters.FORCED_LINE_BREAK`), so the docs name Word's convention rather than InDesign's. IDML import is untouched: XML 1.0 can't carry U+000B, and its forced breaks already arrive as U+2028.

Validation:
- `line_end_tests::vertical_tabs_are_forced_line_breaks`: fails on main (`("One\u{b}Two", 1)` instead of `("One\u{2028}Two", 1)`), passes here; mapping U+000B to `\n` instead also fails it (two paragraphs)
- `cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib line_end_tests`, `cargo test -p designcraft-cli --test cli`
- `cargo clippy -p designcraft-engine -p designcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(export): reject oversized page selections
author: skylartaylor
body:
Reject PDF and PowerPoint export page numbers that cannot fit the target's index type before converting them. On WASM, values such as 4294967296 and 4294967297 previously wrapped to zero or one, causing an overflow or selecting the wrong page. Direct PPTX export also handles the largest possible page index without overflowing its error message.

Add permanent boundary tests for scalar and array page selections, valid-page controls, and the direct PPTX error path. Fresh native and WASM before/after tests reproduce the three original failures and pass on the fix. All seven `cargo xtask ci` gates passed, including 1,966 passing native tests and the WASM compilation checks.

title: Canvas: Enter and Tab in a panel field no longer reach the selected text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1082.

It happens on desktop too, not only on the web. The panels are drawn before the canvas, and a panel field gives up keyboard focus on Enter (and Tab) while it draws, so by the time the canvas reads the frame's keys no text field is focused any more and the Enter goes to the Type tool: the selected text became a paragraph break, or a tab with Tab. The app now notes at the start of the frame whether a text field had focus, and the canvas leaves that frame's keys to the field. Every field in the panels and the Control bar goes through the same path, so the fix covers them all, not just font size. The note is kept per window, since egui keeps one keyboard focus per viewport: a field focused in the main window doesn't mute the canvas of a second window (Window > Arrange > New Window).

This is a different cause from #598, which keeps arrow keys and Tab on the canvas while the canvas itself has focus; the two don't overlap.

Validation:
- `canvas::tests::enter_or_tab_in_a_panel_field_leave_the_selected_text_alone` (types 18 in the font size field over a selection of "ell" in "Hello", then Enter, then Tab): fails on main (`"H\no"` after Enter, `"H\to"` after Tab), passes here, and the size is applied
- `cargo test -p designcraft-ui-egui --lib canvas`, `cargo clippy -p designcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- The second-window case isn't covered by a test: egui_kittest only drives the root viewport
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Print: network printers, Grayscale and queue paper through craft-libs
author: b1tninja
body:
## Blocked: merge these first

This PR needs the print stack, which is not merged yet. Merge in this order:

| # | PR | What it provides |
|---|----|------------------|
| 1 | storytold/winprint.rs#7 | Windows PDF printing (cancel guard, device resolution, bands); craft-print depends on it |
| 2 | storytold/craft-libs#113 (craft-wsd) and #120 (craft-job) | shared building blocks that craft-print builds on |
| 3 | storytold/craft-libs#116 | craft-print: the print backends (WS-Print, IPP, system spooler) |
| 4 | storytold/craft-libs#112 | craft-ui: the Print dialog's network-printer controls (independent of 1 to 3) |

**The pin.** So that it builds today, this branch pins craft-libs by *PR ref*, which moves with the PR and cannot be merged as is:

```
Cargo.toml:17  craft-print  rev = "refs/pull/116/head"
Cargo.toml:76  craft-ui  rev = "refs/pull/112/head"
```

**After #112 and #116 have merged:** replace each `rev = "refs/pull/N/head"` above with the craft-libs `main` revision that contains both (`rev = "<sha>"`), then run `cargo update -p craft-print -p craft-ui` so `Cargo.lock` resolves to that one revision. Nothing else in this PR changes. Do not merge this PR with the PR refs in place.

Draft. Adds printing through the shared craft-libs stack to designcraft: the Print dialog gets one Printer list (system queues plus "Network printer…", WS-Print and IPP by address), a Grayscale option that really grays the output and the preview, and queue-paper jobs (no paper demanded unless one was picked).

## Commits
- File > Print: network printer destination (WS-Print and IPP) on craft-print's registry
- network print: no deny-list code in the app

title: Placed greyscale and bitmap images take the swatch applied to them, as in InDesign (IDML, screen, PDF)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Placed greyscale and bitmap images now show the colour InDesign applied to them, on screen and in PDF.

Part of #1094.

In InDesign you can apply a swatch to the image itself (Direct Selection, then a swatch). That only works for greyscale and 1-bit bitmap images; colour images, and images with alpha or spot channels, keep their own colours. On a greyscale image each pixel becomes a tint of the swatch as strong as the pixel is dark, and white stays opaque. On a bitmap the black pixels take the swatch and the white ones turn transparent, so the frame's fill shows behind them. IDML stores this as `FillColor`/`FillTint` on `<Image>`, which the importer used to ignore. This PR reads and writes those attributes on `Graphic.fill`, so it also survives in the native format. The canvas tints the decoded pixels, and the result is cached per image and on-screen colour, like the plate previews. PDF export paints the swatch through a luminosity mask of the image's coverage, over 0% ink for greyscale, so a spot swatch prints on its own plate.

`FillColor="Color/Black"` at 100%, which InDesign writes on images nobody coloured, imports as no swatch, the same as a missing attribute. The export only writes the attribute when there is a swatch and it exists. A swatch that has been deleted leaves the image as it is.

Left out:
- Applying a swatch to a selected image from the Swatches panel or a command. That comes in a follow-up PR, together with its Undo.
- A bitmap's white is not made transparent unless a swatch is applied, so existing documents render exactly as before. Doing it for every bitmap would be closer to InDesign and could be another follow-up.
- GIFs are indexed, so the palette decides: black and white only counts as a bitmap, opaque neutral greys as greyscale, anything else as colour. I couldn't check what InDesign does with GIFs (the two in the issue are GIFs). Happy to switch.

title: Keep desktop PDF export responsive with background generation and atomic saving
author: ForestParks
body:
Desktop PDF export currently blocks the interface while generating the PDF, then base64-encodes the entire file into JSON and decodes it before saving. Large exports can therefore appear to hang even when generation is progressing.

This runs the existing export pipeline on one native worker using an immutable document snapshot and retained document fonts. The desktop host writes the raw bytes atomically on that worker, avoiding the base64 round trip. The interface keeps processing window events and shows a working indicator, destination and elapsed time. Editing and normal Quit wait until completion; failures and export warnings are displayed. No percentage or cancellation is claimed.

The worker retains the caller's automation roots and checks its output path. A custom host without a background writer rechecks those roots before its deferred UI-thread write. The synchronous engine `file.exportPdf` command and browser export keep their existing behavior. Native programmatic `app.exportPdf` now returns `{path, queued:true}`; clients use `ui.inspect.pdfExport` for final completion or failure.

All current export options and page-selection validation flow through the same engine pipeline. This does not add image downsampling or change PDF rendering decisions.

Validation after integrating `main` at `c2609f921bb6`: `cargo xtask ci` passed all seven gates, including WebAssembly: **2,851 tests passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored**. The headless native UI exported the public four-page sample (558,907 bytes); a PDF parser verified four pages and the rendered interface showed successful completion. Regressions cover continued frame processing, OS-close/Quit guards, writer failure, document/font lifetime, writing off the UI thread, completion of the PDF dialog test and denied background output under automation roots. title: fix(release): embed a Simplified Chinese UI font in releases
author: sumingwang233
body:
## Problem

The Simplified Chinese interface shows tofu (missing-glyph boxes) for Simplified-only characters (`简` `车` `门` `东` `见` `说` `对` `们`…) in release builds — confirmed on 0.8.0 Windows. Shared Han characters (`中` `文` `字`…) render, so only part of the text is boxes.

## Root cause (two stacked causes)

1. **0.8.0 predates the installed-font fallback entirely** (PR #814, merged 2026-10-14 22:05, after that day's release build): back then the zh interface had only the Latin UI face plus the craft Japanese faces, and nothing scanned system fonts for scripts they lack.

The Hans UI face (Noto Sans CJK SC) was added later the same day (8dcdacd5), but the pin never moved. So even current releases embed no Simplified Chinese UI font, and the interface leans entirely on PR #814's system-font install — which is exactly what ROADMAP promises releases ship (`BIZ UDPGothic and Noto Sans CJK SC for the UI … (all releases)`).

- Bump `craft-fonts-ref` in `release.yml` and `freebsd.yml` to `3d9ab3a` (adds Noto Sans CJK SC, Noto Sans Arabic, Noto Sans Thai), the set the current code and docs already expect.

title: Keep large documents responsive with cached previews and image-drag rendering
author: ForestParks
body:
Image-heavy documents repeatedly decode large originals and repaint expensive pages during navigation and image-frame moves. This adds bounded shared image previews, background thumbnails, coarse scrolling previews and a retained-render path for eligible image dragging.

- Reuse larger cached mip levels before decoding full pixels. Keep separate original/preview targets (192/96 MiB), weak ownership for closed documents, a serialized decode miss path, and the upstream 64-entry failed-asset cap. Retain one current original even when it alone exceeds the original target; older originals still evict, avoiding repeated full decodes of a large print image.
- Enable optional disposable desktop disk previews, keyed by source SHA-256, page, mip and renderer/dependency fingerprint; verify dimensions, checksums and premultiplied pixels and fall back to originals on cache errors. Count all versioned preview files toward the 512 MiB disk budget, evict oldest first, and remove abandoned temporary writes after 24 hours without touching active writes or unrelated files. Preferences → Display Performance can disable persistent image previews, including startup cache cleanup; the docs explain privacy, platform locations and safe clearing. The filesystem guard explicitly documents this host-configured cache module; commands cannot choose its directory or filenames.
- Render visible page thumbnails in the background, reject stale revisions and fit uploads to the GPU texture limit, including unusually wide pages. Retain at most 32 coarse 128-pixel spread previews beneath the sharp canvas; uncached areas show page paper until ready.
- Prepare below/image/above textures for eligible single-image translations. Use draft motion for complex cases, restore quality on release, cancel superseded work and defer thumbnail work during interactions. Escape cancels the transaction without a later mouse-up committing it.

title: Refuse table row moves across the header/footer boundary
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/table.rs:882 (Table::move_row, called from crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:1437 and :1369)` (no existing issue): table.moveRow / table.dropCells can move a header or footer row out of place; the saved .designcraft file then fails to open.

## Cause
`Table::move_row` moved a row together with its `RowKind` and never checked the target position. A header row moved below the body rows, or a body row moved above a header or below a footer, left the table failing `Table::check` ("header/footer rows out of order"). The command still reported success, so the saved file would not load again.

## Fix
`move_row` now returns an error when the row being moved and the row at the target position have different kinds (header, body or footer). `table.moveRow` and `table.dropCells` both go through it, so both now report an error and leave the table unchanged. Moves within the same kind of row still work.

## Verified
- Regression tests `move_row_keeps_header_and_footer_rows_in_place`, `move_row_cannot_move_a_header_row_out_of_place`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-doc --lib move_row_keeps_header_and_footer_rows_in_place && cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib move_row_cannot_move_a_header_row_out_of_place`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`move_col` is unchanged because columns have no header or footer kind. Moving header or footer rows by changing the table's header/footer row counts is not changed either.

title: IDML: keep column guides that were dragged off centre
author: Hamza0101
body:
Part of #1096. The reporter's own guess was right: the custom gutter was lost because the importer threw the positions away.

## The bug

InDesign stores dragged column guides in `MarginPreference ColumnsPositions`, as pairs of offsets from the margin box's left edge. The importer did not read it:

```rust
Columns { count: …, gutter: …, positions: None }   // always
```

So a two-column page whose gutter had been dragged came in evenly divided. On a 450 pt margin box with `ColumnsPositions="0 150 170 450"`:

```
before:  columns at (30, 245) and (265, 480)   — the even split
after:   columns at (30, 180) and (200, 480)   — where the designer put them
```

`Columns::positions` already existed in the model, documented as "Custom column positions (after dragging column guides)". Nothing ever set it and nothing ever read it, so the field was dead. This fills it in and uses it:

- **`Page::column_rects`** returns the custom rects when they are set, the even split otherwise. Every page-column consumer goes through that one method — canvas guides, snapping, text threading, the first frame a story is placed into — so they all follow the dragged gutter now.
- **Import** reads `ColumnsPositions`.
- **Export** writes the page's real positions instead of recomputing an even split, so the round trip keeps them.
- **`layout.marginsAndColumns`** clears them when a count or gutter is set, which is what InDesign's Margins and Columns does. Without that, dragged positions would silently outrank the new value and the dialog would look broken — the bug this change would otherwise have introduced.

## Verified against real InDesign output, not guessed

The repo has no real IDML (gap 3: "IDML round-trip isn't proven on real files"), so before writing anything I read InDesign-authored spreads checked into public repositories (`nclm/versioning-an-idml`, `bakku99/Colab-Work`). Three things came out of that, all of which shaped the code:

1. `ColumnsPositions` is margin-box-relative and runs…

author: answ-kaz
body:
Opening real Japanese IDML files (exported from InDesign 2026) in DesignCraft 0.8.0 showed hundreds of preflight errors: every Japanese font "missing" and many text frames "overset" that InDesign itself does not report (I checked with InDesign: 1 of 543 text frames overflows in one document; DesignCraft reported 27).

What this PR does now (it includes a merge of main; main's mojikumi spacing table and font alias lookup replaced my first line-end punctuation and native-name code, so only what main still lacks is left):

1. **compose: Metrics - Roman Only kerning.** The default of Japanese documents was imported as plain Metrics, so Kana pair kerning (e.g. メ 6.51 pt vs 6.38 pt em) changed widths InDesign keeps at exactly 1 em. New `Kerning::MetricsRomanOnly` (IDML import/export round trip); `kern` is off for CJK characters of such runs.
2. **compose: line fitting like InDesign.**
   - The tracking after a line's last glyph no longer has to fit (checked against InDesign with a synthetic document: the narrowest one-line measure is the last glyph's offset plus its natural advance, tracked or not).
   - The fill glue before a forced break or the paragraph end carries the hang of the line end, or a line that only fits by hanging its last glyph was given up at the glue.
   - A justified line ended by a forced line break is justified too; a justified CJK line is rated by the space it leaves, so the composer prefers fuller lines over breaking at a lone word space.
   - Spacing the mojikumi table allows to be closed up (between punctuation, at a line end) is taken first at no cost, as in InDesign: a headline that only fits by closing up two punctuation marks stays one line instead of being given up for two looser ones.
3. **fonts: test for native-language family names** (`游明朝`): main already resolves them through the family aliases; the test keeps it that way.
4. **idml: embedded EPS previews and EPS text.** InDesign stores a placed EPS as an `EPSImage` raster blob (QR codes)…

title: Panels: open icon panels as flyouts after customizing the dock
author: moppeeer
body:
Opening Color or Links after customizing the dock inserted it as another full-size dock tab. In the [Customizing the Interface chapter, around 8:15](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY&t=495s), these panels open from the icon column while the floating style group stays in place.

`window.panel` now opens an unassigned icon panel as a flyout beside the measured icon rail. Clicking its icon again, its Collapse to Icons button, or Close closes the flyout. The dock's active tab and floating groups stay unchanged. Panels explicitly docked earlier still return to their saved locations, and saved workspaces restore the flyout.

Behaviour changes to note:

- **Properties › Stroke link.** In a customized workspace the link now opens Stroke as a flyout beside the icon rail. It used to add Stroke to the dock as a tab. A Stroke panel the user docked earlier still opens in its dock place.
- **Rail icons.** The rail sends `window.panel` (with `from: "icons"`) instead of `window.panel.activate`. Closed dock tabs (Properties, Pages, Layers) come back exactly where Activate Panel put them. Paragraph Styles and Character Styles icons open a flyout like the other icons. Window › Paragraph Styles still opens the floating Character Styles | Paragraph Styles group.
- **Dragging.** Starting to drag a dock tab or a floating group collapses an open flyout, as in InDesign.

### Before / after

Same synthetic document, commands and offscreen harness. Before is `main` at `c2609f92`; after is this branch at `27a3420`. The document JSON is identical apart from its creation timestamp.

title: feat: keyed script labels (insertLabel/extractLabel), IDML KeyValuePairs
author: Kerrrunchhh
body:
IDML `<Label><KeyValuePair Key Value/>` on page items was dropped on import. Items now keep keyed labels (`Item::labels`), read from IDML and written back before the path geometry, as InDesign writes them; the native file keeps them through serde.

- object.insertLabel {key, value, ids?}: set a keyed label; an empty value removes the key
- object.extractLabel {key, id?} → {value}, "" when absent
- object.labels {id?} → {label, labels}
- object.findByLabel gains {key, value?} and now finds anchored objects

Commands reach anchored objects (also inside anchored groups) through the new Document::item_any / item_any_mut; object ids in stories were out of reach before. Template IDML whose scripts read labels such as imagepath, fit or signet can now be processed by DesignCraft commands.

title: feat: anchored.frame — the text frame and column an anchored object is set in
author: Kerrrunchhh
body:
Builds on #1129 (this branch contains its commit; review that one first).

InDesign scripts size inline graphics to their column by reading the anchor's `parentTextFrames`, then the frame's column width. That depends on composition, so a template generator can't know it in advance.

`anchored.frame {id | story+index}` returns, from the composed story:
- the text frame the object is set in, and its bounds
- the column it sits in, the column count, and the composed column's width and rectangle

`frame` is null while the object is overset. `id` may be an item inside an anchored group.

The test covers a two-column frame where the object falls in the second column, a group child, the overset case and errors. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

title: feat: fixed and flexible column widths by command
author: Kerrrunchhh
body:
The model and IDML already carried a column width for fixed- and flexible-width columns (UseFixedColumnWidth, TextColumnFixedWidth), but no command could set it and none reported it.

- object.textFrameOptions takes columnWidth (pt, 1–100000; documented with columnsKind, which it already took)
- document.inspect reports columnsKind, gutter and, for fixed and flexible widths, columnWidth (InDesign's textColumnFixedWidth)

title: feat: tables for scripts — list, set width, style cell paragraphs
author: Kerrrunchhh
body:
InDesign scripts walk a frame's tables, set table.width and apply a paragraph style to every cell's paragraphs. DesignCraft had no table listing or width, and its table commands that take {story, table} were disabled without a caret in a table, so they could not be used on a named table at all.

- table.list {story?, frame?}: tables with size, width, style, anchor, and the frame and column they are set in (from composition)
- table.setWidth {width, story?, table?}: scales the columns, shares kept
- table.paragraphStyle {name, clearOverrides?, story?, table?}
- style.table.apply, table.setColumnWidth and table.setRowHeight are enabled with a document open (they have no menu items) and act on the named table; without one, they still ask for a caret

title: feat: object.graphic — a frame's placed graphic for scripts
author: Kerrrunchhh
body:
Builds on #1129 (this branch contains its commit; review that one first).

InDesign scripts read a placed graphic's type (`images`, `pdfs`, `epss`) and its `geometricBounds` to size the frame to the graphic's proportions. No command reported either.

`object.graphic {id?}` returns:
- the kind (image, pdf, eps, svg, psd), mime, name and link
- the pixel size and PDF page
- the natural size, and the bounds in the frame and on the spread (null for an anchored frame)
- the scale and the effective resolution

Anchored frames are included. The test covers kind, sizes, 72 → 144 ppi at half size, an anchored frame, and errors. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

One finding while testing with a generated template IDML: an image's natural size comes from the IDML's `GraphicBounds` (a placeholder there, 95 × 190 pt for a 255 × 37 px PNG). `object.graphic` makes the mismatch visible through `pixels` and `ppi`. Whether IDML import should prefer the linked file's proportions is a separate question.

title: Panels: dock floating tab groups together (requires #1128)
author: moppeeer
body:
Dragging a floating panel group's grip over the dock moved its window but never docked it. In the [Customizing the Interface chapter, around 9:04–9:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY&t=544s), the instructor drags Character Styles and Paragraph Styles together into the icon column. Half-second reference frames confirm that destination.

The gesture now shows a drop highlight and moves the whole group atomically:

- Into the icon column: its ordered tabs stay grouped and reopen in one flyout. The flyout can float the group again, and saved workspaces retain the grouping.
- Into an expanded dock: all tabs move together, stay contiguous and keep the active tab. Side drops create a separate tab group.
- Invalid destinations leave ownership unchanged. Other floating windows and modal surfaces block drops through them.

`window.panel.dockGroup` and `window.panel.floatGroup` expose the same operations to automation. The shared docking library already supplies the gesture; no dependency update is needed.

### Dependencies / review scope

**Requires #1128.** The branch includes `27a3420`, its icon-panel flyout support, and its review follow-up `b6e56bd` (merged in `5794e64`). **Review `9204e95`** for this change, plus review follow-up `318729f`: a wide icon group's flyout scrolls the opened panel's tab into view, and a test covers collapsing a group of dock-only panels (Properties, Layers) to icons. #1022 supplies the automatic paired style window used in the tutorial; the test scenes create that group explicitly.

### Before / after

Before is #1128 at `27a3420`; after is `9204e95`. Same synthetic document, pointer path and offscreen harness. Both saved documents are identical apart from creation time.

title: fix: allow deleting parent pages (#956)
author: harrisonoconnorhover
body:
Parent rows in the Pages panel have no deletion command. This adds **Delete Parent** to each parent row's context menu, using the clicked parent's stable ID even when prefixes are shared.

Deleting a parent clears page assignments and based-on references, removes its shared items through normal story/thread cleanup, and preserves customized local copies as ordinary objects. Undo/Redo restores the document relationships in one step. Deleting the final parent returns to document pages.

Addresses the deletion portion of #956. The integration with main `5aeb4dd743067e5a6d797d0f613448a06d141a09` preserves its parent navigation, thumbnail renderer, binding order, and both panel layouts. Regression fixtures account for upstream's inherited-item behavior and text-frame caret selection: deletion clears the selection, Undo restores the prior caret, and Redo clears it again.

Validation for published head `9434e96dbf002b523adeb8194d003d4d7610feb5` (tree `db9b9d73515f23e6a1ecf6326b4db55c61e0aeba`), macOS arm64 with Rust 1.99.1:

- `cargo xtask ci`: all seven gates passed—formatting, strict workspace/all-target Clippy, workspace tests, PDF dependencies, asset attribution, layering, and WebAssembly checks. Dependencies were locked and offline during validation.
- Workspace tests: **2,878 passed, zero failed, five intentionally ignored**. The three parent-deletion regressions and the real parent-row context-menu test in both vertical and horizontal layouts pass. All **16 WebAssembly crate checks** pass.
- Whole-window offscreen GPU inspection confirmed the actual right-click action deletes A-Other while retaining A-Parent and both document pages, Undo/Redo works, and deleting the final parent returns to the two document pages. These screenshots preceded only the final test-assertion correction; runtime and UI source files are identical to this head.

Packaged native application behavior, Windows/Linux runtime behavior, and browser runtime behavior were not requalified locally.

title: InDesign's type shortcuts: Justify All Lines ⇧⌘F, Em Space ⇧⌘M, En Space ⇧⌘N, Paragraph Rules ⌥⌘J
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Justify All Lines, Em Space, En Space and Paragraph Rules now have InDesign's shortcuts: ⇧⌘F, ⇧⌘M, ⇧⌘N, ⌥⌘J (Shift+Ctrl+F, Shift+Ctrl+M, Shift+Ctrl+N, Ctrl+Alt+J on Windows).

InDesign's default set binds Justify All Lines to Shift+Ctrl+F (next to Justify Left, Shift+Ctrl+J), Insert White Space › Em Space and En Space to Shift+Ctrl+M / Shift+Ctrl+N, and Paragraph Rules… to Alt+Ctrl+J (Option+Cmd+J on the Mac). The spaces only work at an insertion point. This PR adds `type.justifyAll` next to `type.justify`. Em Space and En Space become `app.insertEmSpace` / `app.insertEnSpace`, the same way #894 handled Current Page Number, so Insert White Space and the Mac menu bar show ⇧⌘M / ⇧⌘N. The two items are disabled without an insertion point: on the Mac the key does nothing, and elsewhere it leaves "no text insertion point" in the status bar, the same as ⇧⌘L with no text. Paragraph Rules… gets ⌥⌘J, shown in the Paragraph panel menu. Alignment and Paragraph Rules stay out of the Type menu, as #894 arranged. None of the four chords was taken, and the dispatcher compares Shift exactly, so ⌥⌘J doesn't clash with ⌥⇧⌘J (Justification in #533).

One fix comes along with it. On the Mac the menu bar takes a shortcut before the window does, so with the Story Editor, Find/Change or Quick Apply focused, ⇧⌘M would have typed an em space at the canvas caret behind the field. The three menu-bar inserts that have a shortcut (Em Space, En Space, Current Page Number) now do nothing while a text field has focus. This also covers #894's ⌥⇧⌘N.

Left out: InDesign's other white-space shortcuts (thin, hair, nonbreaking…). Happy to add them here or in a follow-up. Like the existing Ctrl+Alt shortcuts, Ctrl+Alt+J arrives as AltGr+J on Windows, which types a character on a few layouts.

Validation:
- `justify_all_lines_has_indesigns_shortcut_and_justifies_the_last_line_too` (engine): fails on main (`UnknownCommand("type.justifyAll")`), passes here
- `indesigns_type_shortcuts_insert_spaces_justify_a…

title: View: retain the last presented spread at the editing zoom
author: moppeeer
body:
Leaving Presentation after navigating returns to the starting spread on current `main`. For example, starting on spread 2, pressing Shift+W, Right Arrow and Escape returns to spread 2 instead of staying on spread 3. In the [Navigation chapter around 18:50–19:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY&t=1130s), the instructor enters on pages 2–3 and exits on pages 10–11 at the previous editing zoom.

The canvas keeps temporary per-document and per-pane editing views and the last presented center. That center survives the screen-mode command restoring its saved view. Without navigation, the original view returns; after navigation, the last presented spread is centered at the original editing zoom. Viewport changes on entry also retain the current spread. Document data and project configuration are unchanged.

**No prerequisite PR remains.** #1043/#1044 and #503 are now in `main` through #1139. This branch is rebased onto `c2609f92`; its only change is the view-restoration follow-up in `4563eb563f91edd669abd6c43127230e1e8d305d`, in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`.
