title: Docs: the overset rule matches InDesign (#180)
author: y-az
body:
A line is now set when its baseline fits in the frame, as in InDesign, so the parity docs and the gap list no longer list the overset rule as a difference.

Docs only: upstream fixed the rule itself in d52ef6b.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: Hyphenation: bundle the Dutch patterns
author: y-az
body:
Enable hypher's "dutch" feature: Piet Tutelaers's hyph-nl.tex 1.1 from hyph-utf8, MIT licensed (added to NOTICE). Dutch text, including InDesign's nl_NL_2005, now hyphenates instead of never breaking a word.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: Breaker: keep a page number's digits together
author: y-az
body:
The emergency break inside a word wider than the measure could fall between glyphs of one source character: an automatic page number wider than its frame came out as "13" over "4". Glyphs sharing a cluster (the generated digits of a page number, multi-glyph clusters) now stay together and the number hangs out of its frame, as in InDesign.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: Shaping: Arabic keeps contextual alternates
author: y-az
body:
Contextual alternates are part of how many Arabic fonts join (connecting strokes, tatweel and letter variants). InDesign keeps them in Arabic text when Contextual Alternates is off, so `calt` off is now dropped for Arabic runs.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: Shaping: runs that differ only in paint shape as one
author: y-az
body:
A colour change inside a word split the text into runs shaped apart: Arabic letters coloured one by one lost their joins and lam-alif, and a vowel mark in a colour of its own fell off its base letter. InDesign shapes across such runs. Neighbouring runs that meet between two Arabic characters, or where the second starts with a combining mark, now shape together when they differ only in paint (fill, stroke, underline, strikethrough, structure tag) and feature switches.

Every character then keeps its own cluster (HarfBuzz's monotone-characters level), so each glyph takes the style of its own character. Ligatures off and OpenType features apply as ranged features over their run's bytes (designcraft_fonts::features_in clips them to the part being shaped).

Tracking is no longer added between a letter and a mark in a cluster of its own, and an inline object is bidi-neutral (U+FFFC), so it keeps its place in Arabic text.

If the text-stroke PR (join and miter limit) lands too, `shaping_key` should reset `stroke_join` and `stroke_miter_limit` like the other stroke attributes; until then runs that differ only there are shaped apart, as now.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: Text: custom glyphs from the Glyphs panel
author: y-az
body:
A glyph without a Unicode value, inserted from InDesign's Glyphs panel, is stored in IDML as <?ACE 1a?> with the run's CustomGlyph name. It vanished on import. It is now a CUSTOM_GLYPH character with a custom_glyph character attribute naming the glyph, read from and written to IDML as InDesign writes it, and drawn as the glyph the font names (FontFace::glyph_by_name) at that glyph's advance.

Letters next to it join it as they would the letters its name stands for (uniXXXX and uXXXX names, ligature components, .init/.medi/.fina/.isol suffixes, else the character the font maps to that glyph). For bidi it is the character it draws first, so it reads in their direction.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: Text: World-Ready paragraph attribute
author: y-az
body:
InDesign's Paragraph and Single-line Composers aren't World-Ready: they set a line left to right in text order, and Arabic letters stand unjoined with their marks still placed. The new world_ready paragraph attribute (on by default) models that: off, a line ignores bidi, and joining scripts are shaped without their joining forms, mandatory ligatures and contextual alternates.

IDML Composer names map both ways: "HL Composer" and "HL Single" aren't World-Ready, the "Optyca" composers are, and [No paragraph style] defaults to the Paragraph Composer. A World-Ready checkbox in the Paragraph panel and Paragraph Style Options.

Behaviour change: World-Ready is on by default (DesignCraft's behaviour so far). IDML `HL Composer` / `HL Single` import as World-Ready off, and World-Ready paragraphs now export as the `… Optyca` composers.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: Leading: empty paragraphs as in InDesign
author: y-az
body:
An empty paragraph takes its font, size and leading from its paragraph mark, not from the paragraph style, and under a leading model an empty line measures from the paragraph font's em box instead of dropping by its depth.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: Tables: Space Before from the baseline, cell height from the ink
author: y-az
body:
InDesign measures a table's Space Before from the previous line's baseline, so descenders may hang into it, as it measures the text after the table from the table's bottom.

A cell now grows only as far as its glyphs reach below the baseline, not by the font's descent: with a font whose descent is deep (many Arabic fonts), every row came out too tall.

Behaviour change: four existing cell-height tests now measure the ink instead of the font descent.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

body:
A centred line wider than its column (a word set to No Break) started at the column's left edge. InDesign centres it, hanging out on both sides.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: IDML import: style names ending in a space, layers of group items
author: y-az
body:
A BasedOn reference to a style whose name ends in a space was trimmed before it was looked up, so the base style went missing and its font and colour with it. The reference is now looked up as written first.

Items inside a group or pasted into a frame carry no ItemLayer in IDML: they sit on their parent's layer. They were put on the first layer, which may be hidden or locked, and took their text wrap and editing with it.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: PDF export: an empty .notdef prints as nothing
author: y-az
body:
Where a font's .notdef glyph is empty, InDesign shows a box on screen but exports nothing in its place. The PDF now does the same; the screen keeps the box, and Preflight still lists the character.

title: Justification: optionally squeeze word spaces below the minimum
author: y-az
body:
InDesign's composers break the minimum word space like the maximum when every choice breaks a limit: measured on InDesign output, justified lines come out at 61-72% of the space width with an 80% minimum.

A new document preference, Preferences > Composition > Squeeze Word Spaces Below the Minimum (document.preferences {squeezeWordSpaces}), lets the composer do the same: word spaces may shrink down to 60% of their desired width, both in choosing the breaks and in distributing a line. A range of shrink past the minimum costs twice a range of stretch past the maximum, so a loose line still wins over a tight one when the violations are alike. Never where kashidas justify Arabic: the composer doesn't count their stretch yet, so it would squeeze lines the kashidas could fill.

The preference is off in new documents, in IDML imports and in documents saved before it existed, so justified paragraphs set as before unless it is switched on. It is stored with the document and part of the composition cache's signature.

As asked in #1014, squeezing word spaces below the paragraph's Minimum is now an opt-in document preference, off by default, so justified paragraphs set exactly as before unless it is switched on. IDML import never turns it on.

Split out of #1014, one PR per topic. `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch.

title: Parent pages: a parent page's overrides and Show Parent Items apply through the based_on chain
author: y-az
body:
Builds on #674, now rebased onto main, so it holds only its own change: a parent page's own overrides and Show Parent Items, which #674 doesn't cover. PPTX export and the CMYK blend-space passes still follow only the first parent; they can go through the same helper in a follow-up.

On top of Based on Parent (#652), a parent page now hides what it hides wherever it shows:

- A parent page with Show Parent Items off (IDML ShowMasterItems="false" on a MasterSpread) ends the chain: its bases' items no longer show behind it, on the document pages using it or on parent spreads based on it.
- Base items a parent page overrides (its overridden list, read from a MasterSpread page's OverrideList) no longer show on the pages using that parent or on parents based on it; only the document page's own overrides were checked. layout.overrideParentItems doesn't copy such an item.
- The transparency flattener rasterises a spread for the parent items that show on it (page side, overrides, Show Parent Items), not for any transparent item anywhere in the chain.

Screen rendering, PDF export, Cmd+Shift-click hit testing, snapping, frame edges, overrides and the flattener all read it. Frame edges now also honour the page's own Show Parent Items, and a page that hides parent items has nothing to override.

title: Anchored text frames: host page, tagged PDF, copy, release and delete
author: y-az
body:
Builds on #124, now rebased onto main, so it holds only its own change; its doc line is in `docs/target-app-parity.md`, on the Anchored objects line.

On top of #124, which threads an anchored text frame to its story, imports, composes, draws and exports it, recomposes it when its geometry changes and rejects cyclic or too deeply nested frames. This adds:

- Composition: an anchored text frame (also nested) is on the page of the first frame of the story it is anchored in, followed outwards, so page-number markers show that page; moving that frame recomposes it.
- Tagged PDF: an anchored text frame's story is tagged as a story of its own instead of inside its host's paragraph.
- Damage: editing an anchored story repaints the view (with the composition cache nothing was repainted).
- Copy and paste: copied text takes the stories of its anchored text frames along. Pasting text (also into another document), pasting items into text, and pasting or duplicating a host frame give the copies fresh ids and stories of their own (Document::adopt_anchored), and the clipboard document keeps those stories.
- Document::fix_anchored_text_frames, run after every edit and for new documents: copies with taken ids get fresh ones and stories of their own, deleted anchored frames leave their threads and their stories go with them, and a frame whose story is missing gets an empty one. Before, copying, deleting or releasing an anchored text frame left a document that Document::check rejects, so it could not be opened again once saved.
- Release threads the released frame, under its new id, to its story.
- IDML import: an anchored text frame with an unknown or missing ParentStory gets an empty story instead of failing the import.

title: Fonts: Type › Reload Fonts reads fonts changed on disk again (#328, #547)
author: MaridWSH
body:
Closes #328. Closes #547.

Fonts installed, edited or removed while DesignCraft runs needed a restart: a font designer reinstalling an edited font kept seeing the old one (#328), and a font installed from another app wasn't found (#547).

**Type › Reload Fonts** (`font.reload`, reachable from the CLI, control channel and MCP like every command):

- `FontDb::reload_fonts` scans the font folders again (the existing `load_system_fonts`), then lets go of the shared faces whose installed file changed or is gone. A file counts as changed when its length or modification time differs from when it was read; `read_installed` records that stamp for every installed file read into the shared fonts. The next lookup reads the file as it is now, or finds the font missing. Variable-font instances and cached outlines of those faces go with them.
- Unchanged files aren't read again (their faces keep their ids). Bundled, added (`add_font`) and document fonts aren't touched.
- The command then gives the session a new composition cache and bumps every open document's revision, so text is composed again with what is installed now and the canvas redraws. It isn't an undo step and doesn't dirty the documents. It returns `{cataloged, changed: [path]}`.
- The reload is synchronous and the cache is replaced only after it, so there's no window in which a recompose can keep the old fonts (the ordering issue that closed #554). Clearing the fallback misses already landed with #315 and is reused.
- Faces are never freed (`FaceRef` leaks them by design), so each reload of an edited file keeps the old copy in memory. This is documented on the method.
- An open Find/Replace Font dialog refreshes its list after a reload.
- The Type menu lists Reload Fonts after Find/Replace Font. The Georgian label is added because the menu test requires every Georgian menu label; other languages fall back to English until translated.

Noticing font changes automatically, as InDesign does, is left open in gap 6. A foll…

title: Graphics: keep a failed OpenGL out of the instance
author: Hamza0101
body:
`cargo xtask ci` is red on `main` on macOS, and it is a real bug rather than a test that needs relaxing.

```
thread 'gpu::backend::tests::a_start_records_its_backend_until_a_frame_is_presented'
panicked at apps/designcraft/src/gpu/backend.rs:498:13:
assertion failed: !s.backends().contains(wgpu::Backends::GL)
```

## What the test was right about

`choose` pruned the failed list to the candidates of this platform:

```rust
failed.retain(|b| candidates.contains(b));
```

Dropping a stale entry is the point of that line and stays. But OpenGL is not only a candidate — off Windows it is also the **in-process fallback**, added to the instance whenever it has not failed:

```rust
fn instance_backends(backend: Backend, failed: &[Backend]) -> wgpu::Backends {
    let mut backends = backend.bit();
    if !cfg!(windows) && !failed.contains(&Backend::Gl) {
        backends |= wgpu::Backends::GL;
    }
    backends
}
```

On macOS `candidates()` is Metal alone, so a start that recorded OpenGL and never presented had that entry pruned a line later, `failed` came back empty, and OpenGL went straight back into the instance. The backend that had just failed to show a frame was offered again, every start, with nothing to retire it — exactly what the test is asserting against. The same holds for any platform where OpenGL is the fallback without being a candidate.

So the fix keeps an entry that can still be reached:

```rust
failed.retain(|b| candidates.contains(b) || (!cfg!(windows) && *b == Backend::Gl));
```

A non-candidate entry still cannot be chosen as a backend — `pick` only looks at candidates — so this changes nothing about which backend starts. It only stops a failed OpenGL from being handed back to the instance.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than skipping on macOS

The test's own comment says it is deliberately exercising this: *"This synthetic prior start records OpenGL even on Metal-only macOS."* It was written for this case, and the behaviour it describes is the o…

title: Native files: preserve automatic Ruby, Kenten and list-tab overrides
author: moppeeer
body:
Opening and saving a native document discarded explicit automatic Ruby/Kenten settings, turning them into inherited values. A child style that explicitly uses automatic Ruby size could therefore reopen at its parent's fixed 30 pt size. The same omission affected automatic list-tab overrides.

Found while auditing an unchanged save of the companion book during the [Navigation chapter](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY&t=809s): eight explicit CJK defaults disappeared from `document.json`, even though the chapter only navigates and inspects the document.

Existing native ZIP and legacy JSON regressions now cover these fields through both local overrides and a based-on style. Two Rust source files change; no project documentation or configuration changes.

**Older files:** documents saved before this change have already lost these explicit values, so they reopen as saved (the attributes inherit). This change stops further loss; it cannot restore what was dropped.

title: Hyphenate Esperanto between morphemes
author: axel584
body:
Closes #1201. **Builds on #1204** (Esperanto as a text language, #1142): until that one is merged, this PR shows both commits. Review only the last one, *Hyphenate Esperanto between morphemes*.

## The gap

Text tagged Esperanto set unhyphenated however narrow the column, so justified Esperanto opened wide gaps.

*Screenshot below: the same 140 pt justified column, 11 pt, rendered by `designcraft-cli script`.*

## Why morphemes, not patterns

Esperanto is agglutinative, and the convention is to break **between morphemes**, with the grammatical ending kept on the last piece: `tranĉ-ilo` (never `tran-ĉi-lo`), `mal-san-ul-ejo`, `vapor-ŝipo`. Liang patterns trained from a word list learn syllables and would break inside roots. Esperanto morphology is regular enough to segment exactly instead.

```
tranĉilojn,       → tranĉ-ilojn,
vaporŝipo         → vapor-ŝipo
akvobirdo         → akvo-birdo             (linking vowel stays)
Malsanulejo       → Mal-san-ul-ejo         (case kept)
lernejo-direktoro → lern-ejo-direktoro    (each part of a hyphenated compound; direktor is one root)
parolas           → parolas                (never before the ending alone)
```

## The change

- `crates/compose/src/hyphen/eo.rs`: the segmenter. Breaks go only between prefixes, roots and suffixes; the ending, and a linking vowel inside a compound (`akvo-birdo`), stay with the piece before them. **A word that doesn't split into known pieces isn't broken at all**: an unknown word gets no break rather than a guessed one.
  - The affixes are the official ones (Fundamento and Oficialaj Aldonoj).
  - Bounded for hostile input: words over 64 chars and pieces over 24 aren't segmented (the search is quadratic in word length). No panics, as the crate's `deny` lints require.
- `Lang::Esperanto` in `hyphen/mod.rs`, resolved from `"Esperanto"` and `eo`. Words with an apostrophe (elided `l'`) aren't broken, as for the pattern languages.
- `assets/hyphenation/eo.roots`: 7,327 roots, one per line.
- `crates/co…

title: Remove empty pages autoflow adds when placing into the primary frame
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1165

## Cause
`autoflow()` guesses how many frames are still needed from how much the full frames hold, then adds that many pages at once. When those frames hold less than a page usually does (because of a text wrap or a large heading), the guess is several times too high. It also rounds up when the text ends right at a page boundary. The cleanup afterwards removed an empty trailing frame only when it shared a page with the frame before it. With Smart Text Reflow there is one frame per page, so every extra page stayed until the next command.

## Fix
Empty trailing frames that are the first frame on their page are now removed too, along with their page, when autoflow added that page in this run and the frame is the only thing on it. The returned page count drops by one for each page removed. As a result, `pagesAdded` from `file.place` and `text.thread` now reports the pages that actually remain.

## Verified
- Regression test `smart_text_reflow_place_adds_no_empty_pages`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib smart_text_reflow_place_adds_no_empty_pages`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `gpu::backend::tests::a_start_records_its_backend_until_a_frame_is_presented`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The frame estimate itself is unchanged: autoflow still adds pages in one go and then removes the extra ones. Pages that were there before autoflow, and pages that hold other items, are never removed. When Smart Text Reflow runs is also unchanged.

title: Window: remember its size, position, maximized and full-screen state between launches
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #786.

The window was built with a fixed `with_inner_size([1440.0, 900.0])` and nothing remembered where it ended up, so every launch put it back at 1440 × 900 in the middle of the screen. This ports what @pravdomil did for EffectCraft in storytold/effectcraft#829 (`apps/effectcraft/src/window.rs`): the geometry goes to `window.json` next to `ui.json` and `prefs.json` (so it follows `DESIGNCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR`, the portable `DesignCraftData` folder from #580, and is skipped under `DESIGNCRAFT_NO_PREFS`), and on the next launch the window comes back with its size, position and maximized state, moved onto a monitor that is still connected: centred on the remaining one when its monitor was unplugged, made to fit and maximized when it no longer fits. A few differences from EffectCraft:

- the first launch keeps today's 1440 × 900 where the system puts it (EffectCraft also adapts the first window to small screens; happy to bring that over too);
- full screen is remembered as well (macOS green button / ⌃⌘F), with the windowed size kept to return to;
- the file is written at most once a second while the window changes, and on quit, never per frame; it is written atomically through `designcraft_engine::atomic`;
- `--control` runs save it like they save `ui.json` today (EffectCraft skips them); happy to switch.

`winit` 0.30 is now a direct dependency on Windows too (it already was on macOS and Linux), to list the monitors. It is the same winit eframe already pulls in, so no new crate in the tree.

One thing you may notice on macOS with Stage Manager on: a window saved left of x ≈ 220 pt reopens just right of the Stage Manager strip. That's macOS moving it when it's shown (winit reports the requested position right after we set it), not something this code does.

title: Skip phonetic guide text when importing XLSX strings
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/xlsx.rs:62 and :112 (shared strings are read with El::text, which includes <rPh> children; inline strings use the same call, crates/textimport/src/docx.rs:37)` (no existing issue): XLSX import appends phonetic guide (furigana) text to cell text, so "日本" is imported as "日本ニホン".

## Cause
The XLSX importer read each shared string (`<si>`) and inline string (`<is>`) with `El::text`, which concatenates the text of every descendant. The furigana in `<rPh><t>` was appended to the visible cell text, so "日本" was imported as "日本ニホン".

## Fix
Added `string_item` in `xlsx.rs`. It reads only the string's own `<t>` and the `<t>` of its `<r>` rich-text runs, and skips `<rPh>` and `<phoneticPr>`. The shared-string reads in `import` and `records`, and the inline-string read in `value`, now use it.

## Verified
- Regression test `phonetic_guide_text_is_not_cell_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport --lib phonetic_guide_text_is_not_cell_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `gpu::backend::tests::a_start_records_its_backend_until_a_frame_is_presented`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
`El::text` in `docx.rs` is unchanged because the DOCX paths still use it. The importer does not keep the phonetic readings anywhere.

title: fix(links): flag edits made in linked table cells
author: ChrisVerbick
body:
## What

Edits made in the cells of a linked spreadsheet (File › Place with Create Links on an `.xlsx`)
weren't detected as edits made in the layout. `story_hash` fingerprinted a story's text, paragraphs
and character runs but not `Story.tables`. As a result:

- the Links panel kept showing `edited: false` after a cell was changed, and
- Update Link replaced the edited cells without the "edits made … were replaced" warning, so the
  edits were lost silently.

## Fix

`story_hash` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/links.rs`) now includes `Story.tables` when the story has
tables. Stories without tables hash exactly as before, so links saved by earlier builds don't all
show up as edited.

## Tests

- `edits_in_linked_table_cells_are_flagged_and_the_update_warns` places a linked workbook, edits a
  cell with `table.setCell`, and checks that `links.list` reports `edited: true` and that
  `links.update` warns. It failed before the fix (`edited` was `false`).
- `story_hash_of_a_story_without_tables_is_unchanged` pins the hash of a story without tables to
  the value earlier builds compute. Hashing tables unconditionally makes it fail.

`cargo xtask ci`'s steps all pass on upstream main (c2609f92) with this change, apart from
`gpu::backend::tests::a_start_records_its_backend_until_a_frame_is_presented`, which fails on this
machine (macOS) on unchanged main too (`!s.backends().contains(wgpu::Backends::GL)`); run with it
skipped, every step passes.

## Note

A linked spreadsheet story saved by an earlier build will show as edited once after this change,
until its next update, because its recorded fingerprint didn't include the table. That errs on the
side of the warning.

title: feat(styles): delete table and cell styles
author: ChrisVerbick
body:
## What

Adds `style.cell.delete {name, replaceWith?}` (default `[None]`) and `style.table.delete {name,
replaceWith?}` (default `[Basic Table]`), mirroring `style.paragraph.delete`.

Table and cell styles are written into the cells and tables when applied, and editing a style
re-applies it, so deleting one re-applies too:

- cells or tables that used the deleted style get the replacement applied;
- styles based on it are rebased onto the replacement, and their cells or tables re-applied (as
  `style.cell.edit` and `style.table.edit` do);
- for a cell style, table styles that name it in a region (header, body, footer, left or right
  column) name the replacement instead.

The default replacements set nothing, so cells and tables keep their look and just lose the style
name. A replacement that was based on the deleted style takes the deleted style's parent instead,
so no style ends up based on itself (the #171 rule for paragraph styles). Built-in styles can't be
deleted, `replaceWith` can't be the deleted style, and unknown names are errors.

## Tests

`cmd::table::style_tests`:

- `deleting_a_cell_style_gives_its_cells_and_dependents_the_replacement` covers: cells, a
  dependent style, a table style region, a cell already using the replacement (its local override
  is kept), the default `[None]`, undo, the self-parent rule, and four error cases.
- `deleting_a_table_style_gives_its_tables_and_dependents_the_replacement` covers: a table using a
  dependent style, the default `[Basic Table]` keeping the look, and three error cases.

`cargo xtask ci`'s steps all pass on upstream main (c2609f92) with this change, apart from

title: Ignore non-finite <cSize> values in Tagged Text import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/tagged.rs:173` (no existing issue): Tagged Text import accepts non-finite font sizes (<cSize:NaN> / <cSize:inf>) and stores them in the story.

## Cause
The Tagged Text importer parsed `<cSize:...>` with `value.trim().parse().ok()`. Rust's f64 parser accepts "NaN", "inf" and "infinity", so these became a non-finite character size on the imported story.

## Fix
The parsed `<cSize>` value is now filtered with `is_finite()`. A non-finite size is treated like an unparsable one, so the run gets no size override. A regression test covers `NaN`, `inf`, `infinity` and `-inf`.

## Verified
- Regression test `non_finite_char_size_is_ignored`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport non_finite_char_size_is_ignored`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `gpu::backend::tests::a_start_records_its_backend_until_a_frame_is_presented`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
Unparsable or non-finite sizes are still not counted in `skipped`, which matches the existing handling of unparsable sizes. I did not change layout or serialization, and did not check layout or save/reopen with the imported value.

title: (fix) macOS: accept .idml dropped on the app icon and opens with contextual "open with..."
author: seanth
body:
## Problem

With #417, `.idml` files open from the Dock but **not** when dropped on DesignCraft's icon in Finder, and DesignCraft is missing from **Open With** for them. This happens on Macs where InDesign is installed.

`Info.plist.in` declares `.idml` only through `LSItemContentTypes` = `ai.storyteller.designcraft.idml`, a type DesignCraft *imports* (`UTImportedTypeDeclarations`). When another installed app *exports* a type for the same extension (InDesign does), macOS gives the exported declaration priority. So `.idml` files carry InDesign's type, DesignCraft's entry no longer matches them, and Finder refuses the drop. The Dock still accepts it, which hides the problem.

You can check this on an affected Mac with:

    mdls -name kMDItemContentType some-file.idml

It reports InDesign's type, not `ai.storyteller.designcraft.idml`.

## Fix

Add a second `CFBundleDocumentTypes` entry that matches by extension (`CFBundleTypeExtensions` = `idml`). It has the same role and rank as the existing IDML entry (Viewer, Alternate), so DesignCraft never takes over as the default app for `.idml`. An extension entry matches whatever type the file ends up with.

It has to be a dict of its own: in a dict that has `LSItemContentTypes`, LaunchServices ignores the extension keys. The existing entry and the imported type declaration are unchanged, so Macs without InDesign behave as before.

Only `packaging/macos/Info.plist.in` changes (15 lines, including a comment that explains the entry).

## Testing

- [x] The generated plist parses, and the three document types read back as expected
- [x] macOS with InDesign installed: build with `packaging/macos/package.sh`, install, and launch once so LaunchServices re-registers the app. Then drop an `.idml` on the app icon in Finder: it opens.
- [x] Open With on an `.idml` lists DesignCraft
- [x] Double-click still opens `.idml` in the default app (InDesign), and Dock drops still work

title: (fix)Drop caps: scale with the cap's point size, as InDesign doesDrop cap size
author: seanth
body:
## Problem

A drop cap is the same size whatever point size it's set in. Set the first letter of a 3-line drop cap at 10 pt, 15 pt or 7.5 pt over 10 pt text, and all three come out identical.

`split_drop_cap` scales the cap by

    k = (drop + body cap height) / (the cap's own cap height)

so that its cap height spans from the first line's cap height down to the last dropped line's baseline. The cap's own cap height grows with its point size, so the point size cancels out of `k`.

## What InDesign does

In InDesign the cap's point size changes its size. InDesign fits the cap as if it were set at the body text's size, then scales it by the cap's size over the body's, keeping the cap's baseline on the last dropped line. A larger cap rises above the first line, and a smaller one falls short of it.

I checked this against an InDesign capture (Palatino, 14 pt body, 18 pt italic T, 2 lines; observed black-box, nothing from InDesign committed). There the cap height is 2.04× the line gap; this formula predicts 2.03×.

## Change (`crates/compose`)

- `split_drop_cap` multiplies `k` by `ratio` = (the point size of the cap's tallest glyph) / (the body's point size). A cap at the body's size fits exactly as before.
  - `ratio` falls back to 1 when either size is missing, zero or not finite.
  - The existing guards still apply: the clamp to (0, 1000], and a one-line drop cap keeps its own size when that is smaller.
- `DropCap` records the cap height it was set at (`cap`).
- The drop cap's box (`DropCapBox::rect`, used for the selection highlight and the caret) starts at the top of the line or the top of the cap, whichever is higher. Selected glyphs are drawn inverted, so without this the part of a cap that rises above its line would vanish when selected.
- The body lines don't move. Only the cap's own size changes.

## Test

`drop_cap_scales_with_its_point_size`: a 3-line drop cap over 10 pt text, with the cap set at 10, 15 and 7.5 pt. It checks that:

- at 10 pt the cap fills …

title: Ignore out-of-range font sizes in RTF import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/rtf.rs:219` (no existing issue): RTF import stores zero, negative and huge font sizes (\fs0, \fs-8, \fs999999999).

## Cause
The RTF `\fs` control word set the character size to `param / 2.0` with no range check. `\fs0`, `\fs-8` and `\fs999999999` produced sizes of 0, -4 and about 5e8 pt in the imported story. The engine limits character size to 0.1–1296 pt.

## Fix
`\fs` now stores the size only when it is within 0.1–1296 pt. Otherwise the run keeps no explicit size and uses the default.

## Verified
- Regression test `font_size_out_of_range_is_not_stored`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport --lib font_size_out_of_range_is_not_stored`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Sizes are not clamped to the nearest limit. A value outside the range is treated as invalid, not as a request for the maximum or minimum size. Rendering of invalid sizes was not looked at.

title: Ignore non-finite w:sz, w:spacing and w:ind values in DOCX import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/docx.rs:183 (run_attrs, w:sz) and :206-214 (para_attrs, w:spacing/w:ind via the `tw` closure)` (no existing issue): DOCX import stores NaN/inf font sizes, paragraph spacing and indents (w:sz, w:spacing, w:ind).

## Cause
The DOCX importer parsed w:sz, w:spacing and w:ind with `str::parse::<f64>()`, which accepts "NaN", "inf" and "-inf". It never checked the result for finiteness, so those values went into the imported character size and paragraph spacing and indents.

## Fix
Both parse sites now apply `.filter(|v| v.is_finite())`: the `w:sz` path in `run_attrs` and the `tw` closure in `para_attrs`. Non-finite values are dropped like any other unparseable value. The regression test imports NaN/inf/-inf in `w:sz`, `w:spacing`, and in `w:ind` left, right, firstLine and hanging, and checks the stored values are None or finite.

## Verified
- Regression test `non_finite_sizes_spacing_and_indents_are_ignored`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport --lib non_finite_sizes_spacing_and_indents_are_ignored`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Finite but extreme values (for example a huge w:sz) are still stored as before. Other importers and attributes are unchanged.

title: (feat? bug?)Flexible word spacing
author: seanth
body:
## Problem

IDML files laid out in DesignCraft break justified lines differently from InDesign. In a 36-page InDesign dictionary, only 72.5% of lines matched exactly. On page 1 a single entry took three lines instead of two, which pushed an inline image into the next column and shifted every later page.

The cause: DesignCraft treats a paragraph's **Minimum Word Spacing** as a hard limit. InDesign doesn't. It squeezes a justified line's word spaces below the Minimum, sometimes to 25–35% of a space, when the alternative is a much looser line. (Its H&J Violations highlight marks these lines; the Adobe help also says the word-spacing limits can't always be honoured.)

## How the rule was found

Observed black-box: InDesign's PDF output was compared with the IDML it was exported from. No InDesign files are committed; the tests use synthetic text.

- **Paragraph Composer:** a 36-page dictionary, 451 justified multi-line paragraphs, hyphenation off. Each paragraph's actual breaks and the exact widths InDesign set were extracted from the PDF. Every possible break sequence was then scored under candidate cost functions.
- **Single-line Composer:** a 30-page story collection exported twice, with hyphenation off and on (same text and settings otherwise), giving about 1,475 line decisions per version.

Findings:

| Composer | Rule | InDesign's breaks reproduced | Minimum as a hard limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paragraph | each line costs ln(spacing ÷ Desired)², ×4 when squeezed; least total wins | 89% of paragraphs (86–90% on held-out halves) | 75% |
| Single-line | fill to the Minimum (hyphenation points included); if that leaves the line looser than Desired, take one more word or word part when the squeeze falls short of Desired by less than 0.19× what the loose line exceeds it | 96.8% / 97.6% of lines (no hyphenation / hyphenation) | 95.1% / 96.2% |

Squeezing costs about 4–5× as much as stretching in both composers. Spaces never went below about 24% in the samples, so the im…

title: Ignore NaN and infinite numbers when importing IDML
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/idml/src/import.rs:2748 (stroke_from: StrokeWeight, MiterLimit), also El::num in crates/idml/src/xml.rs:96 and the plain `.parse().ok()` calls around import.rs:1833, 2823 and 2832` (no existing issue): IDML import accepts NaN/inf in StrokeWeight, MiterLimit, Angle, Width, Height, SpaceBefore, LeftIndent and similar attributes; the saved .designcraft file can't be reopened.

## Cause
The IDML importer reads many numeric attributes with `str::parse::<f64>()`, which accepts `NaN`, `inf` and `-inf`. `El::num`, the stroke weight and miter limit, tab positions, leading, dash and stripe arrays, and gradient start points had no finiteness check, so these values reached the document. serde_json then saved them as `null`, and the saved file could not be loaded again.

## Fix
`El::num` and `names::leading_in` now treat non-finite values as absent. Stroke weight, miter limit and tab positions are filtered the same way. A new module-level `finite_nums` helper returns an empty list when any number in a whitespace-separated list is non-finite, and the stripe, dash and gradient start paths use it. Table cell spans read the raw value, so an infinite span still clamps to the table edge as before.

## Verified
- Regression tests `idml_non_finite_numbers_import_to_a_document_that_reopens`, `non_finite_numbers_count_as_absent`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib idml_non_finite_numbers_import_to_a_document_that_reopens && cargo test -p designcraft-idml --lib non_finite_numbers_count_as_absent`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`designcraft_format::save` still checks only item geometry for non-finite values. This change stops non-finite numbers at the IDML import boundary and does not add a general check to the save path.

title: (bug? feature?)Anchored objects: select and resize them with the Selection tool
author: seanth
body:
Address #1191 

## Problem

An inline (or above-line, or custom) anchored object lives in its story, not on a spread. So the Selection tool's hit test, which only looks at spread items, never finds it: clicking an inline image selects the text frame around it, and the image can't be resized. In InDesign, clicking it selects the image's frame and its handles resize it.

## Behaviour

Matched against InDesign by observing it (no InDesign files committed):

- **Click** an anchored object with the Selection tool: it's selected where it sits in the text, with its bounding box and 8 handles.
  - **Dragging** it doesn't move it; it flows with the text.
  - **A double click** selects it rather than putting the caret in the text around it.
- **Drag a handle.** Only an outline follows the pointer, and only the grabbed edge moves. A W/H readout in the document's ruler units sits by the pointer. The object and the text stay as they are during the drag.
- **On release** the frame takes the outline's size, and the picture is cropped from the sides that moved. Then the text places the object again: a frame made narrower from the left snaps back to the left of its line, and the lines reflow. It's one undo step.
  - **⌘-drag** scales the content with the frame.
  - **Shift** keeps the proportions.
  - **A press on a handle without a drag** changes nothing.
- **Delete** removes a selected anchored object from the text.
- **Object › Anchored Object › Options and Release** act on the selected object.

## Change

- **`doc`:** `Selection.anchored: Option<AnchoredSel { story, index }>`. An anchored object isn't one of `Selection::items`, so it gets its own field. `is_empty` counts it, and `selection.set` / `selection.toggle` clear it.
- **`engine` (`cmd/anchored.rs`):**
  - `anchored.select {story, index}` selects an anchored object.
  - `anchored.resize {story?, index?, from, to, content?}` resizes it in its own space. The frame's path is baked as in `transform.resize`; `content: true` u…

title: Text: the ideographic space from input methods on macOS (winit drops it)
author: con3code
body:
Pressing Space in a Japanese input mode should type the ideographic space (U+3000). On macOS it types a plain space. This PR works around that in the canvas, only where the platform loses the character, and leaves the other platforms as they are.

**Where it goes wrong.** On macOS, winit only forwards `insertText:` as an input-method commit while there is marked text. Space with nothing being composed is inserted by the input method with no marked text, so winit drops that text and reports the key event with the key's own character instead. The canvas receives `Text(" ")` and the U+3000 is lost. This is below egui, so #366 can't see it either.

**Why only macOS.** On current `main` with the Japanese input method, Windows already types U+3000 (the input method's character arrives as the key's text), while macOS types a plain space; Japanese input itself and the candidate window work on both since #366. Linux input methods send the character as a commit and the browser gives it in the input event, so I expect those to be fine too, but I haven't run them. The change does nothing outside macOS (`typed_text` returns the text unchanged unless `cfg!(target_os = "macos")`).

**The workaround.** While the text before it was Japanese the input method committed, a plain space from the Space key is typed as U+3000. The input method counts as Japanese when its composition shows kana, which only Japanese ones do.

- Shift+Space stays a plain space, as the Japanese input methods have it.
- Letters typed straight from the keys (the input method's Roman mode) end this, so spaces between Latin words stay plain.
- Chinese and Korean input methods are left alone. They type plain spaces by default, and Korean separates words with them, so pinyin, zhuyin and hangul compositions don't start it.
- Accents a Latin input method composes (é, ñ) don't start it either.
- Moving the text caret to another story or document, or out of the text (another tool, a text field, a dialog), ends it too.

title: Reject a non-finite or non-positive --scale in designcraft-cli run
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `apps/designcraft-cli/src/main.rs:361 (`--scale` parse) and :386 (export); crates/render/src/lib.rs:422-423 (render_page)` (no existing issue): designcraft-cli run: --scale 0, a negative value or NaN exits 0 and writes a 1×1 PNG; --scale inf reports "no such page".

## Cause
`--scale` was parsed with a bare `f64::parse`, so `0`, negative values, `nan` and `inf` were all accepted. `render_page` clamps the computed width and height with `.max(1.0)`, so zero, negative and NaN scales became a 1×1 image, and those runs exited 0 with a useless file. Infinity was also accepted and was reported as "no such page" for page 0.

## Fix
The `--scale` parse in `designcraft-cli run` now accepts only a finite number greater than 0. Anything else fails up front with "bad --scale: expected a positive number", before any export is written.

## Verified
- Regression test `run_scale_that_is_not_finite_and_positive_is_an_error`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-cli --test cli run_scale_that_is_not_finite_and_positive_is_an_error`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`render_page` in crates/render is unchanged. The CLI is the only caller that takes the scale from user input.

title: Esperanto as a text language
author: axel584
body:
Closes #1142.

## The gap

Esperanto wasn't in the Language list, so documents that mix French and Esperanto (Espéranto-France publications tag Esperanto words through a "mot Eo" character style) couldn't tag those words: typographer's quotes, and later hyphenation and spelling, used the surrounding language.

## The change

`Esperanto` joins the Language list (Character panel, Properties › Character, style options) and maps to the BCP 47 tag `eo`:

```
before:  language_tag("Esperanto") = None
after:   language_tag("Esperanto") = Some("eo")   language_tag("$ID/Esperanto") = Some("eo")
```

- **IDML**: the name keeps its spelling, so `AppliedLanguage="$ID/Esperanto"` round-trips.
- **Quotes**: English-style “…” and ‘…’. Esperanto has no single convention; “…” is the common one in its publications.
- **Hyphenation and spelling**: none for now. Esperanto isn't treated as English (the existing language test asserts it), so English patterns never break Esperanto words. Hyphenation follows in #1168 (#1201); spelling is #1202.
- The label is translated in every UI locale (Espéranto, エスペラント語, 世界语, الإسبرانتو, ესპერანტო, Есперанто…).

13 files, +17/−2. Most are one line per locale.

## Docs

`localization-parity.md` (language list, header) and a `ROADMAP.md` progress-log line.

## Checks

`cargo xtask ci` on this branch, rebased on `main` at `fc36957f`:

```
CI summary: all 7 steps passed (fmt, clippy, test, pdf-deps, assets, layers, wasm)
```

title: Keep a moved equation in place when editing its LaTeX
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/mathexpr.rs:73-83` (no existing issue): math.insert with `id` jumps a moved equation away from its place (offset doubled).

## Cause
`math.insert {id, latex}` took the base position from `old.bounds()`, which already includes the item's transform `xf`. It built the new path and graphic at that position and kept the old `xf`. A moved, rotated or scaled equation therefore had its transform applied twice and jumped.

## Fix
The new path and graphic are now built at the corner of the old path in the item's own inner space (`old.path.bounds()`), and the existing `xf` is kept. The edit returns a `math.insert` error, instead of relocating the item, if the equation has no geometry.

## Verified
- Regression tests `editing_a_transformed_equation_keeps_its_place`, `editing_a_moved_equation_keeps_its_bounds`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib mathexpr::tests::editing`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Inserting a new equation, and the other `math.*` commands, are unchanged.

title: Make the dock collapse and expand chevrons clickable (#1203)

body:

title: PDF/X-4 export: add xmp:MetadataDate and xmpMM:VersionID to the XMP (#1207)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes the two Acrobat preflight errors in #1207: the PDF/X-4 XMP had no `xmp:MetadataDate` (XMP Basic) and no `xmpMM:VersionID` (XMP Media Management).

- `make_pdfx4` now takes the export date and adds one more `rdf:Description` next to the existing `pdfxid:GTS_PDFXVersion` and `pdf:Trapped` ones, with `xmp:MetadataDate` (the same creation time that goes into Info, UTC) and `xmpMM:VersionID` `1`. With no clock (wasm) the date is the epoch, because PDF/X-4 requires the entry.
- `check_pdfx4` reports either entry if it is missing, as it already does for the PDF/X version.
- `docs/target-app-parity.md` lists the two entries with the rest of the PDF/X-4 output.

Test: `pdfx4_xmp_has_metadata_date_and_version_id` exports a PDF/X-4 with a fixed date, checks both entries and their values, checks that `check_pdfx4` passes, and that it reports both entries when they are removed. It fails without the fix.

Not changed here: the issue's other observations. `xmpMM:RenditionClass` `proof` is not a preflight error, and the title (`Untitled-2` for a saved document) needs a decision on whether the file name or a document setting should be used. I can do either in a follow-up if you want.

title: Keep the mapped style of the first paragraph when placing text at an empty caret (#1208)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1208.

`frame.create` with `"content": "text"` leaves a caret in the new frame, so the following `file.place` goes through the insertion-point path, even when `frame` is given. That path calls `Story::insert_story`, which merges the first placed paragraph into the paragraph at the caret and keeps that paragraph's format (`[Basic Paragraph]`). That is the right behaviour for pasting into existing text. Here, though, the styleMap result for the first paragraph was dropped. Later paragraphs keep their own formats, which is why only the first one was wrong.

The fix: when the caret is in an empty paragraph, that paragraph now takes the first imported paragraph's format, keeping its table anchor. This matches what `fill` already does for a whole-story place. Placing at a caret inside existing text is unchanged and still keeps the destination paragraph's format.

Test: `word_first_paragraph_into_empty_caret_keeps_mapped_style` follows the issue's repro: a new text frame, then `file.place` of a .docx with `styleMap {"Title": "Headline"}`. It expects `["Headline", "Body"]`. Without the fix, the first paragraph is `[Basic Paragraph]`.

title: Styles: paragraph direction and kashida level in Paragraph Style Options

body:

title: Mojikumi: consecutive punctuation closes up
author: con3code
body:
A follow-up to #129, as discussed in #353.

Two punctuation marks in a row kept half an em between them: the rule for neighbours took the larger of the two blanks, so 」。 was set 」 + ½ em + 。. JLREQ 3.1.4 closes these up: opening brackets together, and closing brackets, commas and full stops together, touch.

- `」。` `」、` `。」` `」』` `（「` `「『`: no space between them now.
- `」・` `・「` (a middle dot beside a bracket, JLREQ 3.1.4 ⑦): the middle dot's quarter em only, for `・：；`.
- `」「` and `。「` (closing then opening): still half an em, the larger blank, as before.
- Every other pair is unchanged.

The rule is in `Rules::pair`, so line breaking, justification and preflight all see the same widths. It applies to the Japanese base sets only: the Chinese sets keep the larger blank, as before, since Chinese styles set consecutive marks their own way (Taiwan's are centred and full width) and I've only checked the Japanese result against InDesign. title: Mojikumi: reduce middle dots first, never a full stop's space
author: con3code
body:
A follow-up to #129, as discussed in #353. Independent of #1222; the two merge cleanly in either order.

When a line takes a character in (push-in), every punctuation blank in it closed up at once: middle dots, brackets, commas and the space after a full stop all had the same priority and could all reach zero. JLREQ 3.8.3 reduces them in an order:

1. The quarter ems around middle dots (・：；). `！？` share this tier: JLREQ sets them solid (Table 1) and allows the quarter em only as an alternative (3.1.6), so it goes first.
2. The half ems after closing brackets and commas, and before opening brackets.
3. Not the space after a full stop: it stays half an em, before an opening bracket too.

The tier follows the character classes, not the size of the blank.

Wa-ō aki (priority 3) and the spaces between ideographs (10) come after these, as before. Custom mojikumi rows keep their own priorities. Stretching is unchanged: these blanks don't stretch. This is JLREQ's order, so it applies to the Japanese base sets; the Chinese sets keep reducing every punctuation blank together, as before.

Existing Japanese documents that need push-in can break lines differently, including those whose custom tables override only some pairs.

**Testing.**
- `doc::mojikumi`: `middle_dots_reduce_first_and_a_full_stops_space_never`, priorities and minimums in both Japanese base sets (`：；！？` with the middle dots, `！「` with the brackets), and the Chinese sets unchanged.
- `compose`: `mojikumi_push_in_reduces_middle_dots_first_and_never_a_full_stop`. A closing bracket taken into a line a quarter em short closes up only around the middle dot; a line shorter still closes up the comma next, and the full stop's space stays. Without the change the reduction is spread over all three.
- `cargo fmt --check`, clippy, the workspace tests and `cargo xtask wasm` pass. It also merges cleanly with #1127 and #1222, and their tests pass together.

title: Text: adjust hyperlink and placeholder source ranges on story edits (#1219)
author: kk376
body:
Closes #1219

### Problem

Text-anchored hyperlinks (`HyperlinkSource::Text { story, start, end }`) and data-merge placeholders (`PlaceholderAnchor::Text { story, start, end }`) store byte ranges into story text. When text is inserted or deleted earlier in the story, or within the anchored range, these byte offsets remained static:
1. Typing or pasting text earlier in the story drifted hyperlinks and placeholders onto unrelated trailing text.
2. If text containing multibyte UTF-8 codepoints was added or removed before the link, the range shifted incorrectly relative to byte vs character counts.
3. Deleting text inside or encompassing the link left stale or zero-length hyperlinks pointing at empty positions.
4. Wholesale story replacement (`set_story_text`) retained stale hyperlinks and placeholders whose source ranges no longer matched the new content.

### Solution

1. **`Document::adjust_text_ranges` in `designcraft-doc`:**
   - Centralized offset reconciliation helper for any edit that replaces `del_range` with `ins_len` bytes in `story`.
   - Distinguishes deletion before the link (`del_before`) vs deletion inside the link (`del_inside`).
   - Insertion before the link shifts `start` and `end` forward. Insertion at `start` shifts the span forward (so typing immediately before the link does not swallow the new text into the link).
   - Insertion inside the link (`start < pos < end`) expands the link.
   - Deletion consuming the link clamps to surviving text, or prunes it if entirely consumed (`s_new >= e_new`).
   - Prunes stale references when `Document::set_story_text` completely replaces story content.
   - Applies identically to both `doc.hyperlinks` and `doc.data_merge.placeholders`.

2. **Hooked into Engine text mutations:**
   - Typing / pasting (`cmd::text::insert`, including autocorrect and track changes).
   - Deletions (`cmd::text::delete`, `cmd::text::delete_selection`).
   - Programmatic replacements (`cmd::text::story.replaceRange`).

title: Tables: cell First Baseline offset (Cell Options › Text › First Baseline)
author: aykutfirat
body:
### Problem
Cells and cell styles have no first-baseline setting, so every cell sets its first line by the Ascent offset (the
font's typographic ascender). IDML documents often set `FirstBaselineOffset` on a cell style, usually `CapHeight`
and often through a table style's body region. DesignCraft ignores it, so every row composes taller than the
document asks.

With a font whose typographic ascender is a full em, each row grows by roughly a third of the point size, and long
tables overset and lose their last rows.

**Repro** (synthetic, built with DesignCraft's own commands):
```sh
# A 16 × 2 table in a 340 pt frame, rows at least 20 pt; its body cell style sets First Baseline = Cap Height.
args=(run --cmd 'file.new={"preset":"Letter","pages":1}'
  --cmd 'frame.create={"rect":[72,72,372,412],"content":"text","text":""}'
  --cmd 'text.select={"story":9,"anchor":0,"focus":0}' --cmd 'table.insert={"rows":16,"cols":2,"width":300}'
  --cmd 'style.cell.create={"name":"Cap","insets":6,"firstBaseline":"capHeight","vj":"center"}'
  --cmd 'style.table.create={"name":"Tight","body":"Cap"}' --cmd 'style.table.apply={"name":"Tight","story":9,"table":10}'
  --cmd 'table.setRowHeight={"height":20,"mode":"atLeast","story":9,"table":10,"rows":[0,15],"cols":[0,1]}')
for r in $(seq 0 15); do args+=(--cmd "table.setCell={\"story\":9,\"table\":10,\"row\":$r,\"col\":0,\"text\":\"Row $((r+1))\"}"); done
designcraft-cli "${args[@]}" --cmd 'file.exportIdml={"path":"/tmp/cap-height-table.idml"}'   # this branch (writes the attribute)
designcraft-cli run --cmd 'file.openIdml={"path":"/tmp/cap-height-table.idml"}' --cmd preflight.run   # 0.8.0 vs this branch
```
(An IDML with `FirstBaselineOffset="CapHeight"` on a cell style from any other source shows the same thing.)
- **0.8.0:** rows grow and rows 14–16 overset (preflight: `Overset text`).
- **This branch:** all 16 rows fit and preflight is clean.

title: PDF: preserve placed optional-content visibility in vector exports
author: KnottyDyes
body:
Fixes #906.

Keep a placed PDF's layer visibility in plain and PDF/X-4 vector exports.
The export now registers the placed file's optional-content groups in its
own `/OCProperties`, with hidden groups in `/D/OFF`, so viewers and RIPs
both leave them out. This covers the source file's default state and
per-frame overrides from `object.pdfLayers`, and repeated placements of
the same file keep independent states. The layers stay vector.

Files from Illustrator and InDesign record usage events (`/AS`) in their
default configuration. Those are accepted, and the hidden set comes from
`/BaseState`, `/ON` and `/OFF`; the output configuration omits `/AS`, as
PDF/X-4 requires. Groups referenced only from page resources, with no
catalog `/OCProperties`, are drawn as visible.

Files whose layer setup is slightly off still export, with a warning
that names the file:
- `/D` missing or unreadable, or a `/BaseState` other than ON or OFF:
  every layer is shown, and per-frame overrides still apply.
- A group named in `/ON` or `/OFF` but missing from `/OCGs`: the group is
  added and its state kept, so a layer the file hides stays hidden.
- A group with no readable name: a name is generated and its state kept.

Export still fails where hiding would be a guess: a group in both `/ON`
and `/OFF`, references that don't resolve, an override whose group can't
be read, or an encrypted file. The error names the placed file.

A placed file is only rewritten when something has to change. When every
layer stays visible, the original bytes are embedded unchanged, so a file
with a damaged cross-reference table (which the parser repairs on open)
exports as it does on `main`. If a layer has to be hidden in such a file,
export fails with an error saying its cross-reference table is damaged.
Prepared copies are cached per file and hidden-layer set, so a file placed
many times is read once.

Follow-ups: print-usage settings (`/Usage /Print /PrintState`) and IDML
`GraphicLayer` visibility overrides.

title: [fix] Web relink of images
author: seanth
body:
Addresses #1243 

In the browser, a linked graphic can’t be read from its path. An IDML opened in the web build therefore loses every linked picture, because its Links folder isn’t reachable. Links › Relink… and Relink to Folder… didn’t help: both ask the desktop file dialog for a path, the web build has no such dialog, and the clicks were silently ignored. A web user had no way to bring the pictures in.

This adds a relink that works from file contents instead of paths:

links.relinkFiles {files: [{name, base64}], asset?}:
With asset, it relinks that graphic from the first file.
Without it, it relinks every missing graphic from the file of the same name, ignoring case, all in one undo step.
It returns {relinked, notFound, unused}.
It shares the path relink’s code: PDF page and crop, pixel size. Every replacement is built before the edit, so a bad file changes nothing.
A file with the same name as the link keeps the link’s path, so the document still finds the file on the computer it came from. A file with another name becomes the link.
Web, Relink…: opens the browser’s file picker for the selected graphic.
Web, Relink to Folder…: opens the browser’s folder picker (<input webkitdirectory>) and relinks every missing graphic from the images in the chosen folder.
Web, dropping images on the window: an image named like a missing graphic relinks it, and any other image is placed as before. Dropped files are read and delivered together, so a dropped Links folder’s contents relink in one undo step.

Desktop behaviour is unchanged.

Tests:

title: fix(fonts): discover named instances before listing paragraph styles
author: makesomethingshit
body:
## Summary

Related to #1210.

**The reporter's original symptom was not reproduced:** selecting an available named instance such as SemiBold in Paragraph Style Options did not fail to apply in the tested setup. On the unpatched code, selection and persistence worked after the font was loaded. The test uses the Bricolage Grotesque family named in #1210, but the reporter's exact font file/version and original document remain untested.

This PR fixes a confirmed cold-discovery defect for a catalog-only variable family with no same-family static face preloaded: named instances are absent from the initial Font Style combo, and the Family menu caches an incomplete list. The relationship between this defect and the reported application failure remains unproven; resolution of the original report remains unverified.

## Changes

- Read the Family menu's styles after its existing face lookup loads the font and discovers named instances.
- Load the selected family once per Style popup opening and cache the resulting styles until closure, a render gap, or a document font scope change. Missing catalog files are retried on reopening, rather than every frame.

title: IDML: TOC styles read InDesign's $ID/-prefixed separators and Properties-child entry styles
author: aykutfirat
body:
### Problem
InDesign writes a TOC style entry's values in two ways the importer doesn't read:

- **Separator:** written with the built-in prefix, `Separator="$ID/^y"`, where `^y` is the right indent tab.
  `toc_separator_in` kept the prefix, so every regenerated entry read `Welcome$ID/<tab>3`.
- **Styles:** `FormatStyle`, `PageNumberStyle` and `SeparatorStyle` are written as `<Properties>` children, not
  attributes. `toc_of` read only attributes, so a regenerated TOC lost its entry paragraph style and page-number
  character style. Entries came out in the default style, wrapping and with the wrong case.

How InDesign writes it (from a TOC style it exports):
```xml
<TOCStyleEntry Name="Heading 1" Level="1" PageNumberPosition="AfterEntry" Separator="$ID/^y">
  <Properties>
    <FormatStyle type="object">ParagraphStyle/$ID/TOC%3aTOC body text</FormatStyle>
    <PageNumberStyle type="object">CharacterStyle/TOC Page Number</PageNumberStyle>
    <SeparatorStyle type="string">$ID/[Same Style]</SeparatorStyle>
  </Properties>
</TOCStyleEntry>
```

### Change
- **`names::toc_separator_in`:** strips `$ID/` before decoding, so `$ID/^y` becomes a tab, the default separator.
- **`toc_of`:** reads FormatStyle, PageNumberStyle and SeparatorStyle with `prop`, which accepts either an attribute
  or a `Properties` child.
- **Test:** `toc_style_entries_read_id_prefixed_separators_and_styles` imports a synthetic TOC style written as above.
  It checks the separator, the entry style (`TOC/TOC body text`), the page-number style and the title style. Before
  this change it fails on the separator (`Some("$ID/\t")`), then on the entry style (`None`).

### Checks
- `cargo fmt`; `cargo test -p designcraft-idml` (all pass).
- After the change, a regenerated TOC (`toc.update`) in a real 32-page guide template keeps its entry style, its dot
  leaders and its page-number style. That file isn't ours to share.

title: View: Bleed and Slug screen modes show their area; draw the slug guide
author: Hamza0101
body:
## What was wrong

`ScreenMode` has five variants and all five can be picked — from the toolbar, from View › Screen Mode, and through `view.screenMode {mode: normal|preview|bleed|slug|presentation}`. The canvas asked only whether the mode was `Preview` or `Presentation`:

```rust
let preview = matches!(app.ui.screen_mode, ScreenMode::Preview | ScreenMode::Presentation);
```

`Bleed` and `Slug` fell to the `else`, so both drew exactly what `Normal` drew — margin, column, bleed and baseline guides, frame edges, hidden characters, the non-printing indicators, content across the whole pasteboard. Picking either did nothing visible.

Separately, the slug guide was never drawn at all. `settings.slug_color` is in the model, is set from Preferences › Guides & Pasteboard, and is exported and round-tripped — and had **no reader anywhere in the workspace**, while its three siblings are all painted in `draw_guides`:

| | painted |
|---|---|
| `margin_color` | `canvas.rs:977` |
| `column_color` | `canvas.rs:981` |
| `bleed_color` | `canvas.rs:948` |
| `slug_color` | — |

`docs/parity-checklist.md` scores "Screen modes" **D** at P0.

## What this changes

- `Normal` is the only mode that is not a preview mode, so `Bleed` and `Slug` now hide the guides and non-printing marks and render `printing_only`, as `Preview` already did.
- New `shown_area` gives what a mode shows of a spread: the trim for `Preview` and `Presentation`, out to the bleed box for `Bleed`, out to the bleed **and** slug boxes for `Slug`. title: Document Setup: read a number without a unit in the document's units
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1247.

Document Setup formats its fields in the document's units, but `open_document_setup` never set the dialog's own unit, which `Dialog::new` starts at picas. So a number typed without a unit was read in picas: 5 in a millimetre document became 60 pt (21.167 mm). This hit every measure in the dialog (width, height, margins, bleed and slug), not only bleed. The fix sets `d.unit` to the document's horizontal units, as Create Guides and the other dialogs that open in the document's units already do, so a bare 5 now means 5 mm there, matching the ruler units. Values with a unit (5 mm, 1p0, 36 pt) parse as before.

The existing Document Setup tests always typed the unit, which is why this went unnoticed; the new one uses a millimetre document and bare numbers.

Validation:
- `dialogs::tests::document_setup_reads_a_bare_number_in_the_documents_units`: fails on main (bleed `[60.0, 60.0, 60.0, 60.0]`, 5 picas), passes here; the other `document_setup` tests still pass

title: Type: Convert Bullets and Numbering to Text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Type › Bulleted & Numbered Lists › Convert Bullets and Numbering to Text: the selected paragraphs' bullets and numbers become ordinary text.

In InDesign the command works on the selected paragraphs (a caret converts its own paragraph): the bullet or number and what follows it in the label (tab, en space, the number's expression) become characters at the start of the paragraph, and the paragraph is no longer a list item. This PR does the same through a new `list.convertToText` command under the existing submenu. The characters typed in are exactly the label composition drew: named lists carried on from earlier stories, Start At, levels (`^1`…`^9`), the number's expression, and the label's look (number/bullet character style, bullet font, Digits). To guarantee that, the label pass moves into `compose::list_labels`, which the compose loop now consumes as well, so there is one place that counts; the unnamed-list counter used to live in the layout loop and be restored on re-lays, and a pass up front gives the same numbers (the existing compose list tests are unchanged and green). `rewind` no longer takes the counter: #1039 adds one `rewind` call, so on its rebase that call drops one argument. The paragraphs get a `listType: none` override, so when the paragraph style defines the list only the selected paragraphs leave it (round-trips as `NoList` in IDML). When the list sets a Tab Position, the paragraph gets it as a left tab stop (as the IDML export already writes it), so the text after the typed-in tab stays where it was. One undo step; with Track Changes on, the labels are tracked insertions. The menu label is translated in every UI language.

Left out: the Paragraph Styles panel variant (convert every paragraph using a style); a right- or centre-aligned number is left-aligned after conversion (I couldn't verify what InDesign does there); and a pre-existing difference I noticed but did not change here: an unnamed list restarts after a non-list paragraph, so converting…

title: Clamp object.stroke tint and gapTint to 0..1
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/object.rs:299-313 (object.stroke: `st.tint = v as f32`, `st.gap_tint = v as f32`; the no-selection path at :273 clamps, this one doesn't)` (no existing issue): object.stroke accepts an unbounded tint/gapTint; a huge value becomes f32 infinity and the saved .designcraft file can't be reopened.

## Cause
On a selected object, `object.stroke` cast `tint` and `gapTint` to f32 with no range check. A value like 1e300 became f32 infinity, which serde writes as `null`, so the saved .designcraft file failed to load (`invalid type: null, expected f32`). Values such as 2 or -1 were also stored out of range.

## Fix
`object.stroke` now clamps `tint` and `gapTint` to 0..1 before storing them on selected objects. This matches the no-selection branch of the same command. The regression test sets out-of-range values, checks the stored stroke, then saves and reloads the document.

## Verified
- Regression test `out_of_range_stroke_tints_are_clamped_and_the_saved_file_reloads`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine --test stroke_tint_range`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`object.fill` still rejects an out-of-range tint with an error instead of clamping. The no-selection branch of `object.stroke` was already clamped and is unchanged.

author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1245.

A horizontal or vertical line has zero height (or zero width). The Selection tool sends `transform.resize` with the line's bounds as `from`, and `transform_resize` rejected any source rect that was flat on either axis with "degenerate source rect". So dragging a line's handle did nothing.

Now a flat axis keeps scale 1 and only moves; the other axis scales as before. A line drawn from (100, 100) to (200, 100) and dragged to a width of 200 becomes 200 pt long and stays flat. Rects that have size on both axes behave the same as before.

The Selection tool already handles a flat source on its side: `finish_resize` skips the Shift aspect lock when `from` has no width or height, so nothing changes in the tools crate.

Test: `a_flat_line_resizes_along_its_length` creates a horizontal line, resizes it along its length and checks the new bounds. Without the fix, `transform.resize` returns the "degenerate source rect" error and the test fails.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Resizing a line with zero height now allows its length to change without altering its height.

title: Align Story Editor paragraph style labels with the wrapped text rows (#1251)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1251.

The Story Editor's style column guessed how many lines each paragraph takes as `len / 60 + 1` and padded with blank 11 px labels. That ignores the real editor width and font size, so the labels drift away from their paragraphs, and only line up at one particular window width.

Now the text editor is shown with `TextEdit::show`, and each style label is placed at the y position of the first laid-out row of its paragraph in the editor's galley (a paragraph starts after a row that `ends_with_newline`). The labels follow the text when the window is resized or the font size changes. The column keeps its 130 px width. Looking the paragraph up with `paras.get(i)` also removes an index that could go out of range.

Test: `labels_follow_wrapped_rows` checks the row-grouping helper on a paragraph that wraps over three rows, followed by two one-row paragraphs.

title: Show text stroke options in the Stroke panel when text is selected (#1265)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:

With text selected, the Stroke panel went down the object-only path (`sel_info` and the first selected item's stroke) and showed nothing useful for the text.

title: Reject invalid story.replaceRange offsets with an error (#1267)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1267.

`story.replaceRange` clamped and snapped invalid offsets, so a wrong range looked like success but edited the wrong text. It now returns a `BadParams` error and leaves the story unchanged when:

- `start` or `end` is inside a multi-byte character (e.g. 4..5 on `Città`, 8..14 on `Città – perché`),
- `end` is past the end of the story (20..999),
- `start` is after `end` (30..20).

The message gives the story length in bytes, as the issue asks: `range 8..14 must be UTF-8 byte offsets on character boundaries, start <= end; the story is 27 bytes`.

The Story Editor, the only internal caller, already sends ranges on character boundaries, so it is not affected.

`docs/mcp.md` (Text offsets) now says that `story.replaceRange` is the exception to "an offset inside a character snaps back".

Not changed: `text.select` and the other caret commands still snap offsets, as documented. The issue suggests they "could" follow the same rule, and the `units: "chars"` idea is optional; both are design calls for the maintainers.

Test: the existing `replacing_a_range_stays_on_utf8_boundaries` test, on `é漢🙂x` now checks that 3..6, 2..4, 0..99 and 5..2 are refused with "10 bytes" in the message and change nothing, then that the valid 2..5 still replaces `漢`. It fails on main, where those calls returned `Ok`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Invalid text replacement ranges now return an error without changing the story. Valid ranges must be ordered, within the story’s byte length, and aligned to character boundaries.
* **Documentation**
  * Clarified how text offsets behave, including which invalid replacement ranges produce errors and which offsets snap to the start of a character.

title: Keyboard Shortcuts: import an InDesign shortcut set
author: aiongg
body:
Part of #1180.

Keyboard Shortcuts gets an "Import InDesign Set…" button (desktop and browser). It reads the text file InDesign's Keyboard Shortcuts › Show Set saves, and applies its shortcuts to the commands it can match. The command behind it is `window.importShortcuts` (`{"path"}` or `{"text"}`), so the control channel and MCP can run it too.

- **Matching:** by menu path and label, with the product area as the top-level menu and `: ` as submenu levels. `...`/`…`, `&`, case and a leading Show/Hide are ignored.
- **Keys:** Windows Ctrl and Mac Cmd both map to the command modifier. Handles `Num` keys, arrow and Page keys, and the comma key (`Ctrl+,`). Uses the Default context, and the Text context for text commands that have no Default entry.
- **Applying:** the set wins for every matched command, and `[none defined]` clears it. Any other command holding an imported shortcut loses it. When two items in the set want the same keys, the later one takes them. Reset All to Defaults undoes the import.
- **Report:** lists what changed, which conflicts were cleared, and the items that couldn't be matched or read. The dialog shows a one-line summary.
- **Input:** UTF-8 or UTF-16, CRLF or LF, capped at 8 MB. The file is read through the engine's checked reader.

Not imported yet: tool keys (fixed in DesignCraft), panel shortcuts (panels open through one command with a parameter), and some navigation and nudge items that aren't standalone commands. Those belong in a shared keyboard-binding crate (craft-libs #115, craft-keymap); DesignCraft moves onto it when it lands.

Tests: one behaviour test on a synthetic set, and one for hostile input. `cargo xtask ci` passes (2,925 tests, wasm included).

author: Silvertree2010
body:

title: cli: every file a run writes is reported on stdout
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #1214.

## Reproduced

```console
$ designcraft-cli run --sample --all-pages pages > out.txt 2> err.txt
$ wc -l < out.txt
0
$ head -1 err.txt
wrote pages/page-001.png (630×810, 61.2 ms, 103 glyphs)
```

Nothing on stdout, everything on stderr — so a script has to merge the streams and parse prose to learn what was written.

Reading the code it is broader than the title. `--cmd` results go to stdout as JSON (`outln!`), but **every** write reported only to stderr: `--all-pages`, image `--export`, PDF export, PPTX export, document save and command exports. So stdout was empty for any invocation that only exported.

## Change

Each file written now emits one JSON line on stdout, next to where a `--cmd` result already goes, carrying what the stderr line carries:

```console
$ designcraft-cli run --sample --all-pages pages > out.txt 2> err.txt
$ head -2 out.txt
{"glyphs":103,"height":810,"ms":62.6,"width":630,"wrote":"pages/page-001.png"}
{"glyphs":1171,"height":810,"ms":28.0,"width":630,"wrote":"pages/page-002.png"}
$ head -1 err.txt
wrote pages/page-001.png (630×810, 62.6 ms, 103 glyphs)
```

and for the other kinds:

| export | line on stdout |
|---|---|
| PDF | `{"wrote": …, "pages": 4, "bytes": 552552, "warnings": []}` |
| PPTX | `{"wrote": …, "slides": …, "bytes": …, "warnings": []}` |
| document | `{"wrote": …, "saved": true}` |
| command export | `{"wrote": …, "bytes": …}` |

I chose this over moving the human lines to stdout. The lines on stderr are untouched, so anything reading them today keeps working, and warnings stay where they are *and* appear in the JSON for a script that wants them. It also matches the contract the CLI already has: stdout is one JSON object per line, stderr is for people.

## Tests

`files_written_are_reported_on_stdout_as_json` in `apps/designcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs`: every stdout line parses as JSON, there is exactly one per file in the directory, the paths exist and are in page order with sizes, the `wrote …` lines are still on s…
