title: PDF export: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH stands in for the clock, so exports repeat
author: Hamza0101
body:
Exporting one document twice gives two different PDFs.

## Measured

```console
$ designcraft-cli run --cmd 'file.new={"preset":"A4"}' --export rep1.pdf   # one second apart
$ designcraft-cli run --cmd 'file.new={"preset":"A4"}' --export rep2.pdf
$ cmp rep1.pdf rep2.pdf   # 88 bytes differ, same size
at  501:  /ModDate(D:20261019090734Z)      vs  …735Z)
at  533:  /CreationDate(D:20261019090734Z) vs  …735Z)
at 1243:  <xmp:ModifyDate>…T09:07:34…      vs  …09:07:35…
at 1301:  <xmp:CreateDate>…T09:07:34…      vs  …09:07:35…
at 1413:  <xmpMM:InstanceID>qag2XrlBRNXd…  vs  gSzguWYvlhbh…
```

## Change

`export_time` provides the date when the caller gives none: `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` when it holds a non-negative whole number of seconds, else the clock, per the [reproducible-builds specification](https://reproducible-builds.org/specs/source-date-epoch/).

```console
$ SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1791208980 designcraft-cli run … --export a.pdf   # one second apart
$ SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1791208980 designcraft-cli run … --export b.pdf
$ cmp a.pdf b.pdf && echo identical
identical                       # and both read D:20261005140300
```

Three limits, deliberately:

- **A date passed in still wins.** `PdfOptions::created` is taken first, so nothing that already supplies a date changes.
- **A malformed value is ignored** — blank, negative, non-numeric — and the clock answers instead. An export is never refused over the environment, which would be the wrong trade for a desktop app that also exports.
- **The clock is not frozen.** With the variable unset, two exports still differ, as before.

## The instance id is not a second source

`xmpMM:InstanceID` differs between the two files above, which would make this pointless if it were random. It is not: krilla computes it as `stable_hash_base64(pdf.as_bytes())`, so it differed *because* the timestamps did and follows them once they are pinned. That is why the files above come out identical rather than merely closer — I checked rather than assumed…

title: Add multi-image placement and contact-sheet grids

title: Truncate ASE swatch names that overflow the u16 length field
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/ase.rs:131-132` (no existing issue): ASE export corrupts the file when a swatch name is longer than 65535 UTF-16 units.

## Cause
`ase::write` stored the name length as `units.len() as u16`, which wraps for names over 65535 UTF-16 units, but it still wrote every unit. The length field no longer matched the data, so `read` misparsed the block and dropped the swatch.

## Fix
`write` now truncates names to 65534 UTF-16 units plus the terminating NUL, so the length always fits in a u16 and matches the units written. If the cut would split a surrogate pair, it drops the lone high surrogate.

## Verified
- Regression test `ase::tests::over_long_name_is_truncated_to_fit`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-color over_long_name_is_truncated_to_fit`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `read` side is unchanged. The `write` signature is unchanged: it still returns `Vec<u8>` rather than a `Result`, and there is no new error variant.

title: Drop out-of-range font sizes on DOCX import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/docx.rs:183-185` (no existing issue): DOCX import stores out-of-range font sizes (w:sz=0 or huge) unclamped.

## Cause
`run_attrs` in the DOCX importer turned any finite `w:sz` value into `sz/2` with no range check. A run with `w:sz=0` or `w:sz=99999999` therefore imported as 0 pt or about 50 million pt. The engine only accepts 0.1–1296 pt.

## Fix
`run_attrs` now keeps a run's size only if `sz/2` is within 0.1–1296 pt. Otherwise the size is dropped (None) and the default applies, as in the RTF importer. Non-finite values are also dropped, since they fail the range check. The regression test `docx::tests::out_of_range_sizes_are_dropped` imports runs with `w:sz=0` and `w:sz=99999999` and asserts that both sizes are None. Without the fix, the `w:sz=0` run imports as `Some(0.0)`.

## Verified
- Regression test `docx::tests::out_of_range_sizes_are_dropped`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport out_of_range_sizes_are_dropped`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The RTF importer, which already filters sizes, and the other DOCX numeric attributes (spacing, indents).

title: Tables: a table that moves on before any row is set takes the measure of the column it starts in
author: aykutfirat
body:
### Problem
A table that doesn't fit the rest of its column moves on to the next column or frame, but it keeps the column widths it was measured for in the column where the cursor was. When a story is threaded from a narrow frame into a wide one (an intro paragraph in a narrow frame, the table in a wide frame below), the table is set in the wide frame at the narrow frame's width. Its cells wrap, its rows grow, and the last rows run out of the frame as overset.

`place_table` scales the columns to the current column's measure once, before placing any row. When the first row group doesn't fit and the table moves on (`cur.next_column`), nothing of it has been set yet, but the squeezed widths, cell layouts and row heights are kept.

### Change
- **`measure_table`:** the measuring part of `place_table` (column widths scaled to the measure, the x offset for the alignment, each owner cell composed at its width, row heights including row spans) is now a function of the column width.
- **`place_table`:** when the table moves to the next column before any of it is set (still the first fragment), it is measured again for the column it actually starts in. Later fragments keep the first fragment's widths, as InDesign does.
- **Test:** `a_table_moved_on_from_a_narrow_frame_takes_the_measure_of_the_frame_it_starts_in` threads a 100 pt frame holding a paragraph into a 400 pt frame, then adds a 360 pt table that can't fit the first. title: Use standard macOS Settings and Hide shortcuts
author: andeecollard
body:
On macOS, Settings currently defaults to ⌘K, frame edges compete with the native Hide action on ⌘H, and High Quality Display competes with Hide Others on ⌥⌘H. This proposal gives those system actions their familiar Mac shortcuts.

- Settings: ⌘,; frame edges: ⌃⌘H; High Quality Display: ⌃⌥⌘H.
- Keep the existing native Hide/Hide Others and Minimize actions on ⌘H/⌥⌘H/⌘M.
- Preserve Windows/Linux defaults and explicit saved assignments. Add platform-default/override regression checks and document the intentional departure from reference-app shortcut parity.

Related to storytold/designcraft#1317. The matching PhotoCraft and VectorCraft proposals are tracked there.

References: [Apple Mac shortcuts](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102650), [Apple keyboard guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/keyboards), [published InDesign shortcuts](https://helpx.adobe.com/indesign/desktop/get-started/settings-and-preferences/keyboard-shortcuts.html). Research used public documentation only.

Validation: `cargo xtask ci` passed formatting, workspace Clippy (`-D warnings`), all 2,918 native workspace tests, PDF-dependency verification, assets and layering. The web-build step cannot complete locally because this environment lacks the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` standard library. The focused shortcut run passed 11 tests, and the shortcut dialog was rendered and visually inspected. CI must confirm the web build and other host platforms before merge.

Related proposals: [PhotoCraft #7809](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/7809), [VectorCraft #3133](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/3133).

title: Keep CDATA text in the DOCX/XLSX XML parser
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/docx.rs:134-135` (no existing issue): DOCX/XLSX XML parser silently drops CDATA text.

## Cause
The event loop in `parse` in `crates/textimport/src/docx.rs` had no `Event::CData` arm, so CDATA content fell into the `_ => {}` arm and was dropped. DOCX `w:t` runs and XLSX shared or inline strings written as CDATA therefore came in empty.

## Fix
Added an `Event::CData` arm that decodes the CDATA content and appends it as a `Node::Text` on the current element. CDATA is literal, so it is not unescaped. A regression test, `cdata_text`, covers it.

## Verified
- Regression test `docx::tests::cdata_text`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport cdata_text`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other event types, such as comments, processing instructions and doctype, still go to the catch-all arm and are ignored. I didn't add DOCX- or XLSX-level tests, because the unit test already covers the shared parser.

title: Math: stack operator limits with \limits, display style and \underset
author: okc0mputex
body:
## Summary

`\lim`, `\max`, `\min`, `\sup`, `\inf`, `\limsup` and `\liminf` can now stack their limits
under the operator, as LaTeX does:

- with `\limits` straight after the operator (`\lim\limits_{x\to 0}`);
- in display style: `math.insert` / `math.svg` take a new, documented `display: bool` param
  (default `false`, so existing documents and calls set exactly as before);
- through `\underset{under}{base}` (`\underset{n\to\infty}{\lim}`, `\underset{k}{\mathrm{arg}}`).

`\nolimits` does the reverse for any operator, the big ones included (`\sum\nolimits_i`).

## Motivation

Math-heavy textbook layout uses display limits all the time (`lim` with `x → 0` set under it,
`max` over an index range). Today `\lim_{x\to 0}` is always set as a subscript, and `\limits`
and `\underset` come out as raw source (see the before image).

## What changed

- `crates/engine/src/math.rs`
  - `Node::Op(name, stacked)` for named operators; `Node::Big` gains a `stacked` flag
    (`true` by default, so `\sum_{i=1}^n` is unchanged; `\nolimits` clears it).
  - `Parser::limits_flag()` reads a `\limits` / `\nolimits` that follows an operator, as a
    whole word only (`\limitsfoo` stays an unknown command). A stray one sets nothing.
  - `Parser.display` and `parse_at(.., display)`. `pub struct Options { display }` and
    `pub fn to_svg_with(latex, size, &Options)`. `to_svg` is unchanged and still the text-style
    entry point; both go through a shared `render`. There is no test-only `parse`.
  - `\underset{…}{…}` stacks its first argument under its second. A base that isn't a named
    operator or upright text (`\underset{x}{\frac{a}{b}}`) is laid out as itself (`Node::Stacked`).
  - Layout: a stacked `Op` uses the same over/under placement as big operators. It also
    counts as an ordinary atom for spacing.

title: Math: set cases, aligned and array environments as grids
author: okc0mputex
body:
## Summary

`\begin{env} … \end{env}` is parsed into rows (split at `\\`) and cells (split at `&`) and
laid out as a grid centred on the math axis:

- `cases`: a drawn left brace spanning the rows, then the left-aligned columns;
- `aligned`, `align`, `align*`, `split`: right/left column pairs with no gap inside a pair, so
  `a &= b \\ &= c` lines up the relations;
- `gathered`: centred rows;
- `array`: the column spec (`{lcr}`) is read and skipped (columns are left-aligned for now).

## Motivation

Piecewise definitions and multi-line derivations are the bread and butter of a math-heavy
textbook layout. On `main` both come out as raw source (`\begincases…`; see the before image).

## What changed

- `crates/engine/src/math.rs`
  - `Node::Grid { env, rows }`.
  - `Parser::env_body()` returns the raw source up to the matching `\end{env}`, keeping nested
    environments whole; for an unclosed one it returns the rest of the input.
  - `split_grid()` splits outside braces and nested environments, honours `\&` and `\{`/`\}`,
    and doesn't add an empty row for a trailing `\\`.
  - `grid()` does the layout.
  - As in amsmath, the right cell of an aligned pair starts with an empty `{}`, so a relation
    after `&` keeps its thick space on the left (`(a+b)^2 &= …` is set `(a+b)² = …`).
  - A stray `\end{…}` sets nothing.
  - No-panic rules (AGENTS.md): every slice access goes through `get()` and iterators; there is
    no indexing on input-derived data.
  - Recursion: the `begin` branch checks `MAX_NESTING`, and an environment's cells parse a 16th of
    `MAX_NESTING` deeper, so grids nest at most 16 deep: each open environment holds a copy of the
    rest of the input while its cells are parsed.
    `an_over_deep_expression_is_bounded` gains two hostile inputs, 20 000 nested `\begin{cases}`
    with and without braces, and a check that grid nesting stops at 16 levels (the 20 000-level
    input peaks at about 67 MB instead of 208 MB).

title: Math: set and logic symbols, \mathbb and more operator names
author: okc0mputex
body:
## Summary

- **New symbols**
  - Relations: `\mid` `\notin` `\subset` `\subseteq` `\iff`/`\Leftrightarrow` `\implies`
    `\mapsto` `\sim`.
  - Binary operators: `\circ` `\cap` `\cup` `\setminus` `\ast`.
  - Ordinary symbols: `\emptyset`/`\varnothing` `\forall` `\exists` `\neg`/`\lnot` `\angle`

  - Brackets: `\lfloor…\rfloor`, `\lceil…\rceil`, `\langle…\rangle`.

- **Operator names:** `\cot` `\sec` `\csc` `\arcsin` `\arccos` `\arctan` `\sinh` `\cosh` `\tanh`

Set-builder notation, logic and the usual function names are everywhere in math-heavy textbook

title: Text: an inline equation hanging below the line pushes the next line down
author: okc0mputex
body:
## Summary

To sit on the text baseline, an inline math expression is lowered with a negative Y offset by
its depth. Then the deep part of a fraction, or stacked limits, hangs below the descender and
overprints the next line.

After such a line, the next one is now held down until its own text-height ascent (0.72 em of its
text size, or its cap height if taller) plus 0.5 pt clears the equation's bottom.

- Only the line after the equation moves; the paragraph's pitch resumes after it.
- An equation within the descender changes nothing.
- An equation raised above the baseline is already handled by the line's own height and is
  unchanged.

## Scope: equations only

The extra space applies only to math expressions placed by `math.insert`: graphics named
`Math` that carry their LaTeX as alt text. Other inline objects keep hanging over the next line,
as they do in IDML layouts, where #1238 paints them under the text instead. That keeps imported
IDML pages composing exactly as before.

Maintainers might prefer an explicit marker instead, either on `AnchorPosition::Inline` or on
the item. Happy to switch; the compose change is a single predicate (`is_equation`).

## Motivation

Inline equations with fractions or limits are common in math-heavy textbook layout. Aligning
their baseline with the text currently means they collide with the line below (before image).

## What changed

- `crates/compose/src/lib.rs`:
  - `Cursor::hang`: after a line is set, the bottom of its lowest hanging equation, across all

  - `is_equation()`.

title: Paste: other apps' text goes into a text caret after copying objects
author: aiongg
body:
Closes #212.

After copying objects in DesignCraft, text copied in another app and pasted at a text caret was replaced by the copied objects (anchored at the caret), and the other app's text was lost.

- The placeholder DesignCraft writes to the system clipboard when it copies objects is built in the engine (`copied_objects_text`), so the UI and `edit.paste` compare against the same text.
- `edit.paste` at a caret anchors the copied objects only when the system clipboard still holds that placeholder (or no text). Any other text is inserted.
- When the copied objects can't be anchored (text frames, groups holding one, a table cell), pasting at a caret inserts their text instead of failing with "clipboard is empty".
- Anchored pastes get fresh item ids (they kept the source ids, so `doc.check()` failed with a duplicate id), and the default layer when the clipboard came from another document, as page pastes do.
- `edit.pasteWithoutFormatting` is unchanged.

Rich text from another app still pastes as plain text.

Tests: `paste_at_a_caret_prefers_other_apps_text_to_copied_objects` and `copied_text_frames_paste_at_a_caret_as_their_text` (both fail without the change). `cargo xtask ci` passes (2,928 tests), run together with three unrelated fixes opened at the same time.

title: Hidden characters: trailing spaces show their dots before the paragraph mark
author: aiongg
body:
Closes #594.

With hidden characters shown, spaces typed at the end of a paragraph or story had no dots: the ¶ (or # at the story end) was drawn right after the last letter, on top of them. The paragraph mark now follows the trailing spaces, and each space shows its dot. Composition is unchanged; line breaking and justification still ignore trailing spaces.

The marks are computed by a small function (`hidden_marks`) the canvas paints from. It reads characters with checked offsets, so a glyph offset that isn't a character boundary is skipped instead of panicking.

The other parts of #594 (the caret past trailing spaces, the view jumping while typing) were fixed in 0.8.0 and 0.9.0.

Test: `trailing_spaces_show_dots_before_the_paragraph_mark` (fails without the change). `cargo xtask ci` passes (2,928 tests), run together with three unrelated fixes opened at the same time.

title: Math: set matrix environments with delimiters drawn to the grid

body:

> **Stacked on #1325.** This branch includes #1325's commits; only the top commit (`16f30e2`, "Math: set matrix environments with delimiters drawn to the grid") is new here. Please merge #1325 first; once it is in, this diff shrinks to that one commit.

Matrix environments are set as grids with centred columns between delimiters drawn to the
grid's height:

- `pmatrix` ( ), `bmatrix` [ ], `Bmatrix` { }, `vmatrix` | |, `Vmatrix` ‖ ‖;

## Motivation

Vectors, coefficient matrices and determinants are everywhere in linear algebra and analytic

title: Math: set accents centred over their base
author: okc0mputex
body:
## Summary

Accents are set over their base:

- `\hat`, `\check`, `\tilde`, `\acute`, `\grave`, `\breve`, `\dot`, `\ddot`, `\bar`: the serif's
  spacing-accent glyph, its ink centred over the base's ink with a small gap above it;
- `\vec`: a small drawn arrow;
- `\widehat`, `\widetilde`, `\overline`, `\underline`, `\overrightarrow`, `\overleftarrow`: drawn
  across the whole argument.

Over an italic base the accent leans right with the letter (a skew in proportion to the base's
height), and `i`/`j` lose their dot (`\hat{i}` sets ı̂, as `\hat{\imath}` in TeX).

Closes #1330.

## Motivation

Vectors, means, derivatives with respect to time and estimates (`\vec{v}`, `\bar{x}`, `\dot{x}`,
`\hat{\theta}`) and segment and arc notation (`\overline{AB}`, `\overrightarrow{AB}`) appear on
almost every page of a math textbook. On `main` they come out as raw source (`\vecv`, `\hatx`;
see the before image).

- `crates/engine/src/math.rs`

title: Math: set expressions in a chosen font family
author: okc0mputex
body:
## Summary

> **Stacked on #1324.** This branch includes #1324's commits; only the top commit (`40078cc`, "Math: set expressions in a chosen font family") is new here. Please merge #1324 first; once it is in, this diff shrinks to that one commit.

`math.insert` and `math.svg` take a `family` parameter, so an expression is set in an installed
font family instead of always in the bundled serif:

- letters, digits and operators come from that family (named in any case) and are measured with
  its metrics;
- characters the family lacks still come from the fallback sans, as they do for the bundled serif;
- a family without an italic sets italic letters in its upright face, measured as drawn;
- a family that isn't installed falls back to the bundled serif, with no error;
- editing an equation by `id` keeps its family unless `family` is given (`""` goes back to the
  bundled serif), also after a save and reopen or an IDML round trip.

No issue tracks this.

## Motivation

Body text is often set in something other than a serif, and an equation in the middle of a sans
paragraph stands out when it is always set in Source Serif (see the before image). Until now
the only option was the serif. With `family`, an inline equation can use the paragraph's family.

- `crates/engine/src/math.rs`

title: IDML: Q ruler units are Q, as InDesign writes them
author: con3code
body:
Fixes #1360. Part of #1357.

IDML wrote ruler units in Q as `U`. InDesign writes Q as `Q`: a document saved from InDesign 2025 (Japanese edition) with text size in Q has `TextSizeMeasurementUnits="Q"` on `ViewPreference`. `U` is a different unit (the scripting reference lists `Q`, `HA`, `U` and `BAI` as separate `MeasurementUnits`). So a document with Q rulers went out as U, and an InDesign file with Q rulers came back in points.

- `names::unit_out` writes Q as `Q`. Ha was already `Ha`.

An IDML that an earlier DesignCraft wrote with Q rulers says `U`; it now opens in points with that note, which is what InDesign would make of it too.

title: Type fields read the unit typed (13Q, 5mm), as InDesign's do
author: con3code
body:
Fixes #1359. Part of #1357.

Fields that hold a length in points dropped the unit typed into them. They were plain number fields with a ` pt` suffix, whose parser keeps only digits and operators, so `13Q` set 13 pt and `5mm` set 5 pt, with no error. InDesign converts what is typed: in a field shown in Q, `12pt` becomes 16.933 Q.

**The change.**
- `NumKind::Points` is a length in points. It shows as before (`12.5 pt`, same decimals) and reads like a measure field: any unit and arithmetic (`13Q`, `22H`, `5mm`, `1p`, `9pt+1H`). A bare number is still points, and an unknown unit is an invalid value instead of a number.
- About 30 fields use it:

  - Stroke weights: Properties, Control, taskbar, the text stroke and table cell strokes.

  - Ruby size and offsets, tate-chu-yoko offsets, kenten distance.
  - Drop shadow distance and size.
- `char_number`, `char_auto_number` and `widgets::number` pick it for the ` pt` suffix (`NumField::with_suffix`). Other suffixes (`%`, `°`, none) are plain numbers as before.

**Leaving a field unchanged commits nothing.** A field reads its text back when it loses focus. Clicking into `9.21 pt` (13Q) and out again set 9.21 pt, rounding the value to the shown decimals. Now text equal to the shown value is left alone; this applies to every numeric field.

title: Fix "-0p0" for tiny negative pica/cicero values
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/geom/src/units.rs:276` (no existing issue): Pica/cicero formatting shows "-0p0" for tiny negative values.

## Cause
`format_measure_prec` set the sign of Picas and Ciceros from the raw `pt < 0.0`, before the value was rounded to the displayed precision. A tiny negative value such as -0.0004 pt rounds to zero but still printed as "-0p0".

## Fix
The sign is now decided after rounding. It is kept only if the rounded whole or fractional part is non-zero, so these values print "0p0" and "0c0". The change adds a regression test.

## Verified
- Regression test `units::tests::tiny_negative_picas_ciceros_have_no_sign`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-geom tiny_negative_picas_ciceros_have_no_sign`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other units are unchanged, since `trim` already maps "-0" to "0" for them.

title: Clamp polygon side count before narrowing to u32
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/object.rs:710-711 (also :975)` (no existing issue): Polygon side count is truncated to 32 bits before it is clamped.

## Cause
`tool.polygonSettings` and `frame.create` read `sides` as a u64 and cast it with `as u32` before clamping to 3..=100. Values of 2^32 or more wrapped around first, so 2^32+5 gave 5 sides and 2^32+1 gave 3 instead of 100.

## Fix
Both call sites now clamp the u64 to 3..=100 first and then cast to u32. The regression test covers `tool.polygonSettings` and `frame.create`.

## Verified
- Regression test `cmd::object::polygon_tests::polygon_sides_clamp_before_narrowing`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine --lib polygon_sides_clamp_before_narrowing`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The same `as u32` before `.clamp(1, 40)` pattern for text frame `columns` (object.rs, near line 2519) is unchanged. It is a separate command and the report did not cover it.

title: Canvas: draw the overlays only for spreads that can show
author: Hamza0101
body:
Part of #1343 — the frame-edge half only. ticket-craft asked for the two findings to be split, so the start-up GPU fallback is untouched.

This takes the first of @the reporter's three suggestions, the one they put smallest:

> Skip slots whose bounds don't intersect the canvas clip rect in `draw_frames`. The other per-slot overlays (`draw_guides` and the rest) could do the same. At fit-spread that's ~48× less work here.

### The problem

`draw_frames` loops `for slot in &layout.slots` with no visibility test, and everything inside costs work in proportion to the items on that spread — `overset_marks` searches the whole document for each overset frame. So the cost was roughly (frames on all spreads) × (items in the document) on every frame, even with the view sitting still. Their measurement: **198 ms** of UI work per frame with frame edges on, **0.9 ms** with them off, and the graphics backend making no difference.

### Measured here

A 96-page document fitted to one spread, 1440 × 900:

```
slots = 49,  shown_at_fit_spread = 1
```

so 1 slot of work instead of 49, which is the ~48× they predicted.

### One correction to the suggestion

Culling on the slot's **page bounds** would have been wrong: an item may sit off the spread, on the pasteboard, and its frame edges still have to be drawn. Doing it that way would have silently stopped drawing them.

`CanvasLayout::new` already computed the right rectangle — the pages plus the pasteboard around them — to build its pasteboard union, so the slot now keeps it as `reach` and the test uses that:

```rust

pb = Some(pb.map_or(pr, |p| p.union(pr)));
slots.push(SpreadSlot { spread: r, xf, rotation, bounds: cb, reach: pr });
```

It is `#[serde(skip)]`, like `xf`, so `SpreadSlot`'s serialised shape does not change. An item beyond the pasteboard is outside the editable area, so that is the honest boundary for the test.

title: Graphics: the start-up log says which backend was chosen and how to change it
author: Hamza0101
body:
Part of #1343 — the smallest of the three suggestions in its second finding.

`Fallback::begin` returns before the fallback runs when `WGPU_BACKEND` is set:

```rust
// backend.rs:212
if wgpu::Backends::from_env().is_some_and(|b| !b.is_empty()) {
    log::info!("graphics: WGPU_BACKEND is set, wgpu picks the backend and the start-up fallback is off");
    return None;
}
```

so `begin_unforced` below it is reached only when the variable is **not** set. Its log line said the opposite:

```
before: graphics: DirectX 12 (WGPU_BACKEND overrides)
after:  graphics: DirectX 12 (first choice; set WGPU_BACKEND to choose another)
```

Reading a log, the old line says the user's environment chose the backend when nothing had. The report quotes exactly that line as evidence of which backend a start used, which is the wrong conclusion to be led to — and it is the line a user sees when asked for their log.

The new wording says which backend was chosen and how to choose another, so it carries the fact *and* the way out.

### Scope

One message, plus a comment recording why the branch implies the variable is unset, so a later reordering of the two does not quietly make it wrong again. `begin_unforced` is called only from `begin` and from the tests, which bypass the environment check deliberately.

`grep -rn "WGPU_BACKEND overrides"` matched only that line — no test, doc or release note depended on the text.

### Not in this change

The two larger suggestions in that finding — opening the start-up documents only after `presented()`, and recording `Startup::busy` in `gpu.json` so a start that froze in app code does not blame the backend. I have left a note on the issue about why the second is not as simple as it reads: `Watch` resets on `busy` **or** progress and only ever *reports* lateness, while the record *blames*, so excusing a start merely because it was busy would stop the fallback firing for a driver stall reached from inside `ui`. title: Print color: overprint, knockout, CMYK blending and spot gradients through craft-pdf
author: aiongg
body:
Depends on storytold/craft-libs#190.

Print PDFs now separate correctly for overprint, knockout groups, CMYK blending and spot gradients. The writer fixes live in craft-libs' vendored krilla (#190); this PR adopts them and removes DesignCraft's byte-level workarounds. craft-pdf, craft-prepress and the root `[patch.crates-io] krilla` are pinned to the #190 head on aiongg/craft-libs (8fbfea8); the pin moves to storytold/craft-libs at the merge commit.

## What changes in exported PDFs

- **CMYK blending:** print documents (CMYK blend space) write CMYK page and transparency groups through `craft_pdf::write::print`. PDF/X-4 also carries the CMYK working space as its `GTS_PDFX` output intent and `/Trapped /False`; Coated FOGRA39 is used when there is no CMYK profile. Plain exports carry no output intent, as in InDesign. RGB documents are unchanged.
- **Overprint:** Overprint Fill, Overprint Stroke, Overprint Gap and overprinting text are written as `/op`, `/OP` and `/OPM 1`. 100% [Black] fills, strokes and text overprint when Appearance of Black says so (the default). PDF/A leaves overprint out with a warning.
- **Knockout Group and Isolate Blending** are written as the group's `/K` and `/I`. Knockout groups stay vector instead of being rasterized.
- **Spot gradients:** a gradient stop keeps the swatch it was given (Gradient panel, `swatch.create {gradient}`, `object.gradient`, IDML `StopColor`), following renames and edits. One spot with its tints or [Paper] exports as a Separation shading; a spot with process inks, or two spots, as DeviceN. Older documents' plain-color stops export as before.
- **File › Print** spools exactly the PDF Export PDF writes with the same settings (flattener, soft effects, print color, warnings), and accepts Export PDF's settings.

Removed: the group color-space and output-intent byte rewrites (`pdfx.rs` `cmyk_group_spaces`, `make_pdfx4`'s intent edits, the page blend space for print output) and Print's separate shadow path.

title: Saturate table alternating-fill and index paragraph counts
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:1396-1403` (no existing issue): Table alternating-fill counts are truncated to 32 bits instead of being clamped.

## Cause
`parse_alt` in `table.rs` and the `nextParagraphs` range in `index.rs` read u64 values and cast them with `as u32`. Values of 2^32 or more wrapped around, so `skipFirst: 4294967296` became 0 and `first: 4294967297` became 1.

## Fix
Both places now convert with `u32::try_from(x).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)`, so out-of-range values saturate at `u32::MAX`. Regression tests cover the table alternating-fill counts and `index.addReference` with `nextParagraphs`.

## Verified
- Regression tests `tests_table::alternating_fill_counts_saturate_instead_of_wrapping`, `tests_table::index_next_paragraphs_saturates_instead_of_wrapping`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-engine saturat`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other `as u32` casts in the engine are unchanged. Input is clamped rather than rejected, which matches `layout.rs` and `print.rs`.

title: Refuse PDF page ranges in the Place PDF dialog instead of using page 1
author: Silvertree2010
body:

title: Print color: PDF/X-1a export through craft-prepress's flattener
author: aiongg
body:
Depends on storytold/craft-libs#194. Builds on #1374: until #1374 merges, its commits show here too. Part of #873.

File › Export PDF can write PDF/X-1a:2003. DesignCraft writes its print PDF (CMYK blending, output intent, overprint, spot inks) and flattens it with craft-prepress's flattener (craft-libs#194), which writes the PDF 1.4 X-1a:2003 file: transparency goes away, while inks, overprint and live text are kept where possible; complex regions become DeviceN images at the flattener resolution.

## What changes for users

- `file.exportPdf {standard: "x1a"}`; Export PDF has a "PDF/X-1a:2003" preset (High Resolution flattener, crop and bleed marks) and PDF/X-1a:2003 in the Standard list.
- A Transparency Flattener preset in the dialog (None, High, Medium, Low) sets the flattener resolution: High 300 ppi, Medium 150, Low 72, or a number 36–1200.
- New warnings: regions rasterized and their lowest resolution, unreadable images, dropped inks.
- `designcraft-cli validate-pdf FILE [--standard x4|x1a]` checks an X-1a file: version 1.4 or lower, the X-1a identification, a CMYK output intent, `/Trapped`, trim boxes; no soft masks, transparency groups, constant alpha below 1 or blend modes other than Normal; only DeviceCMYK, DeviceGray, Separation and DeviceN (with process alternates); embedded, non-Type 3 fonts. If transparency or a non-print color remains after flattening, the export fails with an error naming it.
- Drop shadows on spread objects reach the flattener as a mask of the shadow over live content, multiplied over what's beneath them (InDesign's default), so a black shadow over a spot flattens to DeviceN with the spot still at 100% instead of an RGB image.
- X-1a files carry no links, bookmarks, tags or form fields.

The placed-PDF renderer (hayro) now comes from craft-libs' vendored copy at the same revision as craft-pdf, which the flattener needs.

title: Object › Fitting › Content-Aware Fit: fill the frame and show what stands out in the image
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while replaying Learn Skills Daily's *InDesign Full Course Tutorial* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY), chapter "Working with Images (Part 1)", 1:01:25–1:02:30). The instructor right-clicks a photo in a round frame, chooses Fitting › Content-Aware Fit, and InDesign fills the frame with the photo's subject in view. He uses it for every photo in the chapter ("I do find that content-aware fit works pretty good"). DesignCraft had every other fitting option but not this one.

## Change
- **`object.fit {mode: contentAwareFit}`:**
  - The graphic fills its frame proportionally, as Fill Frame Proportionally does.
  - Along the axis it overflows, the part that shows is centred on what stands out in the image, instead of the fitting alignment.
  - One undo step, like the other modes.
- **What stands out** (`cmd/content_fit.rs`, a heuristic written for DesignCraft; InDesign's own uses Adobe's AI):
  - The image is analysed on a grid of at most 96 × 96 cells, sampled from at most 400,000 pixels.
  - Each cell scores its luminance gradient (edges and texture) plus how far its colour is from the image's average.
  - The background level, the median of each row's or column's total, is taken off, and the window is centred on the weighted centre of what's left, clamped to the image.
- **Fallbacks:**
  - A plain image, where nothing stands out, stays centred.
  - Vector, PDF and EPS graphics, unreadable data and images over 40 MP are filled and aligned as Fill Frame Proportionally.
- **UI:**
  - Object › Fitting › Content-Aware Fit, after Fit Content Proportionally as in InDesign, with InDesign's shortcut Cmd+Alt+Shift+X. The canvas context menu gets it too, through the same submenu.
  - A Content-Aware Fit button in Properties › Frame Fitting, with a new icon drawn in code.

title: Drop out-of-range RTF \uN values instead of wrapping them
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/rtf.rs:237` (no existing issue): RTF import wraps out-of-range \uN values to 32 bits and inserts a wrong character.

## Cause
The RTF `\uN` handler parsed N as i64 and cast it with `as u32` without checking the range. A value like `\u4294967361` wrapped to 65 and imported as 'A'. A large negative value could wrap to a valid code unit the same way.

## Fix
The handler now accepts only N in -32768..=65535, which is the range RTF allows, and maps negative values with `n + 65536`. Any other value is dropped and no character is inserted. The fallback-character skip count is still set for dropped values.

## Verified
- Regression test `rtf::tests::out_of_range_unicode_escape_is_dropped`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport out_of_range_unicode_escape_is_dropped`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `\uc` handling and the rest of the RTF parser are unchanged.

title: Keep ':', '<', '>' and '\' in Tagged Text style names
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/textimport/src/tagged.rs:35 (also :52)` (no existing issue): Tagged Text export strips ':' from style names, so the style name changes on re-import.

## Cause
The Tagged Text exporter wrote `<ParaStyle:…>` and `<CharStyle:…>` values with `replace(['<', '>', ':'], "")`, which dropped those characters. A style such as "Body: Indent" was re-imported as "Body Indent", so it no longer matched the original style.

## Fix
The exporter now keeps ':' as it is, because the importer splits a tag only at its first colon. It escapes '<', '>' and '\' with a backslash, which the tag scanner already skips over. The importer now removes those backslash escapes from ParaStyle and CharStyle values, so the name comes back exactly as it was exported.

## Verified
- Regression test `tagged::tests::style_names_with_tag_characters_round_trip`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-textimport style_names_with_tag_characters_round_trip`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Other tag values (cFont, cTypeface, DefineParaStyle/DefineCharStyle) and the way non-ASCII characters in style names are written are unchanged.

title: Remember the last print units in the New Document window
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1400

## Cause
The New Document window always opened with the factory settings (`NewDocument::default()`, in Picas), and no preference kept the units of the last document made. Picking a built-in print preset card also replaced the fields with that preset's own units, which are Picas for Letter, Legal, Tabloid and the other US sizes.

## Fix
A new `new_document_units` field in `UiState` stores the units of the last print document created. It is saved with the preferences and left out of the JSON while unset. When the New Document window opens, and when you pick the [Default] card or a built-in print preset card, the measures are shown in those units.

## Verified
- Regression test `new_document::tests::the_chosen_print_units_are_remembered_for_the_next_document`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-ui-egui --lib new_document::tests::the_chosen_print_units_are_remembered_for_the_next_document`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Recent and Saved cards still use the units they were made with, and Web and Mobile presets still switch to pixels. Other code paths that create the dialog directly with `Dialog::new` (for example in tests) still start with the factory units.

title: Reject impossible calendar days in parse_iso_date
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/doc/src/vars.rs:162` (no existing issue): ISO date parser accepts impossible calendar days and silently rolls them into the next month.

## Cause
`parse_iso_date` only checked that the day was in 1..=31 whatever the month. Dates such as `2019-02-31` were accepted, and `days_from_civil` rolled them into the next month.

## Fix
`parse_iso_date` now checks the day against the real length of the month, including leap years (divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400). It returns `None` for days that don't exist. The `iso_dates` test now covers `2019-02-31`, `2019-04-31`, `2019-02-29`, `2021-02-30` and a time-suffixed `2019-04-31T00:00:00Z`.

## Verified
- Regression test `vars::tests::iso_dates`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p designcraft-doc --lib iso_dates`).

title: View: link badge on pictures placed from a file, as in InDesign
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while replaying the Learn Skills Daily *InDesign Full Course Tutorial* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuE8JpajmgY)), chapter 10 "Working with Images Part 2" (1:14:41). In InDesign every picture placed from a file carries a small chain badge on its frame's top edge, selected or not, so linked pictures can be told apart at a glance. DesignCraft showed nothing.

- **Badge:** each frame showing a linked file gets a chain on its top edge, 16 px in from the left corner, in its layer's colour on a light halo.
  - It's drawn in code (no Adobe artwork).
  - It's found inside groups too.
  - Embedded pictures get none.
- **Link status:** the badge follows the Links panel's status.
  - A modified file shows a yellow warning.
  - A missing file shows a red stop.
  - The status is checked again when the document changes, and at most once a second otherwise, because the check reads the linked files.
- **Toggle:** View › Extras › Show/Hide Link Badge (`view.linkBadge`) turns the badges off, and `ui.set {linkBadge}` does the same over the control channel. It's on by default, as in InDesign. Preview modes hide the badges with the other non-printing marks.
- **Translations:** the menu entry is translated in every table.
- **Docs:** ui-parity, the parity checklist, target-app-parity, the control protocol and ROADMAP are updated.

title: Canvas: an empty graphic frame's X joins its corners, as in InDesign
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while checking #1416 against Zero2Graphic's *How to Page Layout design in Adobe InDesign 2022 CC* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vJroNPKnQg8), 1:25). The instructor slants a row of empty graphic frames into parallelograms with Direct Selection. In InDesign each frame's X still joins its corners. In DesignCraft the X stayed across the frame's bounding box, so a slanted frame's X ran past its corners.

- a rectangle's X joins its corners;
- after its two top points move 30 pt right, the X joins the slanted corners.

It fails without the change. The whole ui-egui suite passes. Clippy and fmt are clean.

None. With #1416, slanting a whole row at once shows the X on every frame.

title: Canvas: the cursor readout is InDesign's light grey box
author: moppeeer
body:
Found while checking #1418 against Zero2Graphic's *How to Page Layout design in Adobe InDesign 2022 CC* ([video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vJroNPKnQg8), 0:44). InDesign's readout beside the cursor while drawing a frame is a light grey box (#a8a8a8, measured from the frame) with white text. DesignCraft's was a dark translucent box.

![InDesign, main and this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moppeeer/designcraft-pr-assets/main/readout-grey/readout-grey.png)

## Change
- **New token:** `readout_bg`, InDesign's #a8a8a8, for the readouts beside the cursor (frame size, angles, measurements). The text stays white.
- **High Contrast:** keeps the readout black, because white on light grey is too faint there.
- **Unchanged:** the loaded-text cursor badge keeps `measure_bg`.

The task bar under the readout in the screenshots shows up only in `ui_shot`. Its pointer events go straight to the session, so egui never sees a press. In the app, the bar already hides while the pointer is down on the canvas.

## Test
`the_cursor_readout_is_indesigns_light_grey` checks the readout's colours in every brightness, including High Contrast's black. The whole ui-egui suite passes. Clippy and fmt are clean.

## Dependencies
None. #1418 changes the same readout's text (document units, two lines).
